It always goes in above whatever layer is selected (usually the last thing I added) and starts at the playhead. title: Preview: Audio switch wipes the cache, and playback with audio skips frames
author: thlgr
body:
Two bugs:

1. Turning a layer's Audio switch on or off throws away the whole cache, so everything re-renders. Lock and Shy do the same. None of these change pixels, so they shouldn't be part of the cache key!!

2. With audio off playback waits for each frame (which is good), but with audio on, playback skips frames that aren't rendered yet. I get choppy frames and gaps in the preview (I looked at the source and it seems intentional, I don't know why), in AE it plays every frame and slows down with audio, so this should happen with effectcraft too.

Proposed fix: take audio, locked and shy out of the cache keys. With audio on, wait for frames like the no-audio path does. Slowing the audio down to match the video needs more work, but it can be done I guess

title: Preview does not render more frames when the GPU runs out of memory
author: thlgr
body: When VRAM runs out during preview, effectcraft panics on every frame thread instead of recovering, and the frames that crashed never recover. In the source code, the VRAM budget is just a fixed number that doesn't account for how much memory the GPU actually has, and the GPU setup is missing an error handler entirely, so when it OOMs, it turns into a panic, meaning the crashed frame never gets cleared; it stays marked "in progress" forever, instead of falling back for example.

author: coygeek

## Summary

`.github/workflows/release.yml` twice tells readers to "See docs/releasing.md", but that file is not on any branch or tag of the repository, so the pointer leads nowhere. No other document in the repository describes the release procedure the workflow implements (push to the `release` branch, a draft GitHub Release built from the root `Cargo.toml` version, and publication of that draft outside the workflow), so a maintainer who follows the pointer finds no release guidance. This is a documentation defect; the workflow itself is not affected.

- `main` at commit 2fadd14f09bb064cab8f1f8fe85af601a08b6e53 (fresh clone).
- Latest published release `v0.3.1` (tag commit e6c817bb3f382b7fd71307baba9bb3427ce77fd9), which is also the current tip of the `release` branch.

title: Tracking animator ignores paragraph alignment (centered / right text drifts right)
author: square3ang
body:
## Summary
A text animator with **Tracking** always grows the line to the right, ignoring paragraph justification. On centered (or right-aligned) text, the line drifts instead of expanding around its alignment point. After Effects keeps a centered line centered when tracking is animated.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Create a point text layer `ABCD`, 40 px, paragraph alignment **Center**.
2. Animation ▸ Animate Text ▸ Tracking, set Tracking Amount to 500.
3. The text shifts to the right instead of spreading out from the centre.

## Measured (glyph bounds, layer space)
| Justify | centre before | centre after |
|---|---|---|
| Left   | 55.2  | 95.2 |
| Center | -0.7  | **39.3** (drifts +40 px) |
| Right  | -56.6 | -16.6 (right edge no longer pinned) |

Workaround: add **Line Anchor** to the animator and set it to 50% (centre) / 100% (right).

## Cause
In `crates/render/src/text.rs` (`text_geom`), the per-line tracking compensation uses only the animators' Line Anchor value, which defaults to `0.0` (left) when no animator has a Line Anchor property. The paragraph's justification is never used.

## Suggested fix
When no Line Anchor property applies, default it from the justification:

```diff
-    // Tracking (before / after each character) and Line Anchor, per line.
+    // Tracking (before / after each character) and Line Anchor, per line. Without a Line Anchor
+    // property the line grows from where the paragraph alignment pins it (centre / right).
+    let default_anchor = match doc.justify {
+        Justify::Center | Justify::JustifyLastCenter => 50.0,
+        Justify::Right | Justify::JustifyLastRight => 100.0,
+        _ => 0.0,
+    };
     let mut shift = vec![0.0f64; n];
@@
-        let (mut la, mut la_k) = (0.0, 0.0);
+        let (mut la, mut la_k) = (default_anchor, 0.0);
```

With this, the centered case keeps its centre (-0.7 → -0.7) and right-aligned text grows leftward. All `effectcraft-render` tests pass (178 passed).

Note: this uses the document-le…

title: Pan Behind tool doesn't snap the anchor point to its own layer's centre / corners
author: square3ang
body:
## Summary
With the Pan Behind (Anchor Point) tool, dragging the anchor snaps to other layers, the comp centre, guides and the grid, but not to the layer's own centre, corners or edge midpoints. After Effects snaps the anchor to the layer's own box, which is the usual way to recentre a pivot (e.g. on a text layer).

## Steps to reproduce
1. Select a text or shape layer, press **Y** (Pan Behind).
2. With snapping on (or holding Ctrl), drag the anchor point near the middle of the layer.
3. It never snaps to the layer's centre.

## Cause
`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/viewer.rs`, `Gesture::Anchor`, calls `vt::snap(..., &[layer], ...)`, which passes the dragged layer in `exclude`. `viewer::targets` then skips all of that layer's features: its 9 box points as well as its anchor. Only the anchor needed excluding.

## Suggested fix
Add the layer's own 9 box features (corners, edge midpoints, centre, without its anchor) as extra targets for this gesture. The box doesn't move in comp space while the anchor is panned, because position compensates.

```diff
--- a/crates/ui-egui/src/panels/viewer.rs
-                let sc = vt::snap(app, &ctx, &ectx, &map, &[layer], &[want], mods);
+                let sc = vt::snap_anchor(app, &ctx, &ectx, &map, layer, want, mods);
--- a/crates/ui-egui/src/panels/viewer_tools.rs
 pub(crate) fn snap(...) -> [f64; 2] {
+    snap_with(app, ctx, ectx, map, exclude, sources, mods, Vec::new())
+}
+
+pub(crate) fn snap_anchor(app: &EffectcraftApp, ctx: &egui::Context, ectx: &EvalCtx, map: &ViewerMap, layer: LayerId, want: [f64; 2], mods: egui::Modifiers) -> [f64; 2] {
+    let own: Vec<vw::SnapTarget> = ectx.comp.layer(layer)
+        .map(|l| vw::layer_features(ectx, l).into_iter().take(9)
+            .map(|p| vw::SnapTarget::point(p, vw::PRI_LAYER, SnapSource::Layer(layer))).collect())
+        .unwrap_or_default();
+    let own = if own.len() == 9 { own } else { Vec::new() }; // no content bounds → only the anchor
+    snap_with(app, ctx, ectx, map,…

title: fix(automation): font-list test fails when JetBrains Nerd Font families are installed
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

`list_fonts_lists_families_with_styles` fails on an unchanged checkout when the machine has additional installed font families whose names contain `jetbrains`. The tool correctly returns the bundled JetBrains Mono plus those installed families, but the test requires the filtered count to equal one. This blocks the documented contributor test gate for this valid font configuration.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use the `main` baseline and native environment listed under Runtime or environment. Have JetBrainsMono Nerd Font families already installed in a standard font directory. The observed configuration contains the six installed families listed under Actual behavior.
2. Run the existing test without changing repository source or fonts:

```sh
cargo test --locked -p effectcraft-automation tests::list_fonts_lists_families_with_styles -- --exact --nocapture
```

The focused command was executed once in a fresh checkout. It reproduced the failure. No font installation, deletion or system configuration change was needed for that run. The exact version of the installed Nerd Font package was not measured; the family names returned by EffectCraft are recorded below.

## Expected behavior

The documented contributor tests should pass when `list_fonts` satisfies its contract with supported installed fonts. The tool describes its results as bundled and installed font families, and its `query` schema promises substring matching. The test should still verify the bundled family, its Regular style and the filter's behavior when additional matching installed families exist.

## Actual behavior

The test panics at `crates/automation/src/tests.rs:404:5` because `one["count"]` is seven while the assertion expects one. Cargo exits with status 101. The focused run reports zero passed, one failed and 13 filtered out.

title: New layers should take the label color of their Project item

body:
If I change an item's label color in the Project panel and then drag it into a comp, the new layer doesn't get that color. It gets a fixed color for its type instead (images are always Lavender, comps Sandstone, etc.).

body:
## Summary
The usage text lists `hevc` and `av1` as formats and the README says "HEVC (Main / Main 10) and AV1 MP4". With `--format hevc` or `--format av1` and an `.mp4` output, the file written is H.264 (`avc1`). The two outputs are byte-identical. The status line reports the preset as `Custom`.

## Environment
- Ubuntu (headless, no display), effectcraft-cli 0.3.1 (linux x86_64 release tarball)
- Project: one 1280x720 30 fps comp "Main" (solid + Japanese text layer), `--end 0.5`

## Steps to reproduce
```sh
B=effectcraft-cli
$B render --project main.ecproj --comp Main --out h_hevc.mp4 --format hevc --end 0.5
ffprobe -v error -show_entries stream=codec_name,codec_tag_string -of csv=p=0 h_hevc.mp4
$B render --project main.ecproj --comp Main --out h_av1.mp4 --format av1 --end 0.5
ffprobe -v error -show_entries stream=codec_name,codec_tag_string -of csv=p=0 h_av1.mp4
md5sum h_hevc.mp4 h_av1.mp4
```
Same result with `--profile main` and with `--bitrate 2000` added.

## Expected
`hevc` (`hvc1`/`hev1`) and `av1` (`av01`) streams, as in `--format` in the usage text and README "Export".

## Actual
```
Main → h_hevc.mp4 (1280×720, 15 frames, Custom)
h264,avc1
Main → h_av1.mp4 (1280×720, 15 frames, Custom)
h264,avc1
md5: 2561d433... for both files (without extra options); 045365cb... for both with --bitrate 2000
```
Also: `--format hevc --out x.mov` wrote ProRes, and `--format av1 --out x.webm` wrote VP9. `--format webm --webm-codec av1` correctly wrote AV1, and `--format h264/prores/webm/gif/png/wav` produced the expected streams.
For comparison, MCP `get_state` lists `"export":["H264","Hevc","Av1",...]`.

## Notes
- n=6 renders (hevc and av1, each with no extra option, `--profile main`, `--bitrate 2000`) plus the .mov/.webm cases.
- Not tested: the `--queue` path and the GUI Output Module, which may select HEVC/AV1 correctly.

title: Locked Composition viewer still switches to another comp
author: RalekArts
body:
Steps:
1. Have Comp 1 showing in the Composition viewer and Comp 2 open in a second viewer tab next to it.
2. Lock the "Composition: Comp 1" viewer tab (and the Comp 1 Timeline tab).
3. Double-click Comp 2 in the Project panel.

Result: the locked viewer switches to Comp 2 (its tab becomes "Composition: Comp 2"), even though it's locked and there's already a Comp 2 viewer right next to it.

It doesn't matter how Comp 1 got there. I tried unlocking both, double-clicking Comp 1 in the Project panel, locking both again, then double-clicking Comp 2, and it still switched.

Expected (like After Effects' viewer lock): the locked viewer keeps Comp 1, and Comp 2 shows in the existing Comp 2 viewer.

Looks like an ordering problem in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/viewers.rs`:
- The Project panel runs `comp.open` right away, so Comp 2 becomes the active comp mid-frame.
- Later in the same frame, `viewers::show` for the active viewer does `app.ui.viewers.insert(id, active_comp)` (~line 77), which overwrites the viewer's stored comp (Comp 1) with Comp 2.
- On the next frame `on_open_comp` handles the `OpenComp` event, compares the stored comp to Comp 2, sees they match, and skips the lock.

Recording the viewer's comp before `comp.open` changes the active comp, or not overwriting it in `show` while an `OpenComp` is pending, should fix it.

**System info**
- EffectCraft 0.3.1 (.deb from releases)
- Ubuntu 26.04.1, KDE Plasma 6.6.6
- AMD RX 9070 XT, Mesa 26.0.8

title: fix(cli): early-closing stdout reader causes a broken-pipe panic
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Piping the documented `info --json` command into `head` causes the CLI to panic when the reader closes stdout early. The producer exits with status 101 and prints a Rust panic diagnostic. This breaks pipelines that check producer failures, despite the downstream reader completing successfully.

## Runtime or environment

- Published release: v0.3.1, tag commit `e6c817bb3f382b7fd71307baba9bb3427ce77fd9`, the latest release when checked.
- Current default branch inspected: `main` at `a6e6e2938c3f71062ea7653962186e726ab80237`. The relevant source is unchanged from the release; no equivalent fix was present. I did not build or execute main.
- Executed binary: `effectcraft-cli-0.3.1-macos-universal.zip` on macOS, Darwin 27.0.0, Apple silicon. Archive SHA-256 `960f5ed56e0bf4e481f0582f2e511f6866d22b647d4ed47cfc1340dc72641add` matched the release checksum file. Extracted executable SHA-256 `4b40ee223b5163bd17184e2d25db68b0dcb989dc6e63488df183a950aa0f879b`.
- Headless probes used a disposable working directory and an isolated `EFFECTCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR`; no desktop application was started.

## Steps to reproduce

With the release CLI on PATH, run this in a disposable directory:

```sh
bash -o pipefail -c 'effectcraft-cli info --json | head -c 1500 >/dev/null'
echo "$?"
```

As a control and workaround, run:

```sh
effectcraft-cli info --json > info.json
head -c 1500 info.json >/dev/null
```

## Expected behavior

An early-closing stdout reader must not cause a panic. The project's Never crash contract requires an actionable error rather than a crash; an intentional early close should be handled without a Rust panic diagnostic.

## Actual behavior

The failing pipeline exited 101. `head` exited 0 and consumed 1,500 bytes. The release reproduced the same producer panic on three direct pipeline attempts and one Bash pipefail attempt. Stderr included:

```text
thread 'main' (...) panicked at /rustc/.../library/std/src/io/stdio.rs:1168:9:
failed printing to stdout: Broke…

title: Preview audio goes silent ~12:36 into long audio/video files
author: RalekArts
body:
I imported a long video (about 22 minutes). When previewing, the audio cuts out a little over 12.5 minutes into the clip and stays silent for the rest of it. The cut-off point is tied to the source file, not the comp: it moves with the layer if I slide it in time, and it stays at the same spot in the clip even if I trim the start of the layer with Alt+[.

It looks like it happens to any file longer than about 12:36 at the default 48 kHz preview sample rate. The cached preview audio in `~/.cache/effectcraft/Conformed Audio/` for my file has sound up to 12:37.76 and is pure silence after that. Lowering Preview Sample Rate (Preferences → Audio) to 24 kHz works around it.

One more thing: the broken cached audio file sticks around, so after a fix people will probably need to delete their Conformed Audio cache (or it should get rebuilt automatically).

title: fix(docs): web hosting guide applies year-long immutable caching to unhashed app files
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

The web release's hosting guide (`packaging/web/README.md`, shipped as `HOSTING.md` in the web ZIP) says the app's `.js` and `.wasm` files have content-hashed names, so they "can be cached forever". It tells hosts to send `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` on them. The shipped `_headers` and `.htaccess` samples apply the same rule to every `.js` and `.wasm` file. The build actually emits fixed names (`effectcraft_web.js`, `effectcraft_web_bg.wasm`, `worker.js`, `audio-worklet.js`, `sw.js`), and these names are identical in consecutive releases. A host followed this advice and upgraded in place from the previous release to the latest one. A returning browser page not controlled by the service worker then kept running the previous release from the HTTP cache. The page got the new `index.html` but never requested the new glue or wasm. Pages controlled by the default service worker were not affected beyond the designed one-visit delay, because the worker precaches with `cache: "reload"`.

author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Make each MCP `add_effect` call a single unit of history: a successful call records one undo state for the effect and all of its `values`, and a call that returns an error leaves the project unchanged, the way `batch` behaves by default.

## Problem to solve

`add_effect` applies the effect and then sets each `values` entry as a separate edit (`crates/automation/src/tools.rs`). Each edit becomes its own history state, and a failure partway through leaves the earlier edits in place even though the tool reports `isError: true`. title: feat(cli): report .jsxbin files as unsupported in `effectcraft-cli script`
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

`effectcraft-cli script FILE` runs any file as JavaScript text, so a compiled After Effects `.jsxbin` script fails with `SyntaxError: unexpected '@'` instead of the clear "not supported" message that `file.runScript` and the script installer already give for the same file.

## Problem to solve

Many After Effects scripts are distributed only as compiled `.jsxbin` files. EffectCraft deliberately does not run them (docs/parity.md lists `.jsxbin` as out of clean-room scope), and two entry points already say so plainly: `file.runScript` returns "binary .jsxbin scripts are not supported: run the .jsx source" (`crates/engine/src/commands/file_more.rs`), and `file.installScript` returns "scripts are .jsx or .js files (.jsxbin is not supported)" (`crates/engine/src/commands/scripts.rs`). That message suggests a typo in the script rather than an unsupported format, and it does not point the user to the `.jsx` source.

Observed with the v0.3.1 macOS universal release CLI (`effectcraft-cli 0.3.1`) and with `effectcraft-cli` built from `main` at 2522bbe7f0e05c6b5ef0034224b977d359ca6113, both on macOS (Darwin 27.0, Apple silicon), using a file that starts with the JSXBIN header; both builds gave the same output:

author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

The parameter schemas for `comp.new` and `comp.settings` list a top-level property named `advanced3D`. Parameter validation accepts that key, but neither command reads it. A call such as `comp.new {"advanced3D": true}` succeeds and creates a Classic 3D composition. The params doc names `advanced3D` only as a value of `renderer` (`renderer? classic3D|advanced3D`). Setting a render queue item's output path with `renderQueue.setOutput` (Output To) to a file ending in `.mp4` changes an HEVC or AV1 Output Module to H.264, and the render then writes an H.264 file. `.mp4` is the extension EffectCraft itself gives HEVC and AV1 output, so this happens even when the path is the item's own default output name. title: fix(docs): web hosting guide says the wasm is about 13 MB (5 MB compressed), but the release wasm is 58 MB
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

The web hosting guide (`packaging/web/README.md`, shipped in the web release ZIP as `HOSTING.md`) tells hosts that the app's `.wasm` is "about 13 MB, or 5 MB with compression", and that gzip or Brotli "takes the download from about 13 MB to about 5 MB". title: Preview with audio stays silent until the whole work area is cached
author: square3ang
body:
## Summary
Since #127 (fix for #103), playback with audio on stays silent until every frame from the playhead to the end of the preview, or everything that fits in the RAM preview, has been cached. On any normal-length work area, sound only arrives near the end or on the second loop. That holds even when the comp renders comfortably in real time.

## Steps to reproduce
1. A 30 s comp with an audio layer and light content that renders in real time.
2. Purge the cache, press Space.
3. Frames play at full rate, but there's no sound until the whole work area has rendered.

## Cause
`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`, `advance_playback`: held audio starts only when `cached_ahead(&p, &series, cur, self.frames_that_fit(..))` holds, meaning the whole rest of the preview is cached. During playback, the prefetch only requests a small window ahead of the playhead (`(frames_parallelism()*2).max(4)` frames). So that condition can't become true until everything has rendered.

## Suggested fix
Keep #103's guarantee (no sound over skipped frames), but also start the sound once the silent preview keeps real time and the prefetch window is cached:

```diff
+    /// The preview has been playing in real time for the last ~quarter second up to `now`.
+    pub fn keeps_up(&self, now: f64) -> bool {
+        let step = self.plan.map_or(1, |p| p.step).max(1) as f64;
+        let frame = step / self.fps.max(1.0);
+        let (Some(a), Some(b)) = (self.shown_at.front(), self.shown_at.back()) else { return false };
+        self.shown_at.len() >= 3 && b - a >= (0.25f64).max(2.0 * frame) && now - b <= 2.0 * frame && self.real_time() == Some(true)
+    }
@@ advance_playback
-            && self.cached_ahead(&p, &series, cur, self.frames_that_fit(&c, scale))
+            && ((self.playback.keeps_up(now) && self.cached_ahead(&p, &series, cur, ahead.min(self.frames_that_fit(&c, scale))))
+                || self.cached_ahead(&p, &series, cur, self.frames_that_fit(&c, scale)))
@@ stall fallback
         …

title: Audio Spectrum / Audio Waveform are frozen in the Composition viewer and preview (export is fine)
author: square3ang
body:
## Summary
A solid with **Audio Spectrum** (or **Audio Waveform**) pointing at an audio layer shows the same frame for the whole preview, usually the empty baseline from the first rendered frame. Exporting through the Render Queue or CLI renders the spectrum correctly.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Comp with an audio layer (music) and a solid.
2. Apply Effect ▸ Generate ▸ Audio Spectrum to the solid, set Audio Layer to the audio layer.
3. Scrub or play the preview. The spectrum never changes. Export the same comp, and it animates.

## Cause
The viewer's layer cache (`crates/render/src/cache.rs`, `key_any`) adds the frame time to a layer's key only when `time_dependent(layer)` is true, which checks `effectcraft_effects::TIME_DEPENDENT`. `ec.generate.audiospectrum` and `ec.generate.audiowaveform` are missing from that list, but both read the Audio Layer's samples at the current time (`generate3.rs`, `audio_window` → `host.audio(...)`). So their layer gets one cache key for every frame. Export doesn't use the layer cache, which is why it works.

`time_dependence_is_declared` in `effects/src/lib.rs` didn't catch it because it runs effects without an audio host, so the visualisers pass through unchanged at both test times.

## Suggested fix
```diff
--- a/crates/effects/src/lib.rs
     "ec.text.timecode",
     "ec.text.numbers",
+    // The audio visualisers read the Audio Layer's samples around the frame time.
+    "ec.generate.audiospectrum",
+    "ec.generate.audiowaveform",
     // Path Text's jitter changes every frame.
```
I added a test, `audio_spectrum_follows_time_through_the_layer_cache` in `render/src/tests_audio_fx.rs`. The audio is silent until 0.5 s and then plays a 1 kHz tone. The test renders t=0.8 s with a shared `LayerCache` after first rendering t=0, then compares the result with an uncached render. Before the fix, the cached frame showed the stale baseline (216 vs 345 px). With the fix, render passes 179 tests and effects passes 413.

Remaining gap: the ca…

title: [Bug] Equal-length footage replacement exports stale pixels through a reused browser worker
author: Jagalite
body:

title: [Bug] Chrome DPR2 startup crashes in Project panel scrollbar clamp
author: Jagalite
body:
Opening the empty browser editor at 1280 x 800 CSS pixels with devicePixelRatio 2 crashes during the first Project panel render in Chrome. The canvas goes blank and the command channel stops responding.

Confirmed on main `172b7cfcc0f15eabb4908a6033e43aca7b1e918d`, using a freshly built browser bundle.

Reproduction:
1. Serve the production browser bundle with its usual cross-origin isolation headers.
2. Open Chrome with a fresh profile, viewport 1280 x 800, deviceScaleFactor 2.
3. Navigate to `?empty&storage=memory&noworkers&nosw`.
4. Wait for the first UI render.

Console reports:
```text
min > max, or either was NaN. min = 16.0, max = -7.4400024
```
The Wasm stack includes `effectcraft_ui_egui::panels::project::show`; the page raises `RuntimeError: unreachable`. Source inspection points to the vertical scrollbar thumb calculation that clamps to a lower bound of 16 even when the track height is smaller. This is a suspected cause based on the stack and matching clamp bounds.

The Chrome DPR2 crash reproduced twice in isolated contexts. Chrome DPR1 passed with the same viewport and URL. Firefox and WebKit passed at DPR1 and twice at DPR2, including creation of a 32 x 32 blue CPU composition and independent exact-pixel PNG decoding.

Browsers: Chrome 154.0.8037.93, Firefox 155.0, WebKit 26.6. These are standalone headless browser checks with emulated density, without canvas instrumentation, mocked app commands, or modified production bundle bytes. Physical displays and native GUI are unqualified.

Expected: a short or crowded Project panel handles scrollbar dimensions safely and leaves the editor usable.

Checked all 86 open and closed issues before filing. #45 describes Project details clipping but does not report this startup panic.

title: mcp: keyframe tools take layer time while reads use comp time, so keys land silently outside offset layers
author: pat-the-wizard
body:
### Summary
On a layer that does not start at 0 (typically a precomp layer), the MCP tools don't agree on the time base. `add_keyframe`, `set_property` with `time`, `prop.addKey`, `keys.select` and `keys.set` take **layer time**. `get_property`, `render_frame` and comp navigation use **comp time**. The scripting API (`setValueAtTime`, `keyTime`) also uses comp time, like After Effects; I verified that. An agent that writes keys with one tool and checks them with another therefore puts keys seconds away from where it meant to, and nothing warns about it.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Create a comp (20 s) and add a precomp layer `A` with `startTime = 10.5` (e.g. via `layer.timing {start: 10.5}`).
2. Add an effect with an animatable parameter to `A`, then call `add_keyframe {layer:"A", path:"effects/#1/<param>", keys:[{time:15.3,value:0},{time:16.0,value:100}]}`, intending comp 15.3–16.0.
3. Call `get_property {layer:"A", path:"effects/#1/<param>", time:15.65}`.

**Expected:** 50, or at least a warning that the keys fall outside the layer.
**Actual:** 0. The keys landed at comp 25.8 and 26.5, beyond the layer's out point. No warning.

### Notes
- This is documented ("Keyframe times are layer time", `docs/agents.md:73-74`), but the tool descriptions are uneven:
  - `get_property` says comp time (`tools.rs:558`).
  - `add_keyframe` and `set_property` say layer time (`tools.rs:572`, `:588`).
  - `prop.addKey` and `prop.set` don't say which.
  - `keys.set` says "layer s".
- I also couldn't find how to set a layer's start time at first (I looked for `layer.setStartTime`). `layer.timing {start}` does it, but `docs/agents.md` doesn't mention it.

### Proposal
- Add an optional `timeBase: "layer" | "comp"` to `prop.set`, `prop.addKey`, `keys.set` and `keys.select`. They share `snapped_key_time` (`prop.rs:53-58`) and `anim.rs:209`. Keep `layer` as the default so nothing breaks.
- Echo `compTime` in the reply, and add a `warning` when a key lands outside the layer's in/out range.

title: mcp: headless server has no autosave, so unsaved work is lost when the client restarts the server
author: pat-the-wizard
body:
### Summary
The headless `effectcraft mcp` server keeps the project only in memory. When the MCP client restarts or reconnects the server, a fresh process starts with an empty project, and all unsaved work is gone. The desktop app has autosave and crash recovery; the headless path has neither. This bit me during a longer agent-driven session.

### What I found in the code
- `McpServer::serve` loops until EOF, then the process exits (`server.rs:74-83`).
- `effectcraft_host::session()` sets no config directory and loads no settings.
- `autosave_tick` is only called from the UI (`ui-egui/src/lib.rs:1483`).
- `app.saveProjectOnCrash` in the scripting prelude is accepted but does nothing (`prelude.js:1744`).

### Proposal
An opt-in `mcp --autosave` (or a setting):
- In the `mcp` branch (`main.rs:561`), set `session.config` and call `load_settings()`.
- Call `autosave_tick` after each request.
- Save a dirty project to the autosave location on EOF.
- Test it in `crates/automation/src/tests.rs` with a temporary `EFFECTCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR`.

A larger follow-up could let a new MCP process reattach to a running engine.

It seems to fit AGENTS.md's "never lose work". I'm happy to implement the opt-in flag if this approach works for you.

**Environment:** EffectCraft 0.4.0 (release build), Linux x64, driven through the headless MCP server (`effectcraft mcp`), CPU renderer. Code references in this issue are against `main` @ `72a2d47`, from reading the source, so please correct me where I misread it.

title: Fractal Noise: Noise Type "Soft Linear" shows a visible square lattice
author: pat-the-wizard
body:
### Steps to reproduce
Apply `Fractal Noise` to a 1920×1080 solid with these settings:
- Fractal Type: Turbulent Basic (index 2)
- Noise Type: Soft Linear (index 2, the default)
- Contrast: 140
- Brightness: −35
- Scale: 420
- Evolution: `time*25`

**Actual:** a regular square grid is clearly visible, aligned to the noise cells, and it stays visible as the noise evolves. Switching Noise Type to Spline removes it.
**Expected:** Soft Linear looks smooth, with no visible lattice.

### Possible cause (from reading the code)
- Soft Linear goes to `value_noise` (`noise3.rs:148-149`), which uses the quintic fade `t³(6t²−15t+10)` on each axis (`generate.rs:282-290`). That fade has zero slope on every lattice line.
- The turbulent fold `1 − |s|` (`noise3.rs:206`) and the high contrast turn those flat lines into visible creases.
- Spline (Catmull-Rom) keeps non-zero slopes, which fits the observation that it doesn't show the grid.

`value_noise` has many callers and is mirrored in `fx_noise.wgsl`, so a fix would probably be limited to the Fractal/Turbulent Noise path, with CPU-vs-GPU and determinism tests.

**Environment:** EffectCraft 0.4.0 (release build), Linux x64, driven through the headless MCP server (`effectcraft mcp`), CPU renderer. Code references in this issue are against `main` @ `72a2d47`, from reading the source, so please correct me where I misread it.

title: mcp: get_project says GPU acceleration is on but renders on CPU without saying why; `mcp --gpu` is undocumented
author: pat-the-wizard
body:
### Summary
`get_project` reports:
```json
{"active":"cpu","adapter":null,"gpuAcceleration":true,"renderer":"Mercury GPU Acceleration"}
```
That reads as "the GPU is enabled but broken". In fact the headless MCP server only uses a GPU when started with `--gpu` (`apps/effectcraft-cli/src/main.rs:324-326`, `docs/architecture.md:271`). `docs/agents.md` doesn't mention `mcp --gpu`.

When `--gpu` fails, the adapter error only goes to `log::info!` (`context.rs:711-712`), and the CLI installs no logger, so the reason is never visible.

### Proposal
- Add a `why` field to `render.backend` / `get_project`, e.g. "headless default: CPU; start with --gpu", or the adapter error.
- Document `mcp --gpu` in `docs/agents.md`, including how to pass it in an MCP client config.
- Add an engine/automation test of the status JSON.

**Environment:** EffectCraft 0.4.0 (release build), Linux x64, driven through the headless MCP server (`effectcraft mcp`), CPU renderer. Code references in this issue are against `main` @ `72a2d47`, from reading the source, so please correct me where I misread it.

title: Text: font fallback picks a font whose glyph for the character is empty
author: prekabreki
body:
## Context
`fonts::tests::cjk_falls_back_to_a_system_family` fails on `main` whenever the whole `effectcraft-text` suite runs in parallel. It passes when run alone or with `--test-threads=1`:

```
thread 'fonts::tests::cjk_falls_back_to_a_system_family' panicked at crates/text/src/fonts.rs:772:13:
あ → Black Mountain
```

Black Mountain is a free decorative font installed on that machine (`~/.local/share/fonts/BlackMountain-vmlBZ.ttf`, Linux). Its cmap maps 57,524 code points, including あ, 水, ア and 。, but those glyphs are empty (0 contours, checked with fontTools). fontconfig leaves them out of the font's charset for that reason.

`Face::glyph` (`fonts.rs:207`) treats any non-zero cmap entry as coverage, so `has_char` reports that Black Mountain covers Japanese. `fallback_for` (`fonts.rs:604`) tries "anything loaded already" before the script-aware `system_fallback`. Once another test in the same run has loaded that face's bytes, `fallback_for('あ', Inter)` returns it.

The test failure is the visible part. In the app, Japanese text in a Latin-only family can presumably fall back to a loaded font whose glyphs for it are blank, so the text would render as nothing. That consequence is inferred from the code and was not reproduced in the UI.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A character whose cmap glyph is empty (no outline, no bitmap) doesn't count as covered for fallback, so `fallback_for` and `system_fallback` skip that face. Space-like characters such as U+0020 and U+3000, which are legitimately blank, still count as covered.
- [ ] `cjk_falls_back_to_a_system_family` passes in a normal parallel `cargo test` run on a machine with such a font installed.
- [ ] A regression test exercises a face that maps a character to an empty glyph and asserts that fallback skips it. It must not depend on fonts installed on the test machine; build or embed a minimal font fixture under the repo's asset rules (`cargo xtask assets`).

## Files / where this lives
- `crates/text/src/fonts.rs`:…

title: Feature requests: native support for common AE script workflows
author: barchukmov
body:
### Feature requests
These are features After Effects users rely on third-party scripts and plugins for. They should be built into the software natively. Even if they're out of scope for now, the architecture should leave room for them.

- [ ] **Layer groups in the timeline.** Very important, and not possible in After Effects today. Would be a big organizational improvement and would let you apply effects to multiple layers at once. Continuously rasterized pre-comps already do something similar, but without the option to manipulate the pre-comp's contents from its parent.
- [ ] **Reorderable render stack.** Let users interleave layer styles, transform, track matte, effects and masks in any order (e.g. effect → mask → effect). After Effects hard-codes this order, which forces pre-comps for simple layers.
- [ ] **World-space layer sampling.** Effects can currently only sample other layers in layer space, so both layers need the same size and position for the result to look right. A layer should be able to sample another in world space regardless of either layer's position, scale or rotation, the way track mattes work.
- [ ] **Temporary transform of multiple layers.** Select several layers and scale/rotate them around a shared, user-defined bounding box without moving anchor points or creating a null.
- [ ] **Preview vs. render views.** Hide layers or disable effects in a working (preview) view, then switch to render view to see the final result.
- [ ] **Move anchor point while keeping animation.** Add a 3x3 grid control that snaps the anchor point to one of nine points on the layer bounds, with the animation compensated to follow the new anchor.
- [ ] **Adjustable easy ease.** A slider from 0 (linear) to 100% (speed graph handle pushed to its maximum influence). Made and remade dozens of times as scripts for After Effects.
- [ ] **Motion presets.** Saved graph shapes that can be applied to keyframes.

title: Missing in 0.4.0: Ability to import and work with image sequences
author: HSaouma
body:
**Feature Description**

Note: If this feature already exists in 0.4.0 and I missed the option, my apologies! Please feel free to guide me on how to do it! Otherwise, please see the details below.

In VFX, 3D render pipelines, and animation workflows, working with image sequences (e.g., .png, .exr, .tif, .jpg) is an essential standard. 
Currently, version 0.4.0 lacks support for multiple features for treating a numbered sequence of images as a single playable video clip.

**Key Capabilities Needed**
To match standard industry workflows (similar to After Effects' Import Sequence and Interpret Footage functionality), the following features are required:

1. Sequence Recognition on Import
An option or checkbox in the file picker to detect and import a folder/range of numbered images (e.g., frame_0001.png to frame_0250.png) as a single media asset.

2. Frame Rate Control (Interpret Footage)
Ability to specify or override the sequence's target frame rate (e.g., 24, 25, 29.97, 30, or 60 fps) upon or after import.

3. Sequence Management Options
Alpha Channel Handling: Choose between Premultiplied or Straight (Unmatted) alpha interpret modes.
Missing Frame Behavior: Options for how the software handles missing sequence numbers (e.g., hold previous frame, show a missing frame error/color, or skip).
Timecode / Start Frame Offset: Ability to define the starting frame number or custom timecode offset.

title: fix(cli): render --out resolves a relative path against the project folder, not the working directory
author: Oldrich333
body:
> Agent-written on behalf of @Oldrich333 · agent: hive-admin/main · model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 · origin: owner-requested

## Summary
`effectcraft-cli render --out <relative path>` joins the path to the project file's directory, not to the current working directory. Every other CLI path argument (`--project` included) is cwd-relative, so a path that already names the project directory is doubled, and a relative output path never lands where the shell user expects.

## Runtime or environment
- EffectCraft 0.4.0 release (`effectcraft-0.4.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`, SHA256 verified), `effectcraft-cli`, headless, Linux x86_64.

## Steps to reproduce
Project at `work/ec/proj/x.ecproj` with comp `C`:
```sh
cd work/ec
effectcraft-cli render --project proj/x.ecproj --comp C --out proj/out/d.mp4
effectcraft-cli render --project proj/x.ecproj --comp C --out e.mp4
cd elsewhere && effectcraft-cli render --project /abs/work/ec/proj/x.ecproj --comp C --out out/card.mp4
```

## Expected behavior
A relative `--out` resolves against the current working directory, like `--project`: `work/ec/proj/out/d.mp4`, `work/ec/e.mp4`, `elsewhere/out/card.mp4`.

## Actual behavior
- `--out proj/out/d.mp4` → `done: C → proj/proj/out/d.mp4`; file at `work/ec/proj/proj/out/d.mp4` (project directory doubled).
- `--out e.mp4` → `C → proj/e.mp4` (project-relative, not cwd).
- from another cwd, `--out out/card.mp4` → written to `<project dir>/out/card.mp4`, nothing in cwd.
- `--out ./f.mp4` → `<project dir>/./f.mp4`. An absolute `--out` works. Exit code 0 in all cases; the log line shows the real path.

title: segment: weighted_nms loops forever on a NaN or zero-area detection box
author: KazW
body:
## Summary

`mediapipe::weighted_nms` loops forever when a detection's box is degenerate: any NaN coordinate, or zero area. Each pass partitions `dets`, including `top` itself, by `iou(d, top) > NMS_IOU`. For a degenerate box, `iou(top, top)` is `0.0` (the `union > 0.0` guard fails), so `top` lands in `rest`. Then `dets = rest` never shrinks, and `while let Some(top) = dets.first()` spins.

Found while reviewing CharacterCraft (github.com/KazW/CharacterCraft), which carries an attributed copy of `crates/segment` from rev d60cb71e. The code is unchanged at `main` cae67546.

## Where (main @ cae67546)

- `crates/segment/src/mediapipe.rs:110`: `dets.into_iter().partition(|d| iou(&d.bbox, &top.bbox) > NMS_IOU)`.
- `crates/segment/src/mediapipe.rs:96-102`: `iou` returns `0.0` when `union` is not `> 0` (NaN or zero area).
- It is called from `FaceLandmarker::detect` (`mediapipe.rs:187`).

**Reachability.** A NaN or zero-area box needs NaN or exactly-zero detector regressors. I could not trigger it with the pinned official weights: a NaN or infinite input pixel is cleared by the ReLUs, and every score stays finite. So it takes a non-official detector loaded through the public `FaceLandmarker::from_task`, or a future model or interpreter change. `segment::load` checks the SHA-256, so the app path isn't exposed today. It is still a hang, not an error, which is why I'm reporting it.

## Reproduction

Copy `iou` and `weighted_nms` from `main` verbatim into a scratch binary, with `NMS_IOU = 0.3` and the `Detection` struct, and call it:

```rust
let d = Detection { bbox: [f32::NAN; 4], keypoints: [[f32::NAN; 2]; 6], score: 0.7 };
weighted_nms(vec![d]); // never returns
```

A zero-area box hangs the same way: `Detection { bbox: [0.0; 4], keypoints: [[0.0; 2]; 6], score: 0.7 }`.

**Expected:** it returns, for example one output per degenerate detection.

**Actual:** it never returns. `timeout 10` kills it with exit 124.

## The fix we applied

`top` always joins its own cluster, …

title: segment: tiny hostile .tflite aborts the process (unbounded CONV_2D scratch allocation in Model::run)
author: KazW
body:
## Summary

`tflite::Model::read` accepts a tiny model whose `CONV_2D` needs an enormous scratch buffer. `Model::run` then aborts the process (SIGABRT, `memory allocation of 549755813888 bytes failed`). An abort is not a panic, so `catch_unwind` cannot recover from it. `MAX_TENSOR` bounds each tensor, but nothing bounds a kernel's scratch space or the model's total work.

Found while reviewing CharacterCraft (github.com/KazW/CharacterCraft), which carries an attributed copy of `crates/segment` from rev d60cb71e. The code is unchanged at `main` cae67546.

## Where (main @ cae67546)

- `crates/segment/src/nn.rs:117`, `Conv::forward_sized`: `let mut patch = vec![0.0f32; ow * kk];` allocates `ow · ks² · inp` floats per output row. Only `ow` (through the output tensor) and `ks² · inp` (through the filter tensor) are bounded, each separately, by `MAX_TENSOR`.
- `crates/segment/src/tflite.rs:113`: `MAX_TENSOR = 1 << 28` is a per-tensor cap only.
- `crates/segment/src/tflite.rs:365`: CONV_2D is accepted with any kernel side.

**Reachability.** `segment::load` checks the SHA-256 before parsing, so the app path with the pinned official model is not exposed. The public `tflite::Model::read` / `Model::run` and `mediapipe::FaceLandmarker::from_task` are.

## Reproduction

Build an 8,616-byte model with one `CONV_2D`:
- input `x`: `[1, 1, 33554432, 1]`, float32, no buffer;
- filter `w`: `[1, 64, 64, 1]`, float16, 4096 zero values (8 KB);
- output `y`: `[1, 1, 33554432, 1]`, float32;
- `Conv2DOptions`: padding SAME, stride 1.

All three shapes pass `MAX_TENSOR`, and SAME padding with stride 1 gives the declared output shape. It was built with the PyPI `flatbuffers` (25.12.19) and `tflite` (2.18.0) packages:

<details><summary>build script (Python)</summary>

```python
import importlib, flatbuffers, numpy as np
m = lambda n: importlib.import_module("tflite." + n)
M, SG, T, B, O, OC, C2, BO = (m(n) for n in ["Model", "SubGraph", "Tensor", "Buffer", "Operator", "OperatorCode", "Conv2…

title: segment: face crop samples differently from MediaPipe's ImageToTensor (landmarks offset by about a pixel)
author: KazW
body:
## Summary

`effectcraft_segment::face::crop` samples the frame with a different convention from MediaPipe's CPU `ImageToTensor`, so the pure-Rust Face Landmarker's landmarks are offset from MediaPipe's by about a pixel or more on large faces. It also makes the face detector disagree with MediaPipe on some frames.

Found while porting `crates/segment` to another project (a copy of rev d60cb71e). The code is unchanged at `main` 735482d.

## What differs

MediaPipe's `ImageToTensor` (`image_to_tensor_converter_opencv.cc`) maps the box corners to the output corners `(0,0)` to `(n,n)` and calls `cv::warpPerspective` (bilinear) on the uint8 frame. So:

1. Output pixel `i` is at `u = i/n`. `crop` uses `(i + 0.5)/n`.
2. The source position is used directly as a pixel-centre index. `crop` subtracts 0.5 first.
3. The result is rounded to a whole 0-255 value before the range map. `crop` keeps the float.
4. The face mesh input uses a replicate border (the detector uses a zero border). `crop` always uses zero.

The net effect is a shift of about `0.5 * roi_size / n - 0.5` pixels per axis: about 1 px for a 785 px ROI, and about 0 for a 200 px ROI. It grows with face size.

## Reproduction

Step 1: compare the crop with OpenCV on a synthetic frame (no model needed). In `crates/segment/src/face.rs` tests, crop a deterministic 64x48 frame (pixel `(x, y)`, channel `k` = `(x*7 + y*13 + k*50 + (x*y) % 11) % 256`) with `Roi { center: [30.0, 20.0], size: 40.0, angle: 0.3 }`, `n = 16`, range `[0, 1]`, and print the values times 255. Compute the same crop in Python with `cv2.getPerspectiveTransform` from the ROI's four corners (`to_frame(0,0)`, `(1,0)`, `(1,1)`, `(0,1)`) to `(0,0)`, `(16,0)`, `(16,16)`, `(0,16)`, then `cv2.warpPerspective(img, M, (16, 16), flags=cv2.INTER_LINEAR, borderMode=cv2.BORDER_CONSTANT)`.

Result on `main`: max absolute difference 242.7, mean 30.1 (0-255 scale; the pattern is noisy, so a half-pixel shift is large). With the change below, the difference is exactly …

title: Feature: 3D transform gizmos (move / rotate / scale) for selected 3D layers
author: doolecg
body:
# Feature: 3D transform gizmos (move / rotate / scale) for selected 3D layers

**Context:** I'm building an open-source Blender -> EffectCraft live-link/exporter (glTF 2.0 interchange + the control channel). It works - scenes, cameras, lights and animation come through and render in Advanced 3D - but the first thing you reach for after an import is the light or camera in the viewport, and there's nothing to grab.

## The gap

3D layers (models, cameras, lights, nulls) currently get only a small orientation axis at the anchor - display-only, no hit-testing, no dragging. Cameras and lights have no handles at all; after a Blender import you have to select the layer and type numbers into the timeline to place a sun or aim a camera. 2D layers already have the full 8-handle transform gizmo, so the hit-testing, drag-remapping and merged-undo machinery exists - it just hasn't been extended to 3D.

## Proposal

Interactive move / rotate / scale manipulators for selected 3D layers in the Composition viewer, in three phases:

1. **Move** - RGB axis arrows (X/Y/Z) from the layer's anchor, projected through the active camera, plus a screen-plane centre handle. Drag an arrow to translate along that axis. Cameras and lights also get a second manipulator on their Point of Interest (so you can aim an imported sun or camera by dragging).
2. **Rotate** - axis-aligned rings + an outer screen-plane ring, 15? snap with Shift.
3. **Scale** - per-axis + uniform, hidden for cameras/lights (which don't scale).

Mode toggle (W/E/R a la Blender, or cycling like AE's Q); local/world space switch in the tools bar.

## Why it fits EffectCraft's architecture

- All the plumbing exists: `EffectCtx::world_matrix`, `CameraState::projection`, the 2D handle pattern (`handle_hits`, `viewer.handle.<id>.<i>`), automation-id registration, merged-undo property edits.
- **No new engine commands** - drags commit through ordinary merged `prop.set` edits, so the CLI, MCP server and control channel replay identi…

title: OCIO effects with a custom config (Blender 4.5): Linear Rec.709 → sRGB gets no sRGB curve and a blue cast, AgX breaks
author: Romasikkk
body:
**Version:** EffectCraft 0.6.0, Windows 11 x64 (MSI)

I want to convert only specific layers (Blender EXR renders) through Blender's own OCIO config, the way I do in After Effects with the OpenColorIO plug-in. With Blender's config loaded, the OCIO effects don't apply the sRGB curve and they tint neutral greys blue.

**Steps**
1. 32 bpc project. Solid with Gradient Ramp: black at the left, white at the right (a linear 0…1 ramp).
2. Add **OCIO Color Space Transform**, Configuration = Custom,
   Config File = `C:\Program Files\Blender Foundation\Blender 4.5\4.5\datafiles\colormanagement\config.ocio`,
   Source = `Linear Rec.709`, Destination = `sRGB`.
3. Same again with **OCIO Display Transform**, Input = `Linear Rec.709`, Display = `sRGB`, View = `Standard`, and with View = `AgX`.

**Expected:** sRGB encoding of the ramp (input 0.18 → about 0.46), the same as the built-in config gives.

**Actual** (8-bit RGB of the rendered ramp at three grey inputs):
| Setup | grey 0.18 | grey 0.50 | grey 1.00 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Built-in config, Linear Rec.709 (sRGB) → sRGB (correct) | 118, 118, 118 | 188, 188, 188 | 255, 255, 255 |
| Blender config, Color Space Linear Rec.709 → sRGB | **44, 46, 50** | **121, 128, 139** | **242, 255, 255** |
| Blender config, Display sRGB / Standard | **44, 46, 50** | **121, 128, 139** | **242, 255, 255** |
| Blender config, Display sRGB / AgX | 0, 1, 1 | 85, 135, 203 | 255, 255, 255 |

So with Blender's config there is no sRGB curve, and neutral greys come out blue. Blender's reference space is `Linear CIE-XYZ E`, so I suspect the white point (E vs D65) isn't handled.

**Likely cause:** the config reader's supported subset (`crates/effects/src/ocio_config.rs`) doesn't include transforms that Blender's config uses. In Blender 4.5, `sRGB` is
```

  children:

    - !<ExponentWithLinearTransform> {gamma: 2.4, offset: 0.055, direction: inv…

title: Interpret Footage: option to read float EXRs as-is (no automatic linear → sRGB), for per-layer OCIO conversion
author: Romasikkk
body:
**Version:** EffectCraft 0.6.0, Windows 11 x64 (MSI)

Float EXRs are sRGB-encoded automatically on decode (`crates/media/src/convert.rs`, `dynamic_to_image`: "Float images … hold linear light and are sRGB-encoded here"), and Interpret Footage can't turn that off. That's a sensible default and it matches After Effects' "Interpret As Linear Light" for 32 bpc. I checked a Blender render against AE 2025 and the difference is 0.25/255.

But it blocks the other common workflow: keep the footage values untouched and convert only chosen layers with an OCIO effect, as in AE (Interpret As Linear Light = Off, plus the OpenColorIO effect) or in Nuke (Read node colorspace = raw).

**Steps**
1. 32 bpc project, import a linear EXR (Blender render).
2. Add **OCIO Color Space Transform** (built-in config), Linear Rec.709 → sRGB.

**Expected:** if the footage is interpreted as raw, one correct sRGB conversion.

**Actual:** the effect gets already-encoded values, so the conversion is applied twice: 58/255 mean error against sRGB(EXR), a very bright, washed-out image. Without the effect the picture is correct (0.25/255).

It also matters for data passes (Mist / depth / normals used as mattes or for effects), where the raw values are wanted.

**Request:** an Interpret Footage ▸ Color option for float footage, such as "Interpret As Linear Light: Off" / "Preserve RGB" / "Raw (non-colour)". With it, the layer gets the file's values unchanged and an OCIO effect on that layer is the only conversion. Ideally it would be per item and scriptable (`file.interpretFootage {colorProfile: "raw"}` or similar).

Related: #410 (OCIO effects with Blender's config — the other half of this workflow).

title: Layered EXR import (#387): Blender multilayer files would show CryptoMaterial00 instead of the beauty layer named "Image"
author: Romasikkk
body:
Follow-up to #295 / #387 (thanks, layered EXRs are exactly our case: Blender renders written by the compositor's File Output node in multilayer mode).

**Version:** 0.6.0 for the failing import; the fallback below is from reading `layered_image` in `crates/media/src/exr_channels.rs` on `main` (68d94b8). I haven't built `main` myself.

With 0.6.0 our files fail to import with `image does not contain non-deep rgb channels`. They have no `combined` / `beauty` / `rgba` layer. The beauty pass is named **`Image`**, Blender's default socket name. The layers in channel order:
```
CryptoMaterial00 (a,b,g,r float)  CryptoMaterial01  CryptoMaterial02
GlossCol  GlossDir  Image  Mist  VolDir   (A,B,G,R half, DWAA)
```
`layer_rgba` matches R/G/B case-insensitively, so `CryptoMaterial00` (lowercase `r,g,b`) counts as a colour layer. It comes first, so `rgb.first()` would pick **Cryptomatte data as the picture** instead of `Image`.

**Suggestions**
- Add `image` (and maybe `color`, `rgb`) to the preferred layer names.
- Skip `Crypto*` layers (and other data-only layers) in the fallback.
- Let users pick the picture layer in Interpret Footage, like the new EXtractoR layer popup.

**Check:** I copied `Image.*` into root `R,G,B,A` with OpenEXR (keeping all layers). That file imports in 0.6.0, and the picture matches After Effects to 0.26/255. EXtractoR then reads GlossDir from the same file as raw linear values (0.25/255 from the linear decode), so the multi-layer workflow itself works once the right layer is picked.

title: Render Queue export never uses the layer cache: every layer re-renders on every frame (export up to 2× slower; GPU export slower than CPU)
author: pat-the-wizard
body:
## Summary

Render Queue export renders every layer of every frame from scratch. `effectcraft_export::pipeline::Cx::render_at` builds its `Renderer` without a `cache`, so the layer cache that makes viewer playback fast ("static and transform-only layers render once", docs/architecture.md) is never attached to an export job. In motion-graphics projects most layers are static or animated only in their transform, so most of the export's CPU time repeats work it has already done. The GPU compositor suffers more: without cached buffers it re-uploads every layer on every frame, and GPU export ends up slower than CPU export.

## Environment

- EffectCraft 0.6.0, built from `d60cb71` (`cargo build --release`)
- Linux, AMD Ryzen 5 5600 (6 cores / 12 threads), AMD Radeon RX 6750 XT (RADV NAVI22, Vulkan)

## Project

A 69.5 s explainer, 1920×1080 at 60 fps (4,170 frames), Classic 3D. The main comp has 117 layers. It contains a 229-layer UI precomp, four 480×240 card precomps and a node precomp. Most layers are text and shape layers that fly in, fade or move (transform and opacity keyframes). A few static layers carry expensive effects (Gaussian Blur on a full-frame glow, Drop Shadow on panels). There are 68 expressions, mostly `toWorld` positions and a few `createPath` arcs. About 230 opacity-inheritance expressions were baked to keyframes, which changed the full render time by only about 1 % (848 s before, 840 s after).

## Measurements

All numbers come from the machine above, with the stock `effectcr

title: GPU export (Backend::Auto) gives different pixels from run to run
author: pat-the-wizard
body:
## Summary

Exporting the same span of the same project twice with GPU acceleration on produces two different files. Backend::Auto picks the compositor (CPU or GPU) for each top-level frame from measured frame times (`render::auto::AutoPick`, re-probed every `REPROBE` frames). The CPU and GPU compositors differ slightly, so a frame can come out a little differently depending on which side the timings happened to favour in that run. CPU-only export is deterministic.

## Environment

- EffectCraft 0.6.0, built from `d60cb71` (plus the export layer-cache patch from #413; the first run below predates it)
- Linux, AMD Ryzen 5 5600 (6 cores / 12 threads), AMD Radeon RX 6750 XT (RADV NAVI22, Vulkan)

## Steps

```bash
effectcraft-cli render project.ecproj --comp "Main" --gpu --start 20 --end 25 --out a.mp4
effectcraft-cli render project.ecproj --comp "Main" --gpu --start 20 --end 25 --out b.mp4
md5sum a.mp4 b.mp4
```

The project is a 1920×1080, 60 fps Classic 3D motion-graphics comp of about 350 layers in total (text, shapes, precomps, a moving camera).

## Observed

- The same binary run twice with `--gpu` gives different MD5s: `d3dd66ec40717987123a2180533a5f1f` and `458cd91bd4238551acef2a4cccd28b38`.
- Without `--gpu` (CPU only), repeated runs give byte-identical files: `b29d4fb6c31575e9be94fc3004ce6780` both times, across the two builds.
- Decoded frame by frame, those two GPU exports agree on the first 170 of 300 frames and differ from frame 170 on. The PSNR between them averages 69.0 dB (minimum 59.7 dB). Another pair of GPU runs, one before and one after the patch, diverged at frame 130. For comparison, a CPU and a GPU export of the same span differ on every frame (60.4 dB). So the differences have the size of the CPU/GPU compositor difference. They are invisible, but they are real.

## Expected

A final render should produce the same pixels on every run with the same settings, as After Effects does for a given renderer.

title: Composition viewer: text looks soft/jagged at "Fit" zoom (Auto → Half, minification without mipmaps)
author: Romasikkk
body: **Version:** EffectCraft 0.6.0, Windows 11 x64 (MSI), display scaling 150 % (pixelsPerPoint 1.5), RTX 4090 The rendered frames are clean. The viewer shows the same frame noticeably worse, which makes typography hard to judge in the app. **Steps** 1. 2560×1440 comp with large text (e.g. 200 px Inter Tight). 2. Viewer defaults: Resolution = Auto, magnification = fit (46 % here). Settings ▸ Previews ▸ Viewer Zoom Quality = More Accurate. 3. Compare with Resolution = Full, then with magnification exactly 50 % and 100 %. **Actual** (screenshots via `ui.screenshot`, attached): - Auto at 46 % renders the preview at Half (`Resolution::scale` switches below 75 %), so text is soft. - Full at 46 %: sharper but with stair-stepped edges. The frame is minified with a plain bilinear sampler and no mip levels (`zoom_texture_options` / `FilterMode::Linear`), so most source pixels are skipped below 50 %. - Full at exactly 50 %: clean. Full at 100 %: 1:1 and clean. - With Windows scaling at 150 %, `ui.set {viewer: {zoom}}` is in points, so the label reads zoom × 1.5. Not a bug, but easy to get wrong when scripting. - Viewer Resolution and zoom aren't remembered between launches (they aren't in `prefs.json`). **Suggestions:** mipmaps or an area/box downsample for the viewer texture below 100 %; maybe keep Full for paused frames when Auto is selected; remember the viewer resolution per project or globally. 2× crops of the viewer panel (top to bottom: Auto/fit 46 %, Full/fit 46 %, Full/50 %, Full/100 %):

title: Graph Editor: Improve Easy Ease In/Out controls and keyframe easing workflow
author: ReinFreebird
body:
## Summary

Improve the discoverability and usability of keyframe easing in the Graph Editor, particularly for applying Easy Ease In and Easy Ease Out to selected keyframes.

## Problem

Smooth keyframe animation is a fundamental motion-graphics workflow. Users familiar with After Effects expect to be able to apply easing quickly and predictably, then inspect and refine the resulting interpolation in the Graph Editor.

Although EffectCraft advertises Easy Ease and graph editing, the workflow for applying and managing easing could be clearer and easier to use.

## Expected behavior

* Provide an accessible way to apply Easy Ease In, Easy Ease Out, and Easy Ease to selected keyframes.
* Make it clear which easing/interpolation behavior is applied to the selected keyframes.
* Ensure the Graph Editor accurately reflects the resulting interpolation.
* Allow users to further refine easing through the existing graph handles and interpolation controls.
* Apply the behavior consistently to supported animatable properties.

## Acceptance criteria

* [ ] Users can easily discover and apply Easy Ease In, Easy Ease Out, and Easy Ease.
* [ ] Easing affects the intended selected keyframes.
* [ ] The Graph Editor reflects the applied easing correctly.
* [ ] Editing the graph preserves the intended interpolation behavior.
* [ ] Existing linear, Bezier, and hold interpolation behavior remains correct.

## Additional context

The goal is to improve the workflow and consistency of easing controls, not to introduce a second, incompatible keyframe interpolation system.

title: Composition Settings: Allow editing composition properties after creation
author: ReinFreebird
body:
## Summary

Ensure users can reopen Composition Settings and modify an existing composition's properties after it has been created.

## Problem

Composition settings are fundamental to motion-graphics projects. Users may need to change resolution, frame rate, or duration as their project requirements evolve.

Currently, I cannot change these settings after creating a composition. This makes it difficult to adapt an existing project without creating a replacement composition or manually working around the limitation.

## Expected behavior

* Allow users to reopen Composition Settings for an existing composition.
* Allow editing the composition's width, height, frame rate, and duration.
* Validate changes and clearly communicate invalid values.
* Apply changes to the existing composition rather than requiring users to recreate it.
* Preserve existing layers, keyframes, and other project content wherever possible.
* Clearly handle changes that affect timing, rendering, or nested compositions.

## Acceptance criteria

* [ ] Existing compositions can be reopened in Composition Settings.
* [ ] Resolution, frame rate, and duration can be edited.
* [ ] Changes are reflected in the composition and its preview.
* [ ] Existing animation and layer content are preserved where applicable.
* [ ] Invalid settings cannot silently corrupt the project.
* [ ] Undo/redo and project save/reopen behavior remain reliable.

## Additional context

This concerns editing an existing composition, rather than only configuring a new one. If this is already supported through a particular menu or workflow, better discoverability and documentation would also help resolve the issue.

title: Timeline: Support separating dimensions of vector-valued properties
author: ReinFreebird
body:
## Summary

Provide a convenient way to separate supported vector-valued properties into independently editable and animatable component channels.

## Problem

Properties such as Position and Anchor Point contain multiple dimensions. Editing these values as a single vector can make it unnecessarily difficult to animate one axis independently of another.

For example, a user may want to animate horizontal movement without changing vertical position, or create separate animation curves for the X, Y, and Z components of a supported 3D property.

## Expected behavior

* Provide a discoverable control to separate dimensions for supported vector-valued properties.
* Display the resulting component channels independently in the timeline.
* Allow each component to have its own keyframes and interpolation.
* Expose each component independently in the Graph Editor.
* Provide a way to restore the combined property representation.
* Preserve existing animation values and timing when switching between combined and separated representations.

## Acceptance criteria

* [ ] Supported properties can be separated into their component channels.
* [ ] Each component can be animated independently.
* [ ] Component keyframes can be edited in the Graph Editor.
* [ ] Switching representations does not unexpectedly alter the animation.
* [ ] Saving and reopening the project preserves the separated state and animation.
* [ ] Unsupported properties do not expose an invalid separation option.

## Additional context

Position is the primary use case, including X/Y/Z channels where applicable. Please determine which other vector-valued properties can safely support this workflow, rather than requiring every vector property to be separable.

title: UX: Double-clicking a text layer in the Composition panel should enter text-editing mode
author: ReinFreebird
body:
## Summary

Improve text-layer editing by automatically activating text-editing mode when a user double-clicks a text layer in the Composition panel.

## Problem

Editing text is a frequent operation in motion-graphics workflows. Requiring users to locate and manually activate the appropriate tool or mode adds unnecessary interaction steps.

Users familiar with After Effects expect to be able to double-click a text layer in the Composition panel and begin editing its text directly.

## Expected behavior

* Double-clicking a text layer in the Composition panel enters text-editing mode.
* The appropriate text content is ready for editing.
* The interaction works for supported point-text and paragraph-text layers.
* Clicking or double-clicking non-text layers does not accidentally enter text-editing mode.
* Existing text selection, layer selection, and transformation behavior remain predictable.

## Acceptance criteria

* [ ] Double-clicking a text layer enters text-editing mode.
* [ ] Users can edit the text without manually switching tools first.
* [ ] Existing text content is preserved until the user changes it.
* [ ] Non-text layers continue to behave correctly.
* [ ] Single-click selection and existing text-tool workflows are unaffected.

## Additional context

The goal is to reduce friction when making repeated text edits and make the Composition panel interaction more consistent with established motion-graphics workflows.

title: CLI: `render --format webm --bitrate N` has no effect on VP9 WebM (byte-identical output; AV1 WebM and H.264 honour it)
author: cambridgetcg
body:
**Environment**
- macOS 15.7.3 (Darwin 24.6.0), Apple M3
- `effectcraft-cli --version` → `effectcraft-cli 0.6.0` (release asset `effectcraft-cli-0.6.0-macos-universal`)
- Headless CLI, CPU rendering. I used ffprobe 8.0.1 only to inspect the outputs.
- I found this while driving the CLI headless from an automated (agent) pipeline.

**Repro** (in an empty directory)
```sh
# 1 s, 256x256 comp with one text layer that rotates 0 -> 360 degrees
effectcraft-cli run --empty \
  comp.new '{"name":"T","width":256,"height":256,"frameRate":30,"duration":1}' \
  layer.newText '{"text":"Hi","size":120,"fill":"#FFCC00","name":"Title","position":[128,170]}' \
  --save-as p.ecproj
effectcraft-cli set T Title transform/rotation 0   --time 0 --project p.ecproj --save
effectcraft-cli set T Title transform/rotation 360 --time 1 --project p.ecproj --save

# VP9 WebM (the default WebM codec)
effectcraft-cli render --project p.ecproj --comp T --format webm --out vp9-default.webm
effectcraft-cli render --project p.ecproj --comp T --format webm --out vp9-200.webm  --bitrate 200
effectcraft-cli render --project p.ecproj --comp T --format webm --out vp9-3000.webm --bitrate 3000
effectcraft-cli render --project p.ecproj --comp T --format webm --out vp9-200-rc.webm --bitrate 200 --rate-control bitrate

# Controls: the same flag on AV1 WebM and on H.264
effectcraft-cli render --project p.ecproj --comp T --format webm --webm-codec av1 --out av1-default.webm
effectcraft-cli render --project p.ecproj --comp T --format webm --webm-codec av1 --out av1-200.webm --bitrate 200
effectcraft-cli render --project p.ecproj --comp T --format h264 --out h264-default.mp4
effectcraft-cli render --project p.ecproj --comp T --format h264 --out h264-200.mp4 --bitrate 200

ls -l *.webm *.mp4
md5 -r *.webm *.mp4      # md5sum on Linux
```

**Observed**

title: Cryptomatte: Selection can't be set in the UI (no field, no picking), and the GPU path takes ~9 s per 1440p frame
author: Romasikkk
body:
**Version:** `main` @ e9032c5, built from source (Windows 11, Ryzen 9 7950X, RTX 4090).

The matte itself is right. On a Blender-style multi-layer EXR (generator and file attached), the rendered matte equals the Cryptomatte spec's matte (the summed coverage of the selected IDs over all ranks) to 0/255. That holds for a name, a list (`cube, ring`), a wildcard (`s*`) and `<hex>`, on CPU and GPU, and on scaled or rotated layers. What doesn't work is getting a matte in the app:

1. **Selection has no field.** In Effect Controls, Layer, Display and Matte Only each have a value widget, but Selection only shows its name (`ui.elements` lists no `effectControls.prop.<uid>.value` for it). Clicking the row and typing does nothing, and a value set with `prop.set` isn't shown.
2. **No picking in the viewer.** With the layer and the effect selected, a click, Shift-click or Alt-click on an object in the Composition panel leaves Selection empty. In After Effects you pick objects by clicking them in the Composition or Layer panel while the Cryptomatte effect is selected. As it is, the GUI only gets the Colors view, and a matte needs a script.
3. **Layer is a fixed list** (CryptoObject / CryptoMaterial / CryptoAsset, default CryptoObject), not the layers named in the file's `cryptomatte/<key>/name` metadata. A file with only CryptoMaterial still works through the fallback to the first layer, but the popup shows the wrong name.
4. **The GPU path is slow, so the viewer lags.** `render-frame` at 2560×1440 takes 0.52 s without the effect, 1.44 s with Cryptomatte on the CPU and 8.2–9.6 s with `--gpu`. In the app, each change (Selection, Display) reaches the viewer 8–13 s later (measured over the control channel at Auto and Full), so the effect looks unresponsive. In the code, `gpu::fx_depth::cryptomatte` reduces the ranks on the CPU in a single-threaded loop over every aux pixel. For every pixel, `AuxChannels::crypto_ranks` formats the channel names (`format!("{layer}{k:02}.R")`) and sear…

title: Multi-layer EXR without an unnamed RGB layer: every channel is decoded twice per frame with EXtractoR / Cryptomatte (5–20× slower, ~10 GB RAM at 1440p)
author: Romasikkk
body:
**Version:** `main` @ e9032c5, built from source (Windows 11, Ryzen 9 7950X, 64 GB, RTX 4090).

Blender's compositor File Output writes every pass into one multi-layer file with no unnamed RGB layer (the beauty pass is `Image`). Since #449 these files import correctly, but they are much heavier to work with than the same picture in a single-layer EXR.

Repro: the generator from the attached zip (2560×1440, 32 channels: `CryptoMaterial00–02` float and five half layers, DWAA). I copied the file 30 times into a numbered sequence and wrote the same `Image` pixels as a single-layer EXR sequence. Then `render --format h264` of 30 frames on the CPU, with peak RAM of the CLI process:

| Comp | s/frame | Peak RAM |
|---|---|---|
| `Image` as a single-layer EXR (same pixels) | 0.048 | 2.8 GB |
| Multi-layer file, footage only | 0.266 | 10.8 GB |
| + 1 layer with EXtractoR (`GlossDir`) | 0.528 | 12.4 GB |
| + 2 layers with EXtractoR | 0.673 | 12.8 GB |
| Footage + Cryptomatte | 0.960 | 13.1 GB |

`--gpu` gives about the same. With real Blender 5.2 renders (32 channels, ~32 MB per frame), a beauty + 2 EXtractoR comp renders at 0.77 s/frame, against 0.10 s/frame with the same passes as single-layer files.

From the code:
- **The picture.** `image::load_from_memory` rejects the file. Then `exr_channels::layered_image` calls `read_exr_channels`, which decodes all channels of all layers to f32, Cryptomatte floats included (`values_as_f32().collect()`, then a copy into a full-size plane), and keeps only one layer.
- **EXtractoR / Cryptomatte.** `MediaPool::aux` calls `exr_channels::cached`, which runs `read_exr_channels` again on the same bytes. The two decodes share nothing, so the first EXtractoR layer doubles the frame time. Each further one is mostly a cache hit.
- **Memory.** One decoded file is ~470 MB of f32 planes at 2560×1440 × 32 channels. The exr crate's own image (~320 MB) exists alongside it during the decode, the aux cache keeps 4 files, and a render decodes several fr…

title: Scripting: ImportOptions.sequence = false still imports the whole numbered sequence
author: Romasikkk
body:
**Version:** `main` @ e9032c5, built from source (Windows 11).

In After Effects, `ImportOptions.sequence` defaults to `false`, and `app.project.importFile(io)` then imports only the file you picked. With `sequence = true` it imports the numbered run. In EffectCraft, all three cases import the whole run:

```js
var f = new File(".../single_0005.exr");            // single_0001 … single_0030 in the folder
var a = new ImportOptions(f); a.sequence = false;    // → single_[0001-0030].exr, duration 1 s
var b = new ImportOptions(f); b.sequence = true;     // → single_[0001-0030].exr, duration 1 s
var c = new ImportOptions(f);                         // c.sequence reads false → single_[0001-0030].exr
```

The engine command does the right thing: `__call("file.import", {paths: [...], sequence: false})` imports one still (`duration 0`). So the flag just isn't passed through from `ImportOptions`. Scripts written for After Effects that import one frame of a render (a reference still, say) get the sequence instead, and its first frame rather than the picked one at time 0.

title: Animation → Add Expression ignores the selected property (Linux Mint Cinnamon)
author: radeoflier
body:
_Fair warning: this is from Grok Build running on my Mint Cinnamon build. I think I understand what it did and what's going on. I read below and it seemed pushy/rude, but maybe it's helpful to you. The fix it implemented below DID solve it for me, here's it's own feedback:_

**EffectCraft 0.6.0 on Linux. The same path is still on main: Add Expression | prop.setExpression in crates/engine/src/menus.rs, and set_expr in crates/engine/src/commands/prop.rs.**

1. Open a composition and select a layer.
2. In the Timeline, twirl open Transform and click a property name, such as Position, so that property is selected.
3. Choose Animation ▸ Add Expression, or press Alt+Shift+=.

**The toast is:**

invalid parameters for prop.setExpression: missing path(e.g. transform/position) orprop uid

No expression is added. The same property does get an expression if you Alt-click its stopwatch. That click sends prop.setExpression with {"layer", "prop": uid}.

The menu entry and the Alt+Shift+= binding send the command with no parameters. set_expr always starts with prop_ref, which requires path or prop. Clicking the property name already calls prop.select, so the property is in selected_props, and set_expr never reads it. This is every selected property, not only Position. The command stays enabled whenever a layer is selected (has_layers), so the menu item runs and then fails.

essential.addProperty already handles a call with neither path nor prop: it uses selected_leaf_props, and if that is empty it returns select a property in the timeline (or give layerandpath).

prop.setExpression should do the same. Keep prop_ref when path or prop is present, so the stopwatch, scripts, and the pick whip stay as they are. When both are absent, apply the add-or-toggle to each selected_leaf_props target in one edit labeled Expression. If none are selected, use that same "select a property" error instead of missing path.

title: Multi-part EXR from Blender 5.x: channel names get the part name twice, so EXtractoR names don't match and Cryptomatte loses ranks 2–5 and its manifest
author: Romasikkk
body:
**Version:** `main` @ e9032c5, built from source (Windows 11).

Blender 5.0–5.2 save a render as a multi-layer EXR with one part per pass (4.5 still wrote a single part). Each part is named after its pass, and its channels keep the full name: part `ViewLayer.Combined` holds `ViewLayer.Combined.R/G/B/A`, and part `ViewLayer.CryptoObject01` holds `ViewLayer.CryptoObject01.r/g/b/a`. The attached zip has a 480×270 render of a small scene and the Blender script that made it.

`layer.channels` lists them with the part name prefixed a second time (`read_exr_channels` builds `format!("{part}.{channel}")` for every named part):
```
ViewLayer.Combined.ViewLayer.Combined.R
ViewLayer.Depth.ViewLayer.Depth.Z
ViewLayer.CryptoObject00.ViewLayer.CryptoObject00.r
```
The beauty pass (`ViewLayer.Combined`) is still picked correctly, but:

1. **EXtractoR**: `ViewLayer.Depth.Z` and `ViewLayer.Mist.Z`, the names Blender shows, aren't found, so the output is 0. Only the doubled name works.
2. **Cryptomatte loses ranks 2–5.** The layer resolves to `ViewLayer.CryptoObject00.ViewLayer.CryptoObject`, so `crypto_ranks` finds the `…00` channels but looks for rank part 01 under `…00.ViewLayer.CryptoObject01.R`, which doesn't exist. EffectCraft's matte equals the spec's matte computed from rank part 00 alone. In this small render that's at most 3 pixels per object (where three or more IDs overlap), but with motion blur, depth of field, fog or hair those edges are exactly where the matte matters.
3. **The Cryptomatte manifest isn't matched.** The metadata name is `ViewLayer.CryptoObject`, but the layer has the doubled name. Selection by plain name still works, because the hash is computed from the name, but wildcards return nothing: `Sph*` gives 0 % instead of 6.8 % (`Sphere.001`).

A render from Blender 4.5 (the default cube scene, one part, the same `ViewLayer.*` channel names) works: EXtractoR finds `ViewLayer.Mist.Z`, and `Cu*` selects the cube. So does a synthetic multi-part file with plain …
