title: Blend modes in 32 bpc vs After Effects: classic modes apply opacity differently, and Overlay / Exclusion / Luminosity / Color Burn clamp over-range values
author: Romasikkk
body:
**Version:** `main` @ e9032c5, built from source (Windows 11). Reference: After Effects 2025 (25.2).

I compared EffectCraft with After Effects on the same EXR inputs. AE was set up like our production projects: 32 bpc, Working Space None, Blend Colors Using 1.0 Gamma off, working gamma 2.2. EffectCraft used `bitDepth: 32` with no working space. The inputs (generator attached) are `base.exr`, a 0–1 gradient, and `over.exr`, an HDR layer up to 4.0 on top of it. Both apps write their 32-bit output linearised with the sRGB curve (AE's 32-bit float Photoshop output, EffectCraft's `render --format exr`), so I converted both back with the sRGB curve and compared comp values. Below, b is the bottom layer, o the top layer and k the opacity, all in comp values.

**Matches (≤ 1.5/255):** Normal 25 %; Screen 100 / 50 / 20 %; Add 50 %; Linear Dodge 50 %; Darken 30 %; Multiply; Color Dodge 100 / 15 %; Difference 15 %; Classic Color Dodge and Classic Difference at 100 %. A real comp (beauty, a gloss pass in Screen 25 % and a mist pass with Tint in Screen 20 %, 2560×1440) matches After Effects to 0.007/255 on average, 0.64/255 at most. Nice work.

**1. Classic modes at partial opacity.** After Effects fades the top layer toward the mode's neutral colour first and then applies the classic formula. Each model below matches AE to ≤ 0.03/255. EffectCraft mixes the full-strength result with opacity instead:

| Mode at 15 % | After Effects | EffectCraft vs AE, within 0–1 |
|---|---|---|
| Classic Color Dodge | `min(b / (1 − k·o), 1)` | up to 24/255 (mean 19) |
| Classic Difference | `abs(b − k·o)` | up to 35/255 (mean 29) |
| Classic Color Burn | `1 − (1 − b) / (1 − k·(1 − o))` | up to 45/255 |

**2. Over-range values (top layer > 1, normal in 32 bpc).** Within 0–1 these modes match. Above 1, After Effects keeps the plain formula, and EffectCraft clamps:

| Mode | After Effects (matches to) | EffectCraft vs AE |
|---|---|---|
| Overlay | unclamped formula (0.3/255) | up to 57/255 |
| Ex…

title: Project Settings: no Working Gamma 2.4 option (After Effects converts linear EXRs with a 2.4 power curve in that mode)
author: Romasikkk
body:
**Version:** `main` @ e9032c5, built from source (Windows 11). Reference: After Effects 2025 (25.2).

With Working Space None, After Effects converts linear-light footage (EXR, Interpret As Linear Light) using the project's Working Gamma (Project Settings ▸ Color, `app.project.workingGamma`):

- **2.2**: the piecewise sRGB curve. EffectCraft matches it (within 1/255 on an 8-bit render, 0.00/255 on 32-bit output).
- **2.4**: a pure 2.4 power curve. AE's render matches `x^(1/2.4)` within 0.95/255. Examples: 0.051 → 0.290, 0.18 → 0.490, 0.5 → 0.749, against 0.250, 0.461 and 0.736 with the sRGB curve. The shadows differ by up to 12.6/255.

EffectCraft's `file.projectSettings` has no gamma option, so a comp of linear EXRs from a 2.4 After Effects project comes out darker in the shadows in EffectCraft.

**Suggestion:** a Working Gamma 2.2 / 2.4 setting in Project Settings ▸ Color, used where EffectCraft linearises or delinearises footage when there's no working space, as After Effects does.

title: Add a System theme option that follows the macOS light/dark appearance
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Add a System choice to EffectCraft's interface theme setting that follows the macOS light/dark appearance live, so the app changes with the rest of the desktop when macOS switches appearance automatically.

## Problem to solve

macOS can switch between Light and Dark appearance automatically (System Settings → Appearance → Auto changes it at sunset and sunrise), and many Mac apps offer a "System" theme choice that tracks it.

EffectCraft offers only manual interface themes. Settings → Appearance → Theme lists "Dark" (the default), "Darker" and "Light", stored as `appearance.theme` in `prefs.json`. The palette in `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs` comes only from that preference; no code path reads the OS appearance.

Because EffectCraft only has manual choices, a user whose macOS appearance switches automatically has to change the app theme by hand at least twice a day, or leave it mismatched with every other app.

## Proposed behavior

Add System to the existing theme choice. With System selected, the app applies a light theme while macOS is in Light mode and a dark theme while it is in Dark mode, both at launch and immediately when the OS appearance changes while the app is open. The saved choice stays System; only the displayed theme changes. The existing manual choices keep working as they do today.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The theme control offers a System choice (for example "System" or "Use system setting") alongside the existing manual choices, and every place that exposes the theme (Settings → Appearance → Theme) shows it.
2. With System selected, the app starts in its light theme when macOS is set to Light and in its dark theme when macOS is set to Dark.
3. With System selected and the app running, changing the macOS appearance, including the scheduled change made by macOS Appearance "Auto", switches the whole interface (panels, menus, dialogs and custom-painted surfaces) to the matching theme without a restart or any user action.
4. The System cho…

title: Suggestion: optional Nvidia CUDA / NVENC fast lane
author: Jaimetud
body:
Love that EffectCraft uses a wgpu compute backend for GPU compositing and effects — the vendor-neutral route (Metal/Vulkan/DirectX 12/WebGPU) is the right long-term call, and the same goes for the homegrown Rust codecs.

The gap vs. After Effects for Nvidia users is the Nvidia-specific fast lane: Adobe's Mercury GPU Acceleration leans on CUDA cores for GPU-accelerated effects/rendering, and exports can use NVENC hardware encoding, which is a big real-world time saver on long render-queue exports.

Would you consider an optional Nvidia backend that kicks in when an Nvidia GPU is present — CUDA-accelerated effects/3D rendering where it fits, NVENC hardware encode for the render queue, and possibly NVDEC decode — while keeping wgpu compositing and the current Rust encoders as the universal fallback? That would keep the cross-platform story intact (AMD/Mac/Intel users lose nothing) while giving Nvidia folks Adobe-class render times.

Happy to test on an Nvidia Windows rig if it ever lands. Thanks for building this in the open.

title: mcp: add --automation-read-root / --automation-write-root so the server can be confined to a folder

effectcraft-cli.exe mcp --automation-read-root C:\Users\<user>\work --automation-write-root C:\Users\<user>\work
```

title: macOS: render_out_is_relative_to_the_working_directory test fails due to /private/var symlink
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
## Summary
The `render_out_is_relative_to_the_working_directory` test in `apps/effectcraft-cli/tests/cli.rs` fails on macOS due to path canonicalization differences.

## Environment
- **OS:** macOS 15.2 (Sequoia)
- **Arch:** Apple Silicon (aarch64)
- **Rust:** 1.99.0
- **Branch:** main (30aaddf)

## Failure
```
---- render_out_is_relative_to_the_working_directory stdout ----
thread 'render_out_is_relative_to_the_working_directory' panicked at apps/effectcraft-cli/tests/cli.rs:285:5:
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: "/private/var/folders/.../out/d.gif"
 right: "/var/folders/.../out/d.gif"
```

## Root Cause
On macOS, `/var` is a symlink to `/private/var`. The test creates temp dirs under `/var/...` but path canonicalization resolves them to `/private/var/...`, causing the assertion to fail.

## Reproduction
```bash
cargo test -p effectcraft-cli --test cli --release render_out_is_relative_to_the_working_directory
```

## Impact
- Breaks local macOS CI for contributors
- Does not affect runtime behavior (paths work correctly)
- Only affects this one test

## Suggested Fix
Canonicalize both paths before comparison:
```rust
let actual = fs::canonicalize(actual_path)?;
let expected = fs::canonicalize(expected_path)?;
assert_eq!(actual, expected);
```

Or strip the `/private` prefix on macOS before comparison.

title: Feature Request: Support multi-file drag-and-drop into the timeline
author: MusiCrazyJavier
body:
### Description
I would like to suggest a feature to improve the workflow efficiency in EffectCraft: **the ability to select multiple video files and drag-and-drop them simultaneously into the timeline**. 

Currently, adding multiple assets one by one can be time-consuming for larger projects. Allowing multi-file drag-and-drop would significantly speed up the editing process.

### Proposed Behavior
- Select multiple video files from the local file explorer (or the project media bin).
- Drag and drop them onto the timeline track.
- **Ordering:** The clips should be placed sequentially on the timeline track, ordered from the first selected file to the last selected file in a descending/consecutive manner.

### Benefits
- Implements a standard UX convention found in modern video editors.
- Streamlines the import-to-timeline workflow for users dealing with multiple clips.

Thank you for your time and for maintaining this project!

title: Playback stutters even on cached frames + cache gap ahead of playhead; indicators vanish at 1/3 res
author: chikasimp
body:
### Media

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/58f65e82-e3eb-482f-b304-0e788d2addc4

### Description
Two related playback cache bugs on basic playback:

1. **Cache stall at playhead:** frames immediately in front of playhead stop caching, stalling playback, while cache continues building 100s of frames further ahead. Playback can't proceed through the uncached gap right in front.
2. **Lag even when cached + indicators vanish:** there is visible stutter/lag even in already-cached (green) frames. On a 24-thread machine this should not stutter on basic playback. Switching comp viewer to 1/3 res makes the cache frame indicators disappear completely.

Video note: any stutters/pauses in the attached video are the software, not me pressing pause / spacebar.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Open any comp / basic timeline in EffectCraft
2. Press play from uncached section, watch green cache bar
3. Observe: gap of uncached frames right ahead of playhead never fills, but frames 100s ahead do cache — playback stalls at gap
4. Let section fully cache (solid green), play again — still stutters
5. Pause, set comp viewer resolution to 1/3
6. Observe: cache frame indicators gone entirely

### Expected
- Cache priority should fill contiguously forward from playhead first, then look-ahead.
- Cached (green) playback should be smooth on 24 threads / RTX 3090 for basic comps.
- Lowering preview res to 1/3 should still show cache indicators, not hide them.

### Actual
- Uncached hole directly ahead of playhead persists, far-ahead frames cache instead, playback stalls.
- Even fully cached sections stutter.
- At 1/3 res, no cache indicators at all.

### App Version / Build

title: Korean (Hangul) text in the interface renders as boxes on macOS: no Hangul probe in install_script_fallbacks
author: ingprise-cmd
body:
## Problem

On macOS, Korean (Hangul) text in the **interface** is drawn as missing-glyph boxes (□□□): layer names, project/file names, text typed into panels, etc. The same Korean text renders correctly on the **canvas** (the text engine's own per-script fallback finds a Korean face), so only the egui interface is affected.

- EffectCraft 0.6.0 (the code below is unchanged on current `main`, 1446e27)
- macOS 15.7, Intel iMac, interface language English

**To reproduce:** rename a layer to `한글 레이어` → the Layers panel shows boxes.

## Cause

`install_script_fallbacks` (crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs) probes only kana `'あ'` and Han `'文'` for CJK, and never Hangul:

https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft/blob/1446e27d851386d4126f5b1972ed27d69de4c6f3/crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs#L355-L363

On macOS the kana probe resolves to **Hiragino Sans**, which has no Hangul. The Han probe then returns the already-loaded Hiragino Sans (`fallback_for` tries loaded faces first), so it is skipped as `seen`. No face that covers Hangul is ever registered with egui.

Coverage on this Mac (checked with CoreText):

| Family | あ | 文 | 한 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hiragino Sans | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ |
| Apple SD Gothic Neo | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

Windows is probably affected the same way: Yu Gothic and Meiryo have no Hangul. That is not tested.

As far as I can tell from the code, users have no workaround. `EFFECTCRAFT_CJK_LOCALE=ko` only reorders the Han lookup, and by then the kana probe has already registered Hiragino Sans.

## Suggested fix (one constant + one changed line)

Probe Hangul too, **after** kana and Han, so the existing Japanese/Chinese order is unchanged:

```diff
         const KANA: (char, &str) = ('あ', "japanese-system");
         const HAN: (char, &str) = ('文', "chinese-system");
+        // Hangul: the Japanese/Chinese system faces may lack it (Hiragino Sans on macOS has none),
+        // so probe it on its own, after kana and Han so their order is unchanged.
+        const HANGUL: (char, &str)…

title: Expand pre-comp layers in the timeline to edit their contents in place
author: barchukmov
body:
Split out of #288.

**Problem**
Editing anything inside a pre-comp means opening it in its own timeline, away from the comp you're working in. That pushes people away from pre-composing even when it would keep a project organised.

**Proposal**
A pre-comp layer gets an expand arrow in the timeline, like a layer's property twirl-down. Expanding it shows the nested comp's layers inline, indented under the pre-comp layer: you can select, keyframe, switch and edit them without leaving the parent comp. Nested pre-comps expand the same way, to any depth.

The expanded layers aren't copies; they are the nested comp's own layers, shown in place.
- **Several instances:** if the same comp is used by more than one layer, each instance can be expanded, and all of them show the same layers. Selecting a layer in one instance selects that layer in every instance, because it's one layer shown several times.
- **One edit, one change:** an edit changes the nested comp once, as one undo step, and every instance shows the result. Nothing is duplicated or applied once per instance.
- Rendering doesn't change: the pre-comp renders as it does today, with or without Collapse Transformations.


---
_Summarised by Claude from a discussion with @barchukmov. If something doesn't make sense, feel free to contact @barchukmov._

title: Reorderable per-layer render stack (masks, effects, styles, transform, matte)
author: barchukmov
body:
Split out of #288.

**Problem**
Every layer renders in a fixed order: source → masks → effects (in order) → layer styles → transform → track matte → blend. Getting a different order (a mask after an effect, an effect between two masks, an effect after the transform) means pre-composing.

**Proposal**
Each layer has an ordered stack: its masks, effects, layer styles, transform and track matte are items that can be dragged into any order in the timeline (e.g. effect → mask → effect). A layer whose stack is in the default order renders exactly as today, so After Effects parity and existing projects are unaffected.


---
_Summarised by Claude from a discussion with @barchukmov. If something doesn't make sense, feel free to contact @barchukmov._

title: Layer parameters: add a Sampling Space (Layer / Comp)
author: barchukmov
body:
Split out of #288.

**Problem**
An effect with a layer parameter (Displacement Map, Set Matte, Compound Blur, Gradient Wipe, Texturize…) reads the chosen layer in that layer's own space. The two layers only line up when they have the same size, position, scale and rotation; otherwise you have to pre-compose. Track mattes don't have this problem, because they line up in comp space.

**Proposal**
Layer parameters already offer the layer and Source / Masks / Effects & Masks. Add **Sampling Space** next to them:
- **Layer** (default, After Effects' behaviour): the chosen layer in its own space, as today
- **Comp:** the chosen layer where it appears in the comp, after its transform, so it lines up with what you see wherever either layer sits, the way a track matte does

Sampling Space works with all three existing choices (Source, Masks, Effects & Masks).


---
_Summarised by Claude from a discussion with @barchukmov. If something doesn't make sense, feel free to contact @barchukmov._

title: Guide (preview-only / render-only) for effects, layer styles, masks, mattes and layers
author: barchukmov
body:
Split out of #288.

**Problem**
Guide layers let a layer show in the viewer and stay out of the render. Nothing else in a layer's stack can do that. While working you often want a cheap stand-in for something slow (a quick blur instead of a heavy defocus, a simple drop shadow instead of a soft multi-style look, a rough mask instead of a detailed roto) and the real version only in the final render. Today that means swapping them by hand before every export.

**Proposal**
Every item in a layer's stack gets a guide setting: **effects, layer styles, masks, track mattes** and the **layer** itself.
- **Always** (default)
- **Preview only:** applied in the viewer and RAM preview, skipped in the render
- **Render only:** skipped in the viewer and RAM preview, applied in the render

Put a cheap Preview-only item and the real Render-only item side by side: the viewer stays fast and the render comes out right. For layers, Preview only is today's Guide Layer, and Render only is new. Render Settings ▸ Guide Layers decides for all of these, and the render queue, the `render` CLI and `comp.render` all follow it.


---
_Summarised by Claude from a discussion with @barchukmov. If something doesn't make sense, feel free to contact @barchukmov._

title: GPU compositor can't start on DirectX 12 (FXC fails on the `pointwise` kernel)
author: KattKnight
body:
**What happens**

On Windows, when egui-wgpu's device is DirectX 12, `GpuContext::new` fails while building the compute pipelines. The app then quietly composites on the CPU. `session.accel_note` reads:

```
GPU compositor unavailable: GPU initialization (pointwise): Validation Error
  In Device::create_compute_pipeline, label = 'pointwise'
    Internal error: FXC D3DCompile error (Unspecified error (0x80004005)):
    …effectcraft kernels(69,12-24): warning X3571: pow(f, e) will not work for negative f, …
    internal error: compilation aborted unexpectedly
```

**Where seen**

- Windows 11, EffectCraft `main` at 1446e27 (10 October 2026), on a laptop with an RTX 4060 Laptop GPU.
- First seen on WARP (Microsoft Basic Render Driver) on DirectX 12. That is what egui_kittest picks in `ui_gpu`.
- Reproduced in the desktop app by starting it with `WGPU_BACKEND=dx12`. `render.backend` then reports `"active": "cpu"` and the error above as `why`.
- Started normally, the same build picks Vulkan (`NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (Vulkan)`) and the GPU compositor works.
- So any setup where the window's device lands on DirectX 12 should hit it, for example a machine without a working Vulkan driver.

**Why**

FXC (the legacy D3D shader compiler wgpu uses for DirectX 12 by default) aborts on the HLSL that naga generates for `pointwise`. DXC usually compiles such kernels.

**Possible directions (maintainers' call)**

- Select DXC for DirectX 12 in the window's `InstanceDescriptor` (`backend_options.dx12.shader_compiler`). This needs DXC shipped or statically linked.
- Prefer Vulkan over DirectX 12 for the window when both are available.
- Or find which construct in `pointwise` trips FXC and work around it there.

title: [FEATURE REQUEST] Port Duik Plugins to EffectCraft
author: jetrotal
body:
**Describe the feature**
Duik (developed by RxLaboratory) is an open-source library for **rigging and animation, universally recognized as the industry-standard toolset for 2D character animation in Adobe After Effects (known through major releases like Duik Bassel and Duik Ángela).** It provides powerful Inverse Kinematics (IK), auto-rigging for bipeds and quadrupeds, bone structures, and dynamic procedural automations (like springs, wiggles, and overlapping action). 

Since EffectCraft is positioning itself as an open-source, pure Rust alternative to After Effects, supporting a port of Duik—or providing a scripting API robust enough to run it—would instantly transform EffectCraft from a motion graphics compositor into a fully-fledged professional character animation powerhouse.

**The Licensing Consideration: GPL-3.0 vs. MIT**
It is highly important to consider the licensing differences between the two projects:
* **Duik** is licensed under the **GPL-3.0** license.
* **EffectCraft** uses a permissive **MIT / Apache-2.0** license.

Because EffectCraft is MIT-licensed, it is perfectly legally compatible with hosting a GPL-3.0 plugin. The Duik port can retain its original GPL-3.0 license and be hosted as a separate plugin download, meaning EffectCraft's core engine remains safely MIT while users can still enjoy the full power of Duik.

Because GPL-3.0 is a "strong copyleft" (viral) license, directly merging Duik’s source code into the core of EffectCraft would force EffectCraft to adopt the GPL-3.0 license. To keep EffectCraft completely MIT-compliant, the following approaches could be considered:

title: GPU export: precomp layers render on the CPU and upload every frame, so nested comps barely use the GPU
author: MatejKozlovsky
body:
**Version:** 0.7.0 (also 0.6.0) · **Area:** GPU compositor (`crates/gpu/src/walk.rs`)

## What happens

With Mercury GPU Acceleration on (`render --gpu`, or the project setting), a comp whose layers are
precomps (not collapsed) renders very slowly. The GPU compositor draws a precomp layer through
`Renderer::layer_source`, which renders the nested comp with the **CPU** compositor (depth > 0) and
then uploads the full nested frame to the GPU, every frame. A comp built from precomps therefore runs at
roughly CPU speed while the GPU idles.

When the GPU compositor declines a frame, the CPU renders it silently: nothing in the log says why an
export suddenly runs at CPU speed.

## Measured

* test PC (Ryzen 7 5800X, RTX 3090 24 GB, Windows 10), 4K, 60 s comp of nested precomps, GPU export: about **2.1 fps**,
  vs about 9.5 fps for the same content as a flat comp. (Measured on a 0.6.0-based build with export scheduling changes; the precomp path is unchanged in 0.7.0.)
* test Mac (Apple M4, 16 GB), 4K, 3 s / 90 frames, same nested comp: stock 0.7.0 `--gpu` **1.15 fps**
  (77.9 s), GPU busy 92% while the process swaps (mem free min 2%, RSS peak 9.5 GB).

## Expected

A precomp layer's nested comp renders on the GPU (as it does in After Effects with Mercury GPU),
and a declined frame is logged with its reason.

## Repro

1. A 4K comp with a few precomp layers (footage + effects inside, effects/blend mode on the precomp layer).
2. `effectcraft-cli --project p.ecproj --gpu render --comp Main --end 3 --out o.mp4`
3. Compare fps with the same content flattened into one comp.

Add a discoverable agent setup flow in EffectCraft so a desktop user can prepare an agent to edit a composition or render motion graphics with the installed application.

The existing CLI and MCP server require users to locate an executable, choose a mode, and configure their agent client. Packaging differs by platform, and an installed CLI may be absent from PATH. A source inspection of desktop entry points and UI found no guided setup flow; the desktop workflow was not executed.

## Proposed behavior

Offer setup from an identifiable desktop entry. Locate an available `effectcraft-cli`, let the user select another copy, and check its executable identity and compatibility with the app. If no compatible copy is available, offer the matching official release installation route and recheck the chosen executable afterward. Setup must work with today's separate macOS CLI download without waiting for bundling.

Explain that headless MCP owns a separate project and live MCP drives the open app through `mcp --bridge`. For live mode, identify the actual control endpoint or guide the user through the supported `--control 9877` launch prerequisite. Generate a copyable client command or configuration using the verified executable path and selected mode. Distinguish a local MCP connectivity test from registration or approval inside the chosen client.

title: feat(packaging): provide reliable CLI access with desktop releases
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Provide a supported CLI invocation with EffectCraft desktop distributions on Windows, Linux, and macOS, so people, scripts, and agents can edit a composition or render motion graphics through a documented invocation.

## Problem to solve

Desktop acquisition does not imply a command is available in a shell. Windows packages include `effectcraft-cli.exe` without adding it to PATH. Linux native packages install the CLI in `/usr/bin`, while AppImage and Flatpak contain it internally. The macOS desktop DMG and CLI ZIP are separate downloads. Users need reliable CLI invocation without an agent client.

## Proposed behavior

Each supported desktop distribution should supply a usable CLI or an integrated route to install its matching CLI, with a documented invocation. Use the actual executable path, a supported launcher, or a sandbox command override. Optional shell exposure is allowed; invocation must work without global PATH changes.

Preserve native Linux commands and document Windows install paths and portable executables. Make the CLI accessible to AppImage and Flatpak users through supported invocations. For macOS, include the CLI with desktop acquisition or provide an integrated matching install route.

## Acceptance criteria

- The same advertised invocation can initialize MCP and discover tools without an agent client or document edit; the temporary server stops after the check.
- Linux tarball users can invoke the extracted CLI using the advertised path or optional installation procedure without building from source.
- Affected packages and added executables retain the existing release signing, notarization and native-package validation requirements.
- On a fresh Windows MSI install, the documented invocation reaches the installed CLI, including a custom directory containing spaces. Portable ZIP users can invoke the supplied CLI without an automatic global shell change.
- Fresh Linux DEB and RPM installs preserve the existing `effectcraft-cli` command…

title: Security hardening: script-gate preference can be changed through the MCP/automation command path
author: pdaw-cowork
body:
**Environment**
- EffectCraft v0.6.0, macOS Apple Silicon

**Summary (intentionally minimal)**
A preference that gates script capabilities appears to be changeable through the same command interface an MCP-connected agent uses. An agent that has been prompt-injected could therefore, in principle, relax that gate by itself. In line with the security policy used in this project family, I'm not posting details or a reproduction publicly.

Private vulnerability reporting is currently disabled for this repository. **Could you enable it (Settings → Code security → Private vulnerability reporting) or tell me another private channel?** I'll send the exact code locations and reproduction steps there.

**Suggested direction**
Treat scripting-related preferences as UI-only (not modifiable from the MCP/automation command path), or require explicit user confirmation when a non-UI caller changes them.

Thanks for the great project.

title: GPU compositor: effect stacks round-trip through the CPU, intermediates allocate fresh textures, and Noise on an adjustment layer re-uploads its footprint every frame
author: MatejKozlovsky
body:
**Version:** main (after #641/#648) · **Area:** GPU compositor (`crates/gpu`), layer cache (`crates/render/src/cache.rs`)

## What happens

On the GPU compositor (`--gpu`, Mercury GPU Acceleration), a 4K comp with effect stacks spends most of its
time moving pixels rather than compositing:

1. **Effect stacks round-trip.** A layer with effects is processed by the CPU path (`styled_layer`), which
   runs each run of GPU-capable effects as upload → kernels → readback, then uploads the result again to
   place it.
2. **Every intermediate is a new texture.** Within one frame, a working texture released by the encoder
   that made it waits in the shared pool until that encoder submits, so a frame allocates a new texture for
   almost every intermediate (a 4K RGBA f32 texture is 127 MB).
3. **A time-dependent effect re-keys an adjustment layer's footprint.** The footprint (source through the
   masks, without effects) is keyed with the effects included, so Noise or Grain on a finishing adjustment
   layer changes the key every frame and the GPU re-uploads the full-frame footprint each time.
4. **The upload cache evicts silently.** When static layers exceed the fixed 1536 MB upload budget, layer
   textures are evicted and re-uploaded every frame without any log line, and an embedder cannot size the
   budget to the device.

## Measured

On a test PC (Ryzen 7 5800X, RTX 3090 24 GB, Windows 10), `effectcraft-cli bench --gpu` on a 4K comp
with effect stacks (main, median of 5): GPU cold 1181 ms/frame, GPU warm 208 ms/frame. A 3 s / 90-frame
4K export with `--gpu` (`RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1`, so frames stay on the GPU) takes 81.1 s with a 17.2 GB
VRAM peak.

## Expected

Effect stacks stay resident on the GPU, a frame reuses its own intermediates, an adjustment layer's
footprint keeps its key across frames, and a full upload cache is reported.

title: Feature Request: native rolling-number (odometer) text effect and a multi-pass glow
author: brunolpa89
body:
Two effects come up in almost every SaaS / product-launch motion-graphics tutorial, and EffectCraft 0.7.0 has no native equivalent for either. This is **not** about loading third-party plugins (that is #334, #322, #600, #327). It is a request for two native effects, described by observable behaviour only, in keeping with the clean-room rules.

I hit both while rebuilding a 17.6 s product ad in EffectCraft 0.7.0 (macOS, Apple M5) through the CLI/bridge.

## 1. Rolling-number ("odometer") text animation

**Behaviour wanted:** a number or string whose digits roll vertically, each digit on its own strip, from one value to another, then settle.

- per-digit roll with direction and an easing/speed control, so digits can land staggered
- a motion-blur-like streak along the roll axis that goes to zero when the digit settles
- non-digit characters stay fixed, for example a suffix: `44100 Hz` rolling to `48000Hz`
- driven by a single value or two keyframed values, so it can be animated from the timeline or a command

**What exists today:** `Numbers` (ec.text.numbers) prints a value but does not roll digits.

**Workaround I used:** 15 digit layers, each with an expression, plus an animated `Directional Blur`. Two costs: (a) the layer's own temporal blur left residual rows in the settled frame, so I had to turn it off and fake the streak; (b) every change of the string means rebuilding the layer stack.

## 2. A higher-quality multi-pass glow

**Behaviour wanted:** a glow that stays smooth over a very wide radius, with controls that make bright thin lines and large soft light bars look right in the same pass.

- several radii blended together (tight core plus wide falloff) in one effect
- exposure/gamma-style control, so a 2 to 3 px line can bloom strongly without clipping the whole frame
- a uniform, non-grainy halo at large radius
- optional tint along the falloff

**What exists today:** `Glow` (ec.stylize.glow) is good for a single radius.

title: Feature request: Auto-Save parity and project versions on storage you own (local/NAS, Google Drive, OneDrive, S3/R2 via rclone, optionally git), with lease-based sharing
author: fernandodilland
body:
## TL;DR
Please give EffectCraft After Effects' Auto-Save behaviour (interval, maximum versions, crash recovery that never overwrites the original) and let versions go to storage the user owns. Because `.ecproj` is readable, diff-friendly JSON, offer structure-aware merging and an optional git target. Opt-in; the README says no network access unless you ask for it, and this respects that.

## How After Effects does it
- Auto-Save is configured in Preferences: interval and maximum project versions (default 5), written to an "Adobe After Effects Auto-Save" folder next to the project.
- Adobe's recent beta improves it: auto-save also covers untitled projects, runs on a fixed clock, offers one-click crash recovery, and opens a recovered project as an untitled "Recovered Project" so your first Save can't overwrite anything.
- An After Effects engineer notes the project isn't a database, so undo history is cleared when you close, and recommends working in versions instead.
- Team Projects is an explicit push/pull to a cloud version, and the Auto-Save preferences don't apply to it.

## What EffectCraft has today (README only)
Versioned, readable JSON `.ecproj`, Lottie import/export, a Render Queue with post-render actions, expressions, footage referenced from disk, 306 effects, MCP/CLI/control channel, web build.

## Proposal
**Phase 0, Auto-Save parity:** interval + max versions, a recovery prompt, and "recovered projects open untitled".
**Phase 1, Save target:** shared building blocks below, plus an optional **git target** (commit per autosave to a local repo, push optional) because the project format diffs cleanly. Footage stays out of the project target by default.
**Phase 2, portability:** store footage as relative path + size + hash so another machine can relink; a "Collect Files" action copies used media to a target (rclone to S3/R2/NAS). A Render Queue **post-render action** can upload finished renders.
**Phase 3, sharing without a server:** a lease per project wit…

title: Window decorations and title bar inconsistent with VectorCraft / PhotoCraft
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Description
The window decorations and title bar handling in `effectcraft` are inconsistent with the standard established in VectorCraft (PR #969) and PhotoCraft (PR #1903).

### Current Behavior
- On Windows and Linux, the application either does not draw client-side decorations/caption buttons or lacks consistent custom title bar handling.
- There is no option for users to toggle `System Title Bar` (native OS window decorations) in Preferences/User Interface.

### Desired Behavior
Standardize title bar and window decoration architecture to match VectorCraft:
1. Support custom client-side titlebar and window caption buttons (Minimize, Maximize/Restore, Close) with edge resize zones.
2. Provide a `System Title Bar` preference under User Interface to allow users to switch back to native OS decorations on Windows/Linux if desired.
3. macOS retains native window buttons and fullsize content view.

title: Timeline ruler ignores "Frames" time display — labels stay in seconds:frames
author: SamWebCodes
body:
**Describe the bug / improvement**
When the project's Time Display is set to Frames (Cmd+click on the current-time
display, or Project Settings > Time Display Style: Frames), the CTI display
switches to absolute frame numbers, but the timeline **ruler** keeps labeling
ticks in seconds:frames format (`00:15f` style). When stepping the playhead
frame by frame, the seconds:frames labels on the ruler are confusing — the
whole panel should honor the Frames setting, as After Effects does.

**To Reproduce**
1. Open any composition.
2. Set Time Display to Frames: Cmd+click the current-time number at the top
   left of the Timeline (or Project Settings > Time Display Style: Frames).
3. Look at the ruler: the CTI shows frames (00000, 00001…), but the ruler
   labels still read `00:00f`, `00:15f`, `01:00f`…

**Expected behavior**
With Time Display set to Frames, the ruler should label ticks with absolute
frame numbers (0, 1, 2… 30, 31…), the same value shown under the CTI.

**Suggestion (source pointer)**
The ruler labels are hardcoded in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/timeline.rs`,
"Ticks + labels" block:
the label is always `format!("{:02}:{:02}f", fno / fps_i, fno % fps_i)`.
It looks like a one-line fix: when `settings.time_display ==
TimeDisplayStyle::Frames`, use `format!("{:05}", fno)` — the same formatting
already used for the secondary CTI display. Label spacing is already
frame-based, so no other change is needed.

**Environment**
- EffectCraft v0.8.0 (macOS 27, Apple silicon)

title: Color picker (Character panel Fill/Stroke) has no eyedropper — add viewer color sampling

2. In the Character panel, click the Fill swatch.

the Composition viewer (the composited frame) and use that color — as

The infrastructure already exists: `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/fx_widgets.rs`
documents "crosshair and eyedropper buttons … colours sampled from the
composited frame", currently wired only for effect parameters. The
Character panel's color button (srgb_color_button / color_edit_button_srgb
in crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs) could reuse the same sampling mechanism.

title: mcp: a confined scripting mode, so agents can use loops while file access stays inside the roots
author: MazenGit
body:
Thanks for turning the sandboxed MCP request (#500, and storytold/vectorcraft#832) around within a day. It made this test possible. I ran a full job through both apps with the confined MCP servers and want to share what worked and what cost the most time.

**What worked well**

- **The sandbox held.** Every read and write stayed inside the root, refusals were clear, and nothing surprising happened.
- **Errors are actionable.** For example, `prop.get` on a group said to use `layer.tree` instead, and `edit.clear` listed the parameters it accepts. A failed batch named the failing step and rolled back cleanly.
- **The discovery tools are excellent for agents.** `describe_command` with JSON Schema and `command_list` filters make the command catalogue workable.
- **The expression engine handled 138 per-group expressions correctly**, and `get_property` returns the `evaluated` value, which is great for verification.
- **Rendering is fast.** 120 frames at 1080p H.264 took about 1.5 s on the CPU.
- **The VectorCraft-to-EffectCraft round trip works.** The `.ai` export imported as a composition with one layer per VectorCraft layer, and `layer.create shapesFromVector` produced editable shape layers.

The job: take a brand mark from SVG, split it into named layers in VectorCraft, export it, then build a 4-second staggered reveal of 137 shape groups in EffectCraft, render H.264 and GIF, and hand off an editable `.ecproj`. Everything worked end to end. I will file the other findings separately.

## The request

**Problem.** `run_script` and `file.runScript` are refused when the server runs with automation roots, as documented in `docs/mcp.md` (and as answered on #500). For an agent, scripting is the natural interface. This job needed one loop over 136 shape groups; without scripting it took about 410 individual `prop.set` / `prop.setExpression` commands, sent in two very large batches.

title: Bug: a reopened project always opens on its first composition; the active comp is not saved
author: MazenGit
body:
**Summary.** The comp that was active when a project was saved is not restored when the project is reopened. The project always opens on its first (lowest-id) composition. The saved `.ecproj` has no active-comp field at all.

I first hit this after importing an `.ai` as a composition. The import created a helper comp, and the saved project (reopened over MCP and in the desktop app) opened on that static comp instead of the animated one, so it looked as if the animation was broken. A repro with no import shows the same behaviour.

**Steps to reproduce** (headless CLI, Windows PowerShell 5.1; `\"` escaping is needed in 5.1)

```powershell
$ec = "effectcraft-cli"          # 0.8.0
$d  = "C:\Users\<user>\...\scratch"
& $ec --empty --save-as "$d\repro.ecproj" --json run `
  comp.new '{\"name\":\"CompA\"}' `
  comp.new '{\"name\":\"CompB\"}' `
  comp.open '{\"comp\":\"CompB\"}'
# -> comp.new {"comp":1}, comp.new {"comp":2}, comp.open {"comp":2}

& $ec --project "$d\repro.ecproj" info --json
# -> project.activeComp = 1 (CompA)
```

The same happens with the original scenario: `file.import` of an `.ai` with `importAs: compositionLayerSizes` (creates comp 26), two `comp.new` (27, 28), `comp.open` on 28, save. On reopen `project.activeComp` is 26, not 28. Importing the `.ai` after the first comp gives the same result (reopens on id 1).

title: mcp: agent-ergonomics requests from a sandboxed MCP job (motion preview, numeric ids, group anchors, conversion clutter, batch note)
author: MazenGit
body:
These come from the same job as my other reports (a 137-group staggered reveal built over the confined MCP server). They are ordered by impact for agent use. Each section stands on its own, so say if you would rather have any of them split out.

## 1. [Medium] Agents need a way to see motion

**Problem.** An agent can only inspect single frames (`render_frame`, `render_preview`). Timing problems, such as a key element whose entrance is too brief to register, were invisible to the agent and only showed up once a human watched the render.

**Request.** Either of these:
- `render_preview` / `render_frame` with `times: [..]` returning a contact-sheet grid image; or
- a `render_preview_clip` returning a small inline animated GIF or WebP (for example 320 px, 10 to 15 fps).

Both let an agent self-review motion before handing anything over.

## 2. [Medium] Numeric IDs are treated as names in some tools

**Repro.**
- `get_layer {layer: 98}` returns `no layer "98"`, while `execute_command` with `layer: 98` works.
- `render_frame {comp: 2985}` returns `no composition "2985"`, while passing the comp name works.

**Expected.** `docs/agents.md` and the CLI help describe a layer or comp as "id or name", so a numeric value should resolve as an ID.

## 3. [Medium] No command to center shape-group anchor points on their own content

**Problem.** After `shapesFromVector`, every group has its anchor and position at [0,0]. Scaling 136 groups each about its own center needed one anchor plus one position command per group, with the centers computed outside the app.

**Request.** Something like `shape.centerGroupAnchors {layer, groups?}` that moves each group's anchor to its content center and offsets its position so nothing moves on screen. `layer.centerAnchor` already does this for whole layers; this is the same idea for groups inside a shape layer. It matters most for agents without scripting (see [my separate request for a confined script mode](https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft…

title: Working Gamma 2.4 doesn't reach float footage (OpenEXR), and Interpret As Linear Light encodes float footage twice
author: vangel76
body:
After Effects parity, docs/gaps.md ranked gap #10 "Colour pipeline differences" (follow-up of #495, reported there by @Romasikkk after #645).

With no working space, After Effects encodes linear-light footage with the project's Working Gamma: the sRGB curve at 2.2, a pure 2.4 power curve at 2.4 (0.18 → 0.490, 0.051 → 0.290). On main the setting exists and applies to Interpret As Linear Light, but float footage (OpenEXR, float TIFF) is sRGB-encoded when it is decoded, so with Working Gamma 2.4 a linear EXR still gives 0.18 → 0.4627. Turning on Interpret As Linear Light for the EXR encodes a second time on top of the decode's own encoding (0.18 → 0.7255).

Expected: float footage is encoded with the Working Gamma's curve (unmanaged), and Interpret As Linear Light on float footage encodes its linear values once, with the same curve.

I'm working on this and will open a PR.

title: Scripting: property groups and properties are callable (layer("ADBE Effect Parade"), fxGroup(1))
author: vangel76
body:
Split out of #625 (Duik port), as suggested there: scripting-host gaps as separate, focused issues.

**After Effects behaviour:** property groups and properties are callable in ExtendScript. `layer("ADBE Effect Parade")`, `layer("Effects")`, `fxGroup(1)` or `effect("Slider Control")("Slider")` are shorthands for `.property(nameOrIndex)`, and scripts like Duik use them throughout.

**EffectCraft today (reported in #625 by @cdinhoo against main of 10 October):** these calls fail with `TypeError: not a callable function`; only the explicit `.property(...)` form works.

**Expected:** a Layer, PropertyGroup and Property object can be called with a name, match name or 1-based index and returns the same as `.property(...)` (or null when absent), without breaking existing `.property` access.

title: Scripting: support #include / //@include / #includepath in scripts and ScriptUI panels
author: vangel76
body:
Split out of #625 (Duik port), as suggested there: scripting-host gaps as separate, focused issues.

**After Effects behaviour:** ExtendScript's preprocessor handles `#include "file"` (and `//@include`) by inlining the file, resolved relative to the including script, with `#includepath` adding search folders. Script panels and libraries such as Duik/DuAEF rely on it.

**EffectCraft today (reported in #625):** an unchanged script fails at its first `#include`.

**Expected:** `#include` / `//@include` / `#includepath` are resolved relative to the script's folder, with a depth limit and include-once protection against cycles, a clear error for missing files, and the same file-access permissions scripts already have. `#target`, `#targetengine` and `#strict` are ignored.

I'm working on this and will open a PR.

title: Scripting: $.evalFile and a minimal BridgeTalk host identification
author: vangel76
body:
Split out of #625 (Duik port), as suggested there: scripting-host gaps as separate, focused issues.

**After Effects behaviour:** ExtendScript offers `$.evalFile(file[, timeout])` to evaluate another script file, and `BridgeTalk` (`BridgeTalk.appName`, `BridgeTalk.appVersion`, …), which frameworks such as DuAEF read during initialisation to identify the host.

**EffectCraft today (reported in #625):** `typeof BridgeTalk` is `undefined`, so DuAEF's initialisation fails, and `$.evalFile` is incomplete.

**Expected:** `$.evalFile` evaluates a file (path relative to the calling script, same permissions and depth limits as `#include`) and returns its last value; a minimal `BridgeTalk` object identifies the host honestly as EffectCraft (`appName = "effectcraft"`, its version) rather than impersonating After Effects; inter-application messaging stays unsupported with a clear error.

**Expected:** animated WebP imports as footage with duration, frame rate derived from the frame delays, loop count/alpha respected, frames decoded once and cached like GIF; still WebP stays a still; malformed or huge animations fail with a clear error instead of hanging.

title: Proportional Scrubbing: Ctrl+Alt (Cmd+Opt) scrub spreads a value change across selected layers by selection order
author: vangel76
body:
After Effects parity, docs/gaps.md ranked gap #21 "Small 26.x features" (ui-parity.md: Timeline row, "Proportional Scrubbing (26.2) missing").

**Missing:** After Effects 26.2/26.3 (Adobe help "Proportional Scrubbing in timeline" and the 26.2 beta announcement) lets you hold Ctrl+Alt (Cmd+Opt on macOS) while scrubbing a blue hot-text value in the Timeline with several layers selected. Instead of every layer getting the same change, the change is distributed linearly by selection order: the first selected layer doesn't change, the last selected layer takes the full scrubbed amount, and the layers between get even shares. Shift still multiplies the change by 10. Keyframed properties get a key at the current time (or the existing one is changed). Today our multi-layer scrub (#491) always applies the same change to every selected layer.

**Expected:** the Timeline hot-text scrub with Ctrl+Alt / Cmd+Opt sends `prop.set` with a `proportional` flag; the engine weights each selected layer's share as index/(n-1) in selection order, in one undo step, also drivable over the control channel / MCP.

title: Scripting: run repeating app.scheduleTask tasks until cancelTask
author: vangel76
body:
Split out of #625 (Duik port), as suggested there: scripting-host gaps as separate, focused issues (see also #758, #759, #760, #766).

**After Effects behaviour:** `app.scheduleTask(code, delayMs, repeat)` returns a task id; with `repeat = true` the code runs every `delayMs` until `app.cancelTask(id)`. ScriptUI panels use this for polling and UI refresh.

**EffectCraft today:** one-shot tasks run after the script finishes, but repeating tasks are queued and then skipped (`crates/script/src/runtime.rs`, `eval_with_tasks`: `if repeat { continue; }`), so they never run.

**Expected:** repeating tasks keep running at (roughly) their interval while their owner is alive (e.g. an open ScriptUI panel or a running script host session), stop on `app.cancelTask`, when the panel closes or the project closes, and are bounded (minimum interval, cap on concurrent tasks, existing script time limits per run; a throwing task is reported and cancelled instead of spamming errors).

I'm working on this and will open a PR.

title: Fuzz project files: a seeded mutation fuzzer for File > Open (.ecproj JSON and .ecprojx XML)
author: vangel76
body:
After Effects parity, docs/gaps.md workstream G3 "Stability and a green main" — the fuzzing bullet: "Fuzz the inputs we don't control: project files, imported media and documents, expressions, scripts, control-channel and MCP requests. Every crash found becomes a regression test."

What is missing: nothing fuzzes project files today. File > Open reads `.ecproj` JSON and, since Save a Copy As XML, `.ecprojx` through a hand-written XML reader (`crates/engine/src/xml_project.rs`) that has a single round-trip test and no hostile-input coverage (for example its element recursion has no depth limit, so a deeply nested file would overflow the stack and abort instead of returning an error). Opening a project then runs effect migration and effect-bounds evaluation over whatever the file holds.

Expected behaviour: any bytes handed to File > Open give either a project or an error, never a panic, abort or hang.

Plan: a dependency-free, deterministic, seeded mutation fuzzer that runs as a normal bounded `cargo test` in `effectcraft-engine` (byte-level and JSON-structure mutations of seed projects, both encodings, through the real `file.open` path, `catch_unwind` reporting panics as failures, time-bounded, a larger run behind an env var), plus a fix and a minimal regression test for every crash it finds. No cargo-fuzz/libfuzzer dependency (it can be wired to cargo-fuzz later).

I'm working on this and will open a PR.

title: Object Matte: turn a point/box prompt into a tracked object matte (After Effects 26.2)

body:

**Missing:** After Effects 26.2 added Object Matte: pick an object in the frame (a click, optionally a box around it) and get a matte that isolates it and follows it through the shot. EffectCraft has Roto Brush (strokes, MobileSAM optional) but no prompt-driven Object Matte.

**Expected (first slice):**
- An **Object Matte** effect (Effect ▸ Matte, `ec.matte.objectmatte`): Object Point, optional Box, a Reference Frame and a tracking range (frames before/after), Feather / Contrast / Shift Edge, Invert and a Matte view.
- The prompt becomes the matte on the reference frame and is propagated frame by frame (Track Object), or segmented independently on every frame. It reuses the Roto Brush segmentation engine and the model chosen in Settings ▸ Roto Brush (MobileSAM when installed, the classical graph cut otherwise), and its content-keyed cache, so no new model or dependency.
- An `objectMatte.apply {layer, point, box?, frame?, …}` command so agents/CLI can create one; the engine keeps its input key current like Roto Brush so edits upstream recompute the matte.

Not in this slice: an on-viewer hover/click tool, the background propagation job and the disk cache (26.5).

title: Fuzz expressions: a seeded mutation fuzzer for the expression parser and evaluator
author: vangel76
body:
After Effects parity, docs/gaps.md workstream G3 (Stability: fuzz the inputs we don't control — expressions). Follows #779 / PR #785 (File ▸ Open fuzzer) with the same dependency-free, seeded approach.

**Missing:** expressions on properties are arbitrary user/agent/project text, run on the render threads by the boa-based `effectcraft-expr` crate (array-maths rewriter + boa parser/compiler + AE object model). Nothing exercises it with hostile input, so a crafted or corrupted expression can still panic, overflow a render thread's stack (aborting the app), hang a frame, or allocate without bound.

**Expected (AGENTS.md "Never crash"):** any expression text evaluates to a value or an "Error at line N: …" message, within bounded time and memory; the property falls back to its keyframed value.

**Plan:** a dependency-free seeded mutation fuzzer in `crates/expr` tests: a seed corpus of real expressions (wiggle, loopOut, valueAtTime, thisComp.layer(…).transform…, linear/ease, text styles, paths, sourceRectAtTime, markers, seedRandom…), byte- and token-level mutations (flips, splices, deletions, interesting tokens, deep nesting / long operator chains, huge numbers), each run through `check_syntax` and `eval_standalone` on its own thread under `catch_unwind` with a timeout; bounded default run (< 10 s), env vars for long runs. Fix every panic, hang, stack overflow or runaway allocation it finds, each with a minimal regression test.

I'm working on this and will open a PR.

title: Opening a project: hold compositions, solids and footage to After Effects' 30,000 × 30,000 px limit (and sane frame rates, pixel aspect, motion-blur samples)
author: vangel76
body:
After Effects parity, docs/gaps.md workstream G3 "Stability" / AGENTS.md never-crash: our File ▸ Open fuzzer (PR #785) noted that comp sizes (and likely other dimensions: layer/solid sizes, frame rate, duration, pixel aspect, resolution factor) read from a project file are not capped, so a hostile or corrupt project can trigger a huge allocation/render. After Effects limits comps to 30,000 × 30,000 px (public docs); find the existing limits used by the UI/commands (comp.new etc.) and enforce the same bounds when LOADING projects (.ecproj JSON and .ecprojx XML) and in every command that sets them — clamp or refuse with a clear error, never allocate first. Claim via a new issue: `comp.new`/`comp.settings` clamp width/height to 4–30,000 px, frame rate to 0.001–1000 fps and motion-blur samples to 2–64, but `Project::from_json` (File ▸ Open of .ecproj and .ecprojx, templates, auto-save recovery, offload) accepts any value: a comp of 1,000,000,000 px, a solid or footage item of 4 billion px, a 0 or 10^18 fps rate (zero-length frames), a non-positive duration or 4 billion motion-blur samples, all of which reach the renderer. Several commands also set sizes without the upper bound (`layer.newSolid`, `layer.settings`, `file.importSolid`, Crop Comp to Region of Interest / Layer Bounds, New Comp from Selection, Pre-compose). Expected: one set of limits in the project model, applied when a project is read (out-of-range values are clamped and the user is told what was corrected, so the project still opens) and by every command that sets a size.

I'm working on this and will open a PR.

title: Opening long videos reads the whole file into memory
author: vangel76
body:
Importing or opening a movie reads the whole file into memory, so a long clip costs its full size in RAM (twice while probing).

**Measured** (peak RSS of a process that probes one file, then decodes its first frame and 0.1 s of audio through `MediaPool`; Linux, `VmHWM`):

| file | size | peak after probe | peak after frame + audio |
|---|---|---|---|
| H.264 + AAC 1080p MP4 | 245 MiB | 494 MiB | 497 MiB |
| same stream remuxed to MKV | 245 MiB | 494 MiB | 497 MiB |
| ProRes 422 + PCM 1080p MOV | 283 MiB | 571 MiB | 574 MiB |

A 45-minute video costs its full size, ×2 during import.

**Cause:** `crates/media/src/probe.rs` (`probe`, ~L18) and `crates/media/src/pool.rs` (`Inner::source`/`Inner::read`, ~L566) call `std::fs::read` and then `filmcraft_codecs::open_bytes`. The demuxers only need the container index and then single samples.

**Fix plan:** open container footage in place, the way FilmCraft's desktop app does (its `FileReader` + `filmcraft_media::reader::open_reader`). The pinned FilmCraft rev already has `open_reader`/`reader_openers` (MP4/MOV, Matroska/WebM, MXF, Ogg, MPEG-PS/TS); `FileReader` came later, so EffectCraft gets a small positional-read `ByteReader` of its own. Stills, layered/vector documents, models and whole-file audio formats (WAV, FLAC, MP3…) keep reading the file whole. In-memory files (`MediaPool::add_bytes`, the web build) keep `open_bytes`. Probe results, frames and audio stay the same.

Found while working on #329.

I'm working on this and will open a PR.

title: Keyboard shortcuts fail to trigger when using non-Latin keyboard layout (e.g., Arabic)
author: ViolinMai
body:
### Problem Description
Keyboard shortcuts that map to English/Latin letters (e.g., `Ctrl+C`, `Ctrl+Z`, `Cmd+S`, single-key tool shortcuts like `V`) do not register or trigger when an Arabic (non-Latin) keyboard layout is active in the OS.

### Cause ( i think )
Shortcut handling currently inspects the logical/text character produced by the layout (`key_without_modifiers` / logical key character, e.g. mapping to `ؤ` or `س`) instead of checking the physical key position (`KeyCode` / `PhysicalKey` via scan codes), or it lacks a fallback to the US QWERTY equivalent when evaluating hotkeys.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Switch OS input language to Arabic.
2. Focus the timeline, canvas, or main editor window.
3. Press any standard shortcut (e.g., `Ctrl+Z` or single-key tool activation).
4. **Result:** The shortcut is ignored or consumed as plain text input.

### Expected Behavior
Shortcuts should trigger based on physical key positions or resolve against the primary US/Latin layout, regardless of the active typing language (standard behavior in software like After Effects, VS Code, and Blender).

### Suggested Fix
1. **Match on Physical Keycodes (`PhysicalKey` / `KeyCode`):**
   * When handling global action shortcuts and tool selectors, check `KeyEvent::physical_key` instead of relying strictly on `KeyEvent::logical_key`.
2. **Fallback to Latin translation:**
   * If logical key matching is preferred for user-customizable bindings, resolve the active key press through a fallback lookup matching the underlying key's US QWERTY glyph when a modifier (`Ctrl`/`Cmd`/`Alt`) is held down or outside text editing fields.

title: Hardware video decoding (VA-API / NVDEC / VideoToolbox / Media Foundation) via filmcraft-platform
author: vangel76
body:
**Gap:** #15 in `docs/gaps.md` / the "Hardware video decode" row of `docs/hardware-parity.md`: After Effects decodes H.264 / HEVC in hardware; EffectCraft decodes everything in software (FilmCraft's pure-Rust decoders), on every platform.

**What FilmCraft already provides.** FilmCraft's `crates/platform` (`filmcraft-platform`, layer L5, the one FilmCraft crate allowed `unsafe`, for OS FFI only; FilmCraft `docs/adr/0001-platform-ffi.md`) registers a hardware decoder factory in front of FilmCraft's own decoders via `filmcraft_codecs::register_video_decoder`:

- macOS: VideoToolbox (H.264 / HEVC, 8/10-bit, 4:2:0 / 4:2:2)
- Windows: Media Foundation / DXVA
- Linux: NVDEC (NVIDIA driver) and VA-API (libva loaded at run time with `libloading`, so no build-time headers)

Streams the hardware does not take, and every stream while `filmcraft_codecs::hw::set_hardware_decoding(false)`, keep the software decoders; a hardware decoder that fails mid-stream switches to software transparently (`HybridDecoder`). FilmCraft exposes this as Settings ▸ Playback ▸ Hardware decoding.

1. Bump the FilmCraft pin (root `Cargo.toml`, currently `2c5ba7a`, 2026-10-03, before `filmcraft-platform` existed) to one current FilmCraft `main` commit and fix the API breaks with minimal changes; full workspace test run, differences recorded.
2. Add `filmcraft-platform` as an optional, desktop-only dependency of the app binary (`apps/effectcraft`) only. EffectCraft's own code stays free of `unsafe` (`forbid` unchanged); all FFI lives in FilmCraft's crate. L0–L4 and the wasm build are untouched.
3. Register it at startup; Preferences ▸ Media "Hardware decoding" toggle (command id, automation id, i18n) mirroring FilmCraft's, calling `set_hardware_decoding`; the active backend shown in the GPU / system information report. Software fallback stays automatic.
4. Measure headlessly (H.264 / HEVC, 1080p and 4K, long GOP): ms/frame, scrub latency, CPU, software vs NVDEC vs VA-API, PSNR against software…

title: Scripting: `app.executeCommand(16)` is not Undo (EffectCraft's own command numbers)
author: raisulsohan
body:
Found while porting [LazyMapLayers](https://github.com/raisulsohan/lazymaplayers-effectcraft) (a map design and map animation panel for After Effects) to EffectCraft. Its host script runs in EffectCraft with a small compatibility layer, and all 369 kinds of expression it generates match After Effects after the workarounds: thank you for EffectCraft!

**Tested with** EffectCraft 0.8.0, Windows x64 (portable zip), headless: `effectcraft-cli script repro.jsx --empty`. The "Actual" output below is from that run.

**What happens.** `app.executeCommand(number)` treats the number as a position in EffectCraft's own
command list ([prelude.js#L1802](https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft/blob/f953cd2855bf36beffa6a4d608e9bf4b226e9442/crates/script/src/prelude.js#L1802)),
so After Effects' menu command ids run something else. `16` (Edit ▸ Undo in After Effects) is
`roto.model.remove` in EffectCraft 0.8.0. `app.findMenuCommandId("Undo")` returns 22, so scripts that
look ids up by name work; scripts with a hard-coded After Effects id (common, because
`findMenuCommandId` depends on the UI language in After Effects) do not, and the numbers will shift
whenever a command is added.

**What After Effects does.** `16` is Undo; ids are stable across versions and languages.

**Repro.**

```js

var prop = comp.layers.addNull().transform.rotation;
prop.setValueAtTime(1, 45);

writeLn("keys after executeCommand(16): " + prop.numKeys);
writeLn("findMenuCommandId('Undo') = " + app.findMenuCommandId("Undo"));
```

**Expected (After Effects).**

```
keys after executeCommand(16): 0
findMenuCommandId('Undo') = 16
```

**Actual (EffectCraft 0.8.0).**

```
executeCommand(16) threw: invalid parameters for `roto.model.remove`: missing `id`
keys after executeCommand(16): 1
findMenuCommandId('Undo') = 22

body:

EffectCraft's interface is localized — 618/618 fixed menu entries and 463 panel/dialog strings
in `zh-hans` — but **effect names still render in English**: `EffectSpec::name` in
`crates/effects` is a `&'static str` that nothing routes through a catalog.

author: faresdjefaflia

Description:
When importing an SVG file that contains multiple distinct vector paths (or layers) into EffectCraft, the software merges all elements into a single layer/shape. This makes it impossible to animate individual components separately (e.g., moving a background separately from an icon).

Import the SVG into EffectCraft.

title: [Bug] Sequentially named SVG files are incorrectly imported as 'Image Sequence'
author: faresdjefaflia
body:
Description:
When exporting multiple SVG files from VectorCraft at the same time, they are saved with sequential names (e.g., Asset-1.svg, Asset-2.svg, Asset-3.svg). When attempting to import these files into EffectCraft, the software incorrectly assumes they are frames of a video and imports them as a single "Image Sequence". The shapes then appear as tiny, broken, or identical rectangles. Importing a single SVG file (without sequential numbers) works correctly.

Steps to Reproduce:

Select multiple assets in VectorCraft and export them together as SVGs (resulting in names like Asset-1.svg, Asset-2.svg).

Import these files into EffectCraft.

Observe that they are imported as an "Image Sequence" (as shown in the Project panel) and fail to display the actual vector shapes.

Try importing a single SVG from an isolated folder — it works perfectly.

Expected Behavior:
EffectCraft should treat sequentially named SVG files as separate vector assets, not as an image sequence, and should not attempt to merge or sequence them.

OS: Ubuntu (installed via .deb package)

author: akdavid4real

Version: EffectCraft 0.8.0, Linux x86_64 (deb), effectcraft-cli
OS: Ubuntu (kernel 7.0)

2. Run with `effectcraft-cli script repro.jsx --empty`:

```js
var io = new ImportOptions(new File("/path/to/layered.psd"));
io.importAs = ImportAsType.COMPOSITION_CROPPED_LAYERS;
var it = app.project.importFile(io);
it.typeName + " " + it.numLayers;

title: Linux: installed fonts missing from the font list (Flatpak host fonts, XDG and fontconfig folders not scanned)
author: vangel76
body:
Reported on Discord by Prin.Ing (CachyOS, EffectCraft installed and started through the ArtCraft Launcher): fonts installed on the system don't show up in EffectCraft's font list. Dragging font files in doesn't help, and Preferences has no font settings.

## Cause

The ArtCraft Launcher installs EffectCraft as the Flatpak `ai.storyteller.effectcraft`. Inside the sandbox, `/usr/share/fonts` holds only the runtime's fonts and `~/.local/share/fonts` doesn't exist. Flatpak exposes the host's fonts at `/run/host/fonts`, `/run/host/user-fonts` and `/run/host/local-fonts`, and tells fontconfig about them in `/etc/fonts/conf.d/50-flatpak.conf` and `/run/host/font-dirs.xml`. `DirectorySource::system()` (`crates/text/src/fonts.rs`) scans only `/usr/share/fonts`, `/usr/local/share/fonts`, `~/.local/share/fonts`, `~/.fonts` and `EFFECTCRAFT_FONT_DIRS`, so it never sees them.

The same gap affects native installs that keep fonts somewhere fontconfig knows about but the hard-coded list doesn't: `$XDG_DATA_HOME/fonts`, `$XDG_DATA_DIRS/*/fonts`, and `<dir>` entries in `/etc/fonts/fonts.conf`, `conf.d` or `~/.config/fontconfig`.

## Repro

On the same machine, with the same `~/.local/share/fonts/AlexBrush-Regular.ttf`:

```
effectcraft-cli --empty exec text.fonts --params '{"query":"alex"}'      # native build: count 1
flatpak run --command=effectcraft-cli ai.storyteller.effectcraft --empty exec text.fonts --params '{"query":"alex"}'   # count 0
flatpak run --command=effectcraft-cli ai.storyteller.effectcraft --empty exec text.fonts --params '{}'   # 25 families (native: 320)
```

Native build with `XDG_DATA_HOME=/tmp/x` and a font in `/tmp/x/fonts`: the font is not listed.

## Expected (After Effects)

After Effects lists the fonts installed in the operating system's standard font location ([Formatting characters and the Character panel](https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/desktop/add-text/formatting-characters-and-paragraphs/formatting-characters-character-panel.html)). On Linux…

title: [CRASH] Scrubbing over spatial keyframes with huge values panics in motion-path arc length (NaN clamp)
author: vangel76
body:
Found while investigating a crash reported on Discord by BiniFn (#artcraft-bugs, "Effectcraft Crashing", macOS M1): "it crashes when i scrub on the timeline after i add null objects and keyframes on them". **I could not confirm that this is BiniFn's crash.** The ordinary flow (nulls with keyframes, parent chains, expressions, 3D, a camera rig, motion paths and the Graph Editor shown, the time ruler dragged quickly, CPU and GPU viewer) does not crash on main. A fuzzer over keyframe evaluation did find a crash on that same scrub path.

### Repro (main, 67434e9)
1. Add a Null (Layer ▸ New ▸ Null Object) and keyframe its Position at, say, 0 s = `-1.7e308, 0` and 2 s = `1.7e308, 0`. The Position field accepts any finite number. The same values can also arrive through a script, the control channel or a project file.
2. Select the null so its motion path shows, then move the current time between the keys.

The app aborts with `min > max, or either was NaN` in `f64::clamp`: viewer → `viewer_overlays::motion_path` → `Prop::value_at` → `keyframe::evaluate` → `SpatialSeg::at_length`. The coordinates overflow, the arc length becomes NaN (inf − inf), and the `len <= 0.0` guard lets NaN through to `s.clamp(0.0, len)`. This runs on the UI thread, outside the command guard, so the whole app goes down.

### Expected
Per AGENTS.md "Never crash", evaluating any keyframes must not panic. A degenerate segment should just evaluate to a finite fallback.

I'm working on this and will open a PR.

title: Project panel: Tab in the rename field strands keyboard focus, so Enter no longer renames
author: vangel76
body:
Reported on Discord (#artcraft-bugs) by Tony_Rebello: "Effect craft is not allowing to rename files when pressing enter, it either proceeds to rename completely or jumps to another field as if i was pressing TAB."

## What I found on upstream/main (67434e9)
The plain path works: select an item in the Project panel, Enter opens the name field with the name selected, typing and Enter commits and gives the keyboard back.

What breaks is **Tab** inside the rename field. egui treats Tab in a single-line field as "move keyboard focus to the next widget": the rename is committed, and keyboard focus lands on the row's label swatch (another Tab: the row's name cell, and so on through the panel). While that widget holds focus:
- **Enter no longer renames.** The panel's Enter only runs when no widget has keyboard focus, so Enter instead "clicks" the focused widget (egui's keyboard activation).
- **The arrow keys move egui's focus between widgets**, i.e. the keyboard "jumps to another field".
- App shortcuts are paused too (`menus.rs` returns while a widget wants the keyboard).
Only Escape or a mouse click gets out of that state.

## Repro (kittest)
1. A project with a comp; click its name in the Project panel.
2. Enter (rename field opens), type, Tab.
3. Enter: no rename field opens; focus stays on `("plabel", <id>)`.

The same happens on the branch of open PR #780 (Project panel keyboard navigation / AccessKit): there the Enter gate accepts a focused *row*, but the label swatch Tab lands on still blocks it.

After Effects: "Rename selected composition, layer, folder, effect, group, or mask: Enter on main keyboard (Windows) / Return (macOS)", and Enter commits the new name (Adobe, *Keyboard shortcuts in After Effects*, https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/using/keyboard-shortcuts-reference.html). title: Composition viewer blurs pixels at 100 % and above (frame not on the physical pixel grid, bilinear magnification)
author: vangel76
body:
Reported on Discord (#artcraft-bugs) by Arashi (Windows 10, anime footage with aliased lines): "The view on viewport is antialiased, even when on full quality. This means that the pixels are slightly blurred to be smooth ... the final product ends up looking differently than what I see in the viewport."

## Reproduction (upstream/main, headless `snapshot` example)
Comp 301×201, black background, a 1 px white line and a 51×51 red solid (all edges on whole pixels), Resolution Full, nothing selected. Compared `render.frame` with the viewer's on-screen pixels at magnification 100 % and 200 %:

| pixels per point | magnification | frame origin (physical px) | exact pixels | max error |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | 100 % | 689.80, 239.75 | 99.17 % | 102 |
| 1.25 | 100 % | 899.88, 324.81 | 99.17 % | 74 |
| 1.5 | 100 % | 1109.95, 409.88 | 99.17 % | 43 |
| 1.0 / 1.25 / 1.5 | 200 % | fractional | 99.17 % | 159–180 |

title: Timeline current-time field: committing the displayed time jumps to another frame at 29.97 / 59.94 fps (drop-frame mismatch)
author: vangel76
body:
## Problem

Reported on Discord (#artcraft-bugs, "EffectCraft Rabbit's hole") by TW15T: "got this loop bug when try to change time in TL TC, can't validate time, stay stuck".

In a composition at 29.97 or 59.94 fps, committing the Timeline's current-time field moves the playhead to a different frame. Even pressing Enter on the unchanged text jumps the playhead back (e.g. frame 1800, shown `0:01:00:00`, lands on frame 1798), and a typed time never lands where it was typed, so the entry looks like it loops and never validates. The same happens for `time.set` with `timecode`, which is what the field runs. It is the same class of bug as #530 (fixed for Start Timecode and Frames numbering) but for drop-frame rates.

## Reproduce

1. New comp at 29.97 fps (or 59.94), longer than 1 minute.
2. Go to frame 1800: the Timeline shows `0:01:00:00`.
3. Double-click the display, press Enter without changing anything. The playhead is now at frame 1798 (`0:00:59:28`). Typing `0:01:00:00` gives the same.

Headless check: for every frame of a 600 s comp, `time.set {"timecode": <display>}` returns the same frame at 23.976, 24, 25, 30 and 60 fps, but misses 16182 of 17982 frames at 29.97 and 32364 of 35964 at 59.94.

## Root cause

`display_time` formats the Timeline timecode as non-drop-frame (`:` separators), but `parse_display_time` (crates/engine/src/commands/time.rs) parses the typed text as drop-frame whenever the rate supports it, so the displayed text is read as a different frame from minute 1 on.

## Expected

Typing a time in the field goes to that time; the displayed value round-trips. After Effects: Go to Time / the current-time field jump to the entered timecode in the project's Time Display Style (Adobe Help, "Timeline panel" / "Go to Time": click the current-time display, type a new time, press Enter).

I'm working on this and will open a PR.

title: GPU export: `render --gpu` sends the GPU a whole batch of frames, runs out of memory and falls back to the CPU without logging it
author: MatejKozlovsky
body:
## What happens

`crates/export` renders a batch of frames in parallel, one per rayon thread and at most 16. With `--gpu`, every frame of the batch goes to the GPU compositor at once. At 4K the concurrent frames exhaust GPU memory (or system memory with a software adapter). A frame the GPU cannot take renders on the CPU, and nothing is logged, so a `--gpu` export is no faster than a CPU export or runs out of memory.

Each GPU frame is also read back as RGBA f32 (133 MB at 4K) and converted to 8-bit YUV 4:2:0 on the CPU before encoding.

## Measured

On a test PC (Ryzen 7 5800X, RTX 3090 24 GB, Windows 10), main exports a 3 s 4K comp (90 frames, H.264) with `--gpu` in 201.9 s and on the CPU in 171.9 s (median of 3 runs each). The `--gpu` output is MD5-identical to the CPU render, so every frame fell back to the CPU, and none of the fallbacks was logged. VRAM peaked at about 23.8 GB.

On a machine without a hardware GPU (llvmpipe, 8 threads, 16 GB RAM), main `--gpu` on `Bench4K` (0.5 s, half resolution) was killed by the OOM killer after 16.8 s. The CPU export took 5.6 s.

## Expected

`--gpu` keeps a bounded number of frames on the GPU, adds CPU workers only where they help, logs when and why a frame falls back to the CPU, and reads back only the 8-bit 4:2:0 data the encoder needs.

title: Audio: 5.1 and other multichannel sources are not downmixed to stereo (centre/LFE/surrounds dropped)
author: vangel76
body:
Reported on Discord by Risll (clipping report; no clipping reproduced, but investigating it showed this).

## Problem
Footage audio is read through `MediaPool::audio_samples` -> `read_stereo`, which takes only the first two planar channels. For a 5.1 file the centre (dialogue), LFE and both surround channels are dropped, so a 5.1 clip comes out far quieter than a proper downmix. AAC 5.1 is worse: FilmCraft's AAC-LC decoder delivers AAC's native order (C L R Ls Rs LFE), so the 'left' output is the centre and the 'right' output is front-left; front-right is lost. Verified with a 5.1 clip with one sine per channel (AAC: L=FC, R=FL; AC-3, WAV, FLAC, Opus: L=FL, R=FR, everything else lost). Mono plays at full level on both sides and is not touched here.

## Expected
A standard ITU-R BS.775 stereo downmix (L = FL + 0.707 FC + 0.707 surround, R likewise), scaled so loud 5.1 does not clip, in the correct channel order per layout, shared by preview, waveform and export. LFE is left out of the stereo downmix (ffmpeg/swresample default `lfe_mix_level` 0; I could not find Adobe documentation stating it).

I'm working on this and will open a PR.

title: Feature request: Halation and Diffusion (Pro-Mist) effects
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Splitting a concrete piece out of #700 and #600 (Magic Bullet / Red Giant requests).

Two effects that most "film look" setups depend on and that EffectCraft doesn't have yet:

**Halation**: the red/orange glow film gets around bright highlights, from light bouncing off the film base. Glow gets close-ish but it's the wrong shape and colour. Usual controls: threshold, radius, strength, tint, and a highlight-only mask.

**Diffusion**: soft bloom like a Pro-Mist / Black Pro-Mist filter. It lifts highlights and lowers contrast a bit without blurring the image. Usual controls: strength, size, highlight vs. overall diffusion, and whether it lifts the blacks (white mist vs. black mist).

Both would need to work at 32 bpc on linear footage, since that's where people grade. For reference, Magic Bullet Looks has both, and so do Dehancer and the free FilmConvert-style tools.

title: Feature request: film stock emulation (negative + print stock looks)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Another piece from #700 / #600.

Film stock emulation is the main thing people buy Magic Bullet Film, Dehancer or FilmConvert for. You pick a negative stock and a print stock and the footage takes on that stock's colour response, contrast curve and grain.

EffectCraft already has the pipeline for this (OCIO looks, 3D LUTs, ACES, Add Grain). What's missing is the stocks themselves, plus a simple effect to pick one. Something like:

- negative stock + print stock dropdowns
- exposure / push-pull
- strength (blend with the original)
- optional matched grain per stock

The profiles would need to come from our own measurements or published data, not copied from a commercial product.

title: Feature request: look browser and saved looks (Magic Bullet Looks-style workflow)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Last piece from #700 / #600.

Magic Bullet Looks is mostly a UI on top of ordinary corrections. You build a look as a chain (subject → lens filter → camera → post), see the result live, then save it and reuse it. Most of the individual corrections already exist in EffectCraft (Lumetri, Curves, Glow, Vignette, Grain, OCIO/LUTs). What's missing is the workflow:

- a browser of look presets with thumbnails rendered from the current frame
- saving a stack of effects as a named look and applying it to other layers
- a global strength slider for the whole look
- exporting a look as a .cube LUT where possible

Animation Presets cover some of this already. A proper look browser would make grading a lot faster for people coming from Looks.
