title: M2 Mac: graphics device lost during export
author: earlvanze
body:
## Report

Discord user Matt Walak reports that EffectCraft cannot export on an M2 Mac. Their screenshot shows a modal: “EffectCraft: graphics device lost. The graphics driver stopped responding, so EffectCraft has to close.” The modal says unsaved changes were saved to an Auto-Save `.ecproj` file in Documents/EffectCraft Auto-Save before closing.

Source: EffectCraft channel, 2026-10-12 06:26 and 06:36 Europe/Madrid. The user has not yet supplied the EffectCraft version, macOS version, export format, composition details, or exact reproduction steps.

## Expected

Export completes, or reports a recoverable error without terminating the app.

## Actual

Graphics device is lost during the user's export attempt and EffectCraft closes after showing the recovery message.

## Triage

The render queue and export formats exist (docs/roadmap.md M10). This is a platform-specific failure needing reproduction, not a missing export feature. Existing open issues found for GPU/startup problems do not describe an M2 Mac graphics-device loss during export.

## Reproduction details needed

- EffectCraft and macOS versions
- Export format/settings, composition dimensions and frame rate, effects used
- Whether it occurs with a new empty/simple composition
- Any repeatable steps and relevant crash/diagnostic log without private project data

title: `setInterpolationTypeAtKey` / `keys.velocity` silently no-op on effect params (0.4.0)
author: HicyWon
body:
# `setInterpolationTypeAtKey` / `keys.velocity` silently no-op on effect params (0.4.0)

## Summary
`setInterpolationTypeAtKey` and `keys.velocity` work correctly on **transform properties** (e.g. Position), but silently do nothing on **effect parameters** (e.g. CC Sphere's Light Direction). No error is thrown; the calls just have no effect.

## Environment
- effectcraft-cli 0.4.0 (macos-universal)
- macOS (MacBook Pro M2)

## Repro
1. Create a comp, add a solid layer.
2. Add **CC Sphere** effect. Animate **Light Direction** with 2+ bezier keyframes (custom temporal ease, e.g. inEase speed=0 influence=16.67).
3. Via script (`run_script` / MCP):
   ```js
   var parade = layer.property("ADBE Effect Parade");
   var p = parade.property(2).property("lightDirection"); // CC Sphere is 2nd effect
   p.__select(1);
   __call("keys.velocity", {
     comp: comp.id,
     inSpeed: [0], inInfluence: [0.1667],
     outSpeed: [0], outInfluence: [0.3333]
   });
   // Also tried:
   p.setInterpolationTypeAtKey(1,
     KeyframeInterpolationType.BEZIER,
     KeyframeInterpolationType.BEZIER);
   ```
4. **Expected**: keyframe 1 becomes bezier with the given ease.
   **Actual**: keyframe stays linear (straight lines in graph editor). No error.

Same script works on `layer.property("ADBE Position")`.

## Additional context
- `add_keyframe` via MCP with `"interpolation": "bezier"` also results in linear keys for effect params (works for transform props).
- The property object is valid: `p.numKeys` returns correct count, `p.name` is correct. Only the write APIs are no-ops.
- Related: `setTemporalEaseAtKey` has a units mismatch (JS validates influence 0.1–100, Rust `keys.velocity` clamps to 0.001–1.0), forcing a direct `keys.velocity` workaround — which then hits this bug.

## Impact
Blocks precise AE → EffectCraft migration of effect-parameter keyframe easing. Transform easing migrates fine; effect param easing is stuck at defaults.

title: Desktop: unknown arguments are imported as files, and a bad --control value is dropped silently
author: Nael-Nathanael
body:
## What happens

The desktop app accepts any command-line argument it doesn't know and passes it to `file.import` as a file. Nothing is reported. A missing or non-numeric `--control` value is also dropped silently, and the app then starts without a control server.

The `--automation-read-root` and `--automation-write-root` options exist only in `effectcraft-cli mcp`, but VectorCraft's desktop app also accepts them, so they are easy to pass to EffectCraft too:

```sh
EffectCraft --control 47613 --automation-read-root /tmp/ec-repro/dir
# effectcraft: control server listening on 127.0.0.1:47613
```

The app starts and the control channel works, but it is not confined to the folder, and nothing says the flag was ignored. The flag and the folder went to `file.import`; both now show in Recent Footage (`prefs.json`):

```
"recentFootage": ["/tmp/ec-repro/dir", "--automation-read-root", ...]
```

`--control` without a number:

```sh
EffectCraft --control --demo
```

`--demo` is taken as the port, fails to parse, and the app opens with no control server and no message. `EFFECTCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT=abc` is ignored in the same way.

## Expected

An unknown option, or `--control` without a valid port, prints an error naming the argument and exits with a non-zero status before the window opens. VectorCraft already does this for its root flags (storytold/vectorcraft#1157).

## Cause

`parse_args` in `apps/effectcraft/src/main.rs`:

```rust
"--control" => out.control_port = args.next().and_then(|p| p.parse().ok()),
...
_ => out.files.push(a),
```

## Environment

EffectCraft 0.8.0 on macOS 27.0.1, Apple M1. The same code is on `main`.

I'd like to fix this and will open a PR.

title: Composition viewer does not auto-pan when a dragged mask vertex reaches the panel edge (AE auto-scrolls)
author: themsgcentre
body:
## Description

When a mask vertex (or any draggable path point) is moved toward the edge of the
Composition viewer while zoomed in, the view does not pan. The drag stops at the
panel edge and the point cannot be moved further in that direction. AE
auto-scrolls the view in the drag direction once the pointer reaches the panel
edge, which is what makes zoomed-in rotoscoping practical.

## Expected behavior (AE)

While dragging a mask vertex — or a point of a path currently being drawn with
the Pen — moving the pointer against the panel edge pans the view in that
direction, so the drag continues past the previously visible area.

## Current behavior

The view stays fixed. The only way to reach points outside the visible area is
to release the drag, pan (hold Space for the Hand tool), then re-grab the point
and continue. This interrupts rotoscoping badly, since points often need to move
beyond the current view at high zoom levels.

## Steps to reproduce

1. New project, new composition (e.g. 1920×1080), add a solid
2. Zoom the Composition viewer to 200% or more
3. Draw a mask on the solid with the Pen tool
4. Switch to the Selection tool and drag one mask vertex toward the edge of the
   viewer panel
5. The pointer reaches the edge; the view does not move; the vertex cannot be
   dragged any further

## Context

- App version: 0.8.0
- Related: #468 (the Timeline does not pan when its time header is dragged to
  the edge — the same missing drag auto-pan, different panel), #995 (adds
  auto-scrolling during drag selection in the Timeline)

## Notes

The same likely affects other viewer drags: Pen points while drawing, motion-path
handles, layer handles, effect points. It might be worth implementing this once
as a shared "auto-pan at panel edge while dragging" behavior for the viewer
rather than per-drag-type.

title: Mask vertices cannot be multi-selected: no Shift-click, no marquee selection
author: themsgcentre
body:
## Description

After selecting one mask vertex, there is no way to add more vertices to the
selection. Only two states exist: exactly one vertex selected, or all of them
(after clicking the mask's row or Mask Path in the Timeline). AE
supports arbitrary multi-selection of mask vertices, which is essential for
rotoscoping (grabbing several points of an edge and nudging them together).

## Expected behavior (AE)

- **Shift+click** on another vertex adds it to the selection (and toggles it
  off if it was already selected).
- **Marquee**: dragging on empty viewer area draws a selection box and selects
  every mask vertex inside it (additive with Shift).

## Current behavior

- Shift+click on a second vertex: nothing is added (the selection stays as it
  was; the clicked point behaves like a plain click).
- Dragging to draw a box does not start a marquee. Dragging over the layer
  moves the layer's source instead, even over pixels the mask cuts away
  (transparent areas). There is no click-through on transparent pixels, so a
  mask that covers most of the frame leaves no empty area to start a marquee
  from.

## Steps to reproduce

1. New composition, add a solid, zoom in
2. Draw a mask with the Pen tool (several vertices)
3. Switch to the Selection tool, click one vertex — it selects
4. Shift+click a second vertex — the selection does not grow
5. Try to drag a selection box over several vertices — the layer moves instead

## Context

- App version: 0.8.0
- The in-repo precedent for the expected interaction: puppet pins already
  support Shift-click and marquee selection (PR #2). Mask rows selecting all
  their points came with PR #221.
- The missing click-through on transparent/masked-out pixels was reported in
  #513 (last bullet); that issue was closed via #645, which addressed the
  deselect part.
- Related multi-selection gaps: #982 (effects cannot be shift-selected).

vertex moves all se…

title: Quick Offset: Ctrl/Cmd+Alt drag staggers selected layers and keyframes in selection order (AE 25.4)
author: barchukmov
body:
Follow-up to #284. The reply there said Ctrl/Cmd+Alt drag offset isn't an After Effects feature, but it is: Adobe added it as **Quick Offset** in After Effects 25.4 ([Adobe's feature post](https://community.adobe.com/t5/after-effects-beta-discussions/feature-focus-quick-offset-stagger-your-layers-just-by-dragging-them/m-p/15377178)).

**Behaviour in After Effects**
- Select several layers, or keyframes on several layers, and hold **Ctrl+Alt** (Windows) / **Cmd+Opt** (macOS) while dragging in the timeline.
- The drag moves the **last selected** layer; the first selected stays put, and the ones in between spread out evenly between them, **in the order they were selected**.
- For keyframes, each layer's selected keyframes move together as one group, and the groups are staggered the same way.
- With a marquee (box) selection, the order is the layers' order in the comp, not the direction the box was drawn.
- Staggered layers and keyframes can land on subframes, for smoother motion.
- The whole drag is one undo step.

**Today in EffectCraft**
Alt-dragging keyframes scales them in time, and Keyframe Assistant ▸ Sequence Layers offsets layers. Neither one staggers interactively by selection order.

**To do**
- `selected_layers` and `selected_keys` are already ordered lists; make sure every way of selecting (click, Ctrl/Cmd-click, Shift-click, marquee) leaves them in the order described above.
- Ctrl/Cmd+Alt drag on layer bars and on keyframes staggers them as described.
- Add a command (e.g. `layer.quickOffset` / `keys.quickOffset`) so agents and the CLI can use it too.

---
_Summarised by Claude from a discussion with @barchukmov. If something doesn't make sense, feel free to contact @barchukmov._

title: i18n: which signal should the CJK fallback use - curated lists, the font's name table, or coverage?
author: FeiLiuEM
body:
The Craft apps each decide for themselves which face to use when Han ideographs are missing, and they do it in four different ways. effectcraft just split its Chinese list by script (#1015): that fixes the case that was plainly wrong — a `zh-hant` interface drawn with Simplified forms, because the two scripts share their code points, so the fallback search's coverage test cannot tell a Simplified face from a Traditional one. Whether the family should keep that shape is your call, not something I want to settle inside one app.

The three approaches as they exist today:

**1. Curated family lists, one per script** — effectcraft (`crates/text/src/fonts.rs`: `SIMPLIFIED_CHINESE_FAMILIES` / `TRADITIONAL_CHINESE_FAMILIES`, chosen from `zh-hant` / `zh-TW` / `zh-HK` / `zh-MO` against anything else Chinese) and photocraft (`crates/text/src/cjk.rs`: `CjkScript::{Simplified, Traditional}`, a list per script ordered by `script_order(locale)`, from #185).

*Good:* cheapest, deterministic, unit-testable without installed fonts. *Bad:* needs curating, and it only knows the names someone thought to add — today's lists are Windows/macOS-centric plus the Noto and Source Han names.

**2. The font's own `name` table language tags** — wordcraft (`crates/fonts/src/fontdb.rs`: `name_language_matches(ui, tag)` matches `zh-Hans` / `zh-TW` / `ja-JP` against the interface language, with the region rules: Simplified for mainland China and Singapore, Traditional for Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macao, bare `zh` Simplified).

*Good:* works for any installed face, including ones nobody listed, and it judges the face itself rather than its name. *Bad:* needs the name table parsed and the face to ship localised names; the same file still falls back to family-name heuristics for its Chinese tie-break.

**3. Coverage-scored picking, or a single list reordered by the locale** — wordcraft's `pick_face` scores each face by how many of the needed characters it maps, then prefers a Regular style and a Simplified…

`theme::tests::interface_symbols_have_a_glyph_in_every_family` (added in 01400f0, merged as #865) is red on the current tip (9efe753) — the FreeBSD job failed on the push to `release` ([run 38234073233](https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft/actions/runs/38234073233)):

```
test theme::tests::interface_symbols_have_a_glyph_in_every_family ... FAILED
• has no glyph in FontId { size: 12.0, family: Name("medium") }
crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs:667
```

It reproduces on a plain Linux desktop too (Noto and JetBrains families installed), twice: in a working tree, and in a fresh `git worktree` of `origin/main` on the same machine. `main`'s last own push run (67434e9, 2026-10-11 15:51Z) was green, and 01400f0 is the only commit that touched that symbol list (`git log -S'"▸•›·▶◀●○⚠…×"' -- crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs`), so it came in with that change.

Instrumenting the same context shows which families are short — the two *named weight* ones:

```
REGISTERED FAMILIES: [Proportional, Monospace, Name("medium"), Name("semibold")]
  family Proportional      missing = ""
  family Monospace         missing = ""
  family Name("medium")    missing = "•›·▶◀●○⚠…×"
  family Name("semibold")  missing = "•›·▶◀●○⚠…×"
```

So it is not the font data. I parsed the cmaps of the bundled faces (`assets/fonts/`): Inter-Regular/Medium/SemiBold carry `•` (U+2022, glyph 1464) and the other nine, and lack only `▸`; JetBrains Mono carries all eleven (`▸` = glyph 1513). `Proportional` and `Monospace` do find all eleven, so `jbmono` is registered and reachable — the named weight families are the ones whose chain does not reach it.

`install` inserts `Name("medium") = ["inter-medium", "inter"]` and `Name("semibold") = ["inter-semibold", "inter"]`, then pushes `jbmono` into every non-monospace family, so `inter-medium` alone should satisfy ten of the eleven. Something in how those two families resolve keeps them from it — I could not pin that down from outside, so I am reporting the numbers rather than…

title: [Bug Reports & Feature Requests] Viewer Transform Controls Not Working, Render Queue Freezing at 0%, and Workflow Improvement Suggestions
author: fawezzayati
body:
Hi EffectsCraft team!

First of all, thanks for your work on EffectsCraft! I've been testing the software and noticed a couple of issues, along with some features and workflow improvements that I believe would make the editing and compositing experience significantly smoother, especially for users coming from After Effects.

I've organized everything into **bug reports** and **feature requests** for clarity.

## 🐛 Bug Reports

### 1. Transform controls not working in the Composition Viewer
- Moving, scaling, or rotating 2D/3D solids and footage directly in the Composition Viewer sometimes doesn't work.
- However, adjusting the same properties manually through the layer's Transform parameters works correctly.
- This makes it difficult to position and manipulate layers visually.

### 2. Render Queue freezing at 0%
- Occasionally, rendering gets stuck at **0%** immediately after clicking Render.
- The Stop button becomes unresponsive.
- Even after removing the composition from the Render Queue, the interface continues to indicate that rendering is in progress at 0%.
- The render process appears to remain active or frozen, with no way to cancel it normally.

## 💡 Feature Requests & Workflow Improvements

### 1. Quick effect search and application (Ctrl + Space)
It would be great to have an effect search console similar to Video Copilot's FX Console for After Effects.

- Press **Ctrl + Space** to open a searchable effects panel.
- Search for an effect and apply it directly to the selected layer.
- Ideally, support keyboard navigation for even faster workflows.

The 3D Camera Tracker would be much more useful if we could:

- Create solids, null objects, or other layers positioned and oriented according to those points.

This is particularly useful for VFX compositing and integrating CGI elements into tracked footage.

title: Ticket to close tickets: already done, duplicates, or off-topic
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
Yes, this is a ticket whose only job is to close other tickets. If it works, it closes itself at the end. 🎫➡️🗑️

Same format as storytold/photocraft#2993. We went through the open EffectCraft issues looking for ones that are already done on `main`, are duplicates, or are spam/off-topic. Each verdict below was checked against a merged PR (state verified via the GitHub API) or the issue's own comments, and all 2 issues were still open at 2026-10-12 14:47 UTC. When in doubt, an issue stayed off the list: partial fixes, umbrella and tracking issues, and anything whose only fix is a pending PR are not here.

Maintainers: closing these should take one click each. Please spot-check before closing; if one is wrong, say so here and we'll take it off. Each listed issue also has a "Ready to close" comment with the same reason.

## 👯 Duplicates (1)

| Issue | Duplicate of |
|---|---|
| #985 Timeline right-click Pre-compose only takes one layer | #878 (closed as completed: the timeline context menu acts on the whole selection); the reporter agreed |

## 🗑️ Spam, empty and off-topic (1)

| Issue | Why |
|---|---|
| #406 "filmcraft": can't preview 4K log footage | filed in the wrong repo (title says FilmCraft); the same reporter filed it on FilmCraft as storytold/filmcraft#414. No reply to the maintainer's question |

## How this list was made

Candidates were found mechanically across all 186 open issues: a merged PR that references the issue, a contributor or maintainer comment saying "fixed on main by #…" / "duplicate of #…", or a very short or empty body. Each candidate was then read by hand, including later comments (anything where someone reported it still happening was dropped). Issues with no such signal weren't reviewed one by one, so there are surely more in there.

Once the issues above are closed, this ticket has done its job and can close itself. 🎉

title: Re-imported footage shows a stale decode from an earlier project when the file was overwritten with the same byte size
author: noctelvirei
body:
Thanks for EffectCraft. We're moving a book-trailer pipeline onto it (Blender multi-layer EXR → EffectCraft over the control channel), and the Blender round trip is exactly what we needed. We found one footage-cache problem along the way.

**Version:** EffectCraft 0.8.0 (MSI), Windows 11. Driven over `effectcraft.exe --control 9877` with `effectcraft-cli --bridge 9877`.

**What happens**

If a footage file is decoded in one project, then overwritten on disk with a file of the same byte size, a fresh import of that path in a new project shows the old pixels. Reload Changed Footage doesn't catch it either, because the new project sees the file for the first time. An explicit Reload Footage on the item fixes it.

**Minimal repro** (two solid 64×64 PNGs, both 181 bytes: `red.png`, `blue.png`)

```sh
E=effectcraft-cli; x(){ $E --bridge 9877 exec "$@" --json; }
setup(){ x file.newProject; x file.import --params "{\"paths\":[\"$1\"],\"sequence\":false}";
         x comp.new --params '{"name":"c","width":64,"height":64,"frameRate":24,"duration":1}';
         x layer.addItem --params '{"item":1}'; }

cp red.png case.png;  setup $PWD/case.png
$E --bridge 9877 render-frame --frame 0 --out r.png     # red, correct
x file.newProject
cp blue.png case.png; setup $PWD/case.png               # new project, fresh import
$E --bridge 9877 render-frame --frame 0 --out r.png     # RED: stale, expected blue
x footage.reloadChanged                                 # {"files":0,"reloaded":0}
x file.reloadFootage --params '{"items":[1]}'
$E --bridge 9877 render-frame --frame 0 --out r.png     # blue, correct
```

**Observed (centre pixel)**

| Step | PNG (same size) | EXR (sizes differ: 1351 vs 1327 bytes) |
|---|---|---|
| Project A, import red | (255, 0, 0) | (255, 0, 0) |
| Project B, file now blue, fresh import | **(255, 0, 0), stale** | (0, 0, 255) |
| `footage.reloadChanged` | `{"files":0,"reloaded":0}`, still stale | (0, 0, 255) |
| `file.reloadFootage` | (0, 0, 255) | (0, 0, 255) |

title: Windows 11: dragging the window across monitors with different display scales makes it balloon and jump (winit 0.30.13 mixed-DPI drag)
author: msaulc
body:
## Summary

EffectCraft locks winit 0.30.13 without a winit patch, so it should have the Windows 11 mixed-DPI drag bug found in GridCraft (storytold/gridcraft#760, fix in storytold/gridcraft#761). Dragging the window across the boundary between monitors with different display scales makes it flip between the two scales and grow by their ratio.

**Expected effect in EffectCraft:** the window balloons and jumps during the drag. It should not crash: the device asks for the adapter's limits, capped at 16384, and wgpu errors are logged.

This comes from reading EffectCraft's code at its current `main`, not from a run of EffectCraft. GridCraft, on the same stack, was reproduced and fixed on hardware.

## What happens (measured in GridCraft)

Windows 11 24H2, a 3440×1440 monitor at 100 % next to a 3840×2400 panel at 250 %. Dragging the window from the 250 % panel toward the top edge of the 100 % monitor, client size per step: 3600×2250 → 1440×900 → 3600×2250 → **9048×5757**. GridCraft then crashed in wgpu's `Surface::configure`: `Requested was (9048, 5757), maximum extent for either dimension is 8192`.

## Cause

- **winit 0.30.13's `WM_DPICHANGED` handling during a live drag** (rust-windowing/winit#4041, #4600). winit replaces the rect Windows suggests with its own and nudges it back onto the monitor being left, which triggers another DPI change. winit master fixed this in 488c036a (#4341), but only for 0.31; eframe 0.36 needs 0.30.

title: PSD import: thousands of nested groups overflow the stack (SIGABRT)
author: vangel76
body:
Importing a PSD with thousands of nested groups overflows the stack and aborts the whole process (SIGABRT, not catchable by the last-resort panic guard).

Cause: `Psd::tree()` (crates/psd/src/lib.rs) builds an unbounded nested `Node::Group` tree, and the importer (`crates/engine/src/psd_import.rs`: `build_comp` -> `build_layer` -> `build_comp`) recurses over it with no depth limit. The tree's own `Drop`, `Clone` and `PartialEq` recurse too. A ~1 MB file with 4000 `lsct` divider/folder pairs aborts on an 8 MiB stack.

Expected (per AGENTS.md "Bound recursion"): groups nest at most 64 deep; deeper ones are flattened into their depth-64 parent with a warning in the import result, and no layer is lost.

title: PSD: non-finite values from descriptors/EngineData/32-bit samples reach layers; Warp::apply and Rect::new can panic
author: vangel76
body:
Never crash audit of `crates/psd` (and its importer in `crates/engine/src/psd_import.rs`):

**Non-finite values reach the layers.** EngineData numbers are parsed with `str::parse::<f64>()`, which accepts `nan`, `inf`, `-inf` (`/FontSize nan /Tracking inf /Leading -inf` yields `TextStyle { size: Some(NaN), tracking: Some(inf), leading: Some(-inf) }`). The same holds for descriptor doubles, the six `f64` of the `TySh` transform, the `PlLd` quad, the `expA` f32 values and 32-bit samples (`samples()` returns raw f32, `srgb_encode(NaN)` stays NaN). The importer passes them on unchecked (`d.size = s * scale`, `set_vec2` for position and scale).

**Public API panic paths** (not reachable from files today): `placed::Warp::apply` with style `warpCustom` and an empty or short `mesh` panics with index out of bounds (`cols`, `rows`, `mesh` are public, the `mesh.len() == (3c+1)(3r+1)` invariant is only checked in `Warp::read`), and `Rect::new(i32::MAX, 0, 1, 1)` panics with an overflow.

Fix: the reader drops non-finite values and clamps font size and spacing, `samples()` maps NaN to 0 and +inf to 1, the importer guards finiteness, `Warp`/`Rect` use `get()` and saturating/checked math. Each with a regression test.

title: PSD: one damaged layer record discards the whole document
author: vangel76
body:
A single damaged layer record makes `Psd::parse` fail, so the whole Photoshop document is rejected even though the header, the merged (flattened) image and most layers are intact.

Reproduce: write a layered PSD, change the `8BIM` signature of the second layer record to `XBIM`. `Psd::parse` returns `Err(Invalid("layer record signature"))`. The same happens for a channel length that runs past the layer-info end (`r.skip(c.len)?`) or a channel count above 64.

AGENTS.md says lenient readers fall back and record the repair. Expected: keep the header and the merged image, drop the layers, record a warning, and import the flattened image as one layer with a visible "Layers could not be read" message. Damage to the header, or a missing merged image, stays a hard error.

title: PSD: share the duplicated decode, placed-transform and writer helpers
author: vangel76
body:
The PSD crate (crates/psd) has several duplicated code paths that can be shared without changing any behaviour:

- the placed-layer transform reader in `lib.rs` (`SoLd`) re-implements `placed::floats`, and builds the corner quad twice
- raw / RLE / ZIP plane decoding is written twice (`decode_channel` and `composite`)
- `write.rs` has its own big-endian helpers and a UTF-16 string writer that duplicate `descriptor::put_u32` / `put_unicode`; a dead `let _ = h;`
- the `[]<>/(` delimiter set is spelled twice in `engine_data.rs`

I'm working on this: a pure refactor, existing tests unchanged, plus tests for the ZIP / RLE composite paths that had no coverage.

title: PSD: avoid redundant plane copies, per-pixel mask tests and repeated quad solves
author: vangel76
body:
Some hot paths in crates/psd do work that can be avoided without changing any output:

- decoding copies the plane bytes: raw channels (`to_vec`), every ZIP plane of the merged image (`to_vec` only to un-predict in place), and the 32-bit un-predictor allocates a row copy per row
- the layer-mask loop evaluates the "inside the mask rect" test for every pixel, and walks every pixel even when there is no mask data or the factor is exactly 1.0
- placed layers (smart objects) re-solve the corner quad's projective matrix for every mapped point (1089 times for the bounds, again for the size, 2401 times for the grid of one bake), and the bake loop recomputes loop-invariant values per pixel

I'm working on this: results must be bit-identical, proven by tests against the old implementations kept as references, plus counter tests (no timings).

title: PSD decode: bound the memory of one decode and of smart-object bakes (OOM abort on a crafted file)
author: vangel76
body:
## Problem

The PSD reader bounds one decoded image to 2^28 pixels (`MAX_DECODE_PIXELS`), but the real peak of one decode is a multiple of that, and a smart-object bake size comes straight from the file.

**Composite / layer decode** (`crates/psd/src/lib.rs`): `composite()` holds the ZIP output (up to `want * rowbytes * h`, about 5 GiB at 2^28 px), one `Vec<f32>` per channel, and the result `Vec<[f32; 4]>` (4 GiB at 2^28 px) at the same time, roughly 10-14 GiB. `layer_pixels()` holds the channel planes, the alpha plane, the mask plane and the output. A 16384 x 16384 header plus a few-MB ZIP stream of zeros (about 1000:1) therefore ends in an out-of-memory abort, which cannot be caught. On wasm32 `vec![[0f32; 4]; n]` with n >= 2^27 panics with a capacity overflow.

**Smart-object bake** (`crates/psd/src/placed.rs`): `placed_size` clamps only to 16384 x 16384 and `render_placed` then allocates `ow * oh` float RGBA pixels (4 GiB). A perspective quad corner of 1e6 is enough (`needs_bake` is true and the size is 16384 x 16384). The size also arrives from the project (`Footage` width/height) in `media/layered.rs`.

## Expected

An over-large file gives a clean `Err` with a message (an ordinary import/decode error), never an abort or a panic.

## Plan

- A byte budget for the sum of all simultaneously live buffers of one decode (4 GiB on 64-bit, 1 GiB on 32-bit), checked against the expected peak before anything is allocated; `try_reserve` instead of `vec![..; n]`; the ZIP limit sized by what the channels need.
- Channels are written straight into the result instead of one `Vec<f32>` per channel plus a result.
- Smart-object bake: at most 4x the document size across and at most 2^24 pixels.
- Tests: huge header plus tiny ZIP stream is refused, the budget counts the sum, an absurd quad corner stays inside the caps, and normal documents decode bit-identically to the previous implementation (kept as a reference in the test module).

title: Adding a marker interrupts audio during playback
author: nanox333
body:
**Cause:** adding a marker replaces the comp, so every cached viewer frame stops matching. The preview then has to re-render those frames before the sound can continue, and if it falls behind, the audio stops. Markers don't change any pixels, so that re-render is wasted work.

**Repro:** I added a test that adds a marker to a comp and checks whether its frames change. It fails on `main`.

**Workaround:** add markers while playback is stopped.

title: Stretched audio is resampled by copying the nearest sample, which adds audible error
author: nanox333
body:
**Cause:** when a layer is stretched to a speed that isn't a whole number (for example 70% or 33%), the mixer copies the nearest source sample for each output sample, instead of blending the two samples either side. That adds error. At 48 kHz the worst error on a 440 Hz tone is 0.025, about 30 dB below the signal. At 8 kHz it's 0.15.

**Repro:** I added a test that mixes a 440 Hz tone at 70% and 33% stretch and compares it with the exact tone. It fails on `main`.

**Related reports:** two users said audio quality got worse after precomposing and after rendering. I haven't confirmed that this is the same cause, and the render export path isn't covered yet.

Visual Easing / Speed Curve Sliders: • Introduce simple UI sliders to dynamically manipulate the cubic-bezier influence percentages of selected keyframes without forcing the animator into the complex Graph Editor. • Under the hood, this should directly rewrite the keyframe tangent command values (Property and keyframe commands). 2. Instant Anchor Point Matrix (9-Point Grid): • A native UI widget containing a 3x3 grid to instantly snap the bounding box anchor point of selected shape/text layers to the (Top-Left, Center, Bottom-Right, etc.). • Mathematically, this evaluates the layer's local bounding box dimensions and alters the translation matrix vector while preserving the global spatial position to prevent layer jumping. 3. Procedural Keyframe / Layer Offset (Sequencer): • An input field to step/stagger selected layers or keyframes sequentially by an X amount of frames or seconds. • This can easily utilize Rust's thread-safe iteration arrays to apply temporal offsets across hundreds of selected properties instantaneously. 💡 Why this is a Massive Win for EffectCraft Integrating these commands natively eliminates the lag associated with legacy JavaScript-based script engines. title: Codec crates are pinned to a FilmCraft commit that isn't on any FilmCraft branch
author: SteamSmith
body:
EffectCraft's `Cargo.toml` (lines 74 onward) pulls the 26 `filmcraft-*` codec crates from

```toml
git = "https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft", rev = "2c5ba7a72619935f0481f99d59409e0d1844b234"
```

That commit (2026-10-04, "webm: decode VP9 alpha from BlockAdditions") doesn't seem to be part of FilmCraft's history any more:

- `compare/2c5ba7a…main` reports **diverged**: the pinned commit isn't on `main` (which is now ~1,450 commits ahead).
- Its parent, `a27b50a`, *is* on `main`; on `main` the next commit after it is `fafd82b` ("Crash and blank-screen fixes"). So it looks like the commit was amended or rebased after EffectCraft pinned it.
- It isn't part of any FilmCraft PR, and it isn't signed.

Builds still work, because GitHub serves a commit by hash even when no branch contains it. Two practical downsides:

1. Nothing in either repo shows which reviewed FilmCraft history the codecs come from, which makes the dependency harder to audit.
2. If unreachable objects are ever cleaned up (or the repo is recreated or migrated), the pin can stop resolving and EffectCraft won't build.

For what it's worth, I looked through the code of those 26 crates at that commit. There's no network code and no `unsafe`, no build scripts, and process calls appear only in tests (FFmpeg comparison oracles), so this is about traceability, not anything wrong in the code.

**Suggestion:** re-pin to a FilmCraft tag or a commit on `main`. Before re-pinning, check that the VP9-alpha change actually landed on `main`, since it may not exist there in this form. Alternatively, publish or vendor the codec crates.

title: #659's layer cover makes effect stacks on text/shape layers run at comp size (~5 GB extra VRAM in parallel export)
author: MatejKozlovsky
body:
Since fa733bfb (#659), `Renderer` calls `target.cover(layer_size)` (crates/render/src/lib.rs) on every text or shape layer that has an enabled video effect. This grows the effect buffer from the painted content (glyph box, drawn bounds) to the whole layer rectangle (`effect_bounds`, comp-sized). From there, every texture in the stack is at least 1920x1080 RGBA32F (~33 MB) in a 1080p comp, plus any glow or blur margins. Each frame in flight pays this again.

The cover reaches the GPU in two ways:

1. **GPU target:** `GpuFx::cover` (crates/gpu/src/effects.rs) allocates a comp-size texture and copies the content into it. This accounts for ~2.6–2.8 GB.
2. **CPU target:** the `FxTarget::cover` default runs `Buf::cover`, which grows the CPU `Buf` to the layer region. `Accelerator::effects` then uploads that comp-size buffer and runs the GPU chain at that size. This accounts for the remaining ~2.1–2.7 GB. Confidence in this mechanism is medium-high; it comes from reading the code and was not measured separately.

## Measurements

Test PC (RTX 3090 24 GB), Singularity Premium comp, 1920x1080 PNG, 60 frames. Values are peak VRAM over idle. The 60-frame runs agree with 180-frame runs to within 2%. All builds use default threads.

| Build | Peak VRAM |
|---|---|
| main 9efe753 | 22.48 GB |
| #688 before merge | 11.65–12.32 GB |
| main + #688, unmodified | 16.95 GB (5 of 6 runs) |
| main + #688, `GpuFx::cover` disabled | 13.82–14.39 GB |
| main + #688, `cover` call in `Renderer` disabled | 11.65–12.29 GB |

Disabling the cover call removes the whole ~5 GB gap. Bisect on main:
- Commits up to 0b2d85b8 add nothing (11.65 GB).
- d1e6aa2e is the first point that includes #659, and peak VRAM is already up there.

The gap depends on frames in flight: +0.3–0.6 GB with `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1`, ~+5 GB with default threads.

8 layers in the comp go through this path: Disk Inner, Disk Mid, Disk Outer, Photon Ring, Shockwave 1, Shockwave 2, Lensed Halo and Title. Their effects are glow, gaus…

## Summary

Three tests fail on Windows on unmodified `main` (470ea7a3, 0.9.2). Windows 11, Rust 1.99, `cargo test --workspace --release --no-fail-fast`. The failures come from path-format assumptions that hold on macOS/Linux; the same test in #515 was fixed for macOS with `canonicalize()`, which on Windows now yields a `\?\` path. The rest of the workspace passes (about 2000 tests, plus `fmt`, `clippy -D warnings`, `layers`, `assets`, `wasm`).

## Failures

1. `effectcraft-cli`, `render_out_is_relative_to_the_working_directory` (`apps/effectcraft-cli/tests/cli.rs:290`)
   ```
   left:  "C:\Users\…\render-out\proj\out\d.gif"
   right: "\\?\C:\Users\…\render-out\proj\out\d.gif"
   ```
   The test builds its expected path from `root.canonicalize()`, which carries the `\?\` verbatim prefix on Windows; the CLI reports the plain path.

2. `effectcraft-host`, `tests::render_queue_exports_to_a_sink` (`crates/host/src/lib.rs:319`)
   ```
   left:  ["C:/no-such-dir-effectcraft-sink-test/a.gif", …]

   ```
   The expected value is made with `std::path::absolute("/no-such-dir…")`, which resolves against the current drive (here `E:`); the sink reports `C:/…`.

title: Template import: extraction paths can escape the media directory and bypass write-root confinement
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity: High. Confidence: high (source-confirmed mechanism).**
Read-only static audit of upstream `main` at [549e9d8](https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft/commit/549e9d825132986d6167c1432cd3328efcbb0278). No runtime reproduction, destructive testing, or exploit development was performed; production failure frequency is not measured.

## Source and root cause
- [crates/engine/src/commands/essential.rs:901-915](https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft/blob/549e9d825132986d6167c1432cd3328efcbb0278/crates/engine/src/commands/essential.rs#L901-L915)
- [crates/automation/src/confine.rs:46-90](https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft/blob/549e9d825132986d6167c1432cd3328efcbb0278/crates/automation/src/confine.rs#L46-L90)

The importer strips `media/`, computes `media_dir.join(rel)`, creates parent directories, and calls `s.services.write_file(&out_s, v)` without validating archive path components or symlink destinations. `Path::join` does not confine its right-hand operand. Separately, confinement classifies `essential.importTemplate` only as a read of the archive; it does not authorize the extracted writes. Write failures are also silently omitted from `written`.

## Conditions
A user imports a syntactically accepted template containing media entries whose resolved destination is outside the intended extraction directory, or a pre-existing directory symlink redirects extraction. Under confined automation, even ordinary embedded media can be written when only a read root was granted.

## Impact
Files writable by the application can be overwritten outside the extraction directory. Read-only automation policy is violated. This requires template import and application filesystem permissions; no automatic execution or remote-code execution is claimed.

## Recommended remediation
Validate all extraction destinations before any mutation: reject parent/root/prefix components, account for symlinks, and enforce confinement on the actual writes. Use safe extract…

title: Template export: dependency reads are not checked against automation read roots
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity: High. Confidence: high (source-confirmed mechanism).**
Read-only static audit of upstream `main` at [549e9d8](https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft/commit/549e9d825132986d6167c1432cd3328efcbb0278). No runtime reproduction, destructive testing, or exploit development was performed; production failure frequency is not measured.

## Source and root cause
- [crates/engine/src/commands/essential.rs:823-842](https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft/blob/549e9d825132986d6167c1432cd3328efcbb0278/crates/engine/src/commands/essential.rs#L823-L842)
- [crates/automation/src/confine.rs:69-90](https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft/blob/549e9d825132986d6167c1432cd3328efcbb0278/crates/automation/src/confine.rs#L69-L90)

Export iterates footage paths/sequence entries and packages the raw bytes from `s.services.read_file(file)`. Successful media decoding is not a prerequisite for packaging those bytes. Confinement checks the export destination supplied in the command but not these source paths stored in the project.

## Conditions
Confined automation opens a permitted project that references an application-readable file outside the allowed roots, then exports a template containing that footage dependency to an allowed destination.

Bytes outside the automation read roots can be copied into a permitted output archive, violating the advertised read boundary. The outside file still must be readable by the application account.

## Recommended remediation
Authorize every dependency read at the file-service boundary, carrying the automation policy through export. Do not rely solely on top-level command parameter validation. Fail with a clear denied-dependency error before publishing an incomplete archive.

## Suggested regression tests
Create an allowed project/output area and a separate harmless sentinel outside all roots. A template export must reject the outside dependency and never include sentinel bytes; verify in-root footage and image-sequen…

title: Template import: saturating ID offsets collapse distinct objects and silently drop items
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity: High. Confidence: high (source-confirmed mechanism).**
Read-only static audit of upstream `main` at [549e9d8](https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft/commit/549e9d825132986d6167c1432cd3328efcbb0278). No runtime reproduction, destructive testing, or exploit development was performed; production failure frequency is not measured.

## Source and root cause
- [crates/project/src/essential.rs:714-750](https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft/blob/549e9d825132986d6167c1432cd3328efcbb0278/crates/project/src/essential.rs#L714-L750)
- [crates/engine/src/commands/essential.rs:930-945](https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft/blob/549e9d825132986d6167c1432cd3328efcbb0278/crates/engine/src/commands/essential.rs#L930-L945)
- [crates/engine/src/commands/import_project.rs:84-89](https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft/blob/549e9d825132986d6167c1432cd3328efcbb0278/crates/engine/src/commands/import_project.rs#L84-L89)

`offset_ids` uses `saturating_add(offset)` for IDs and reinserts items with `p.items.insert(it.id, it)`. Distinct large IDs can therefore both become `u64::MAX`, and the later insertion replaces the earlier item. Template import calls this without the checked range preflight used by project import. Its manifest comp calculation also uses unchecked `tcomp.0 + base`.

## Conditions

title: Background autosave: a failed write marks the revision saved and suppresses later retries
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity: High. Confidence: high (source-confirmed mechanism).**
Read-only static audit of upstream `main` at [549e9d8](https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft/commit/549e9d825132986d6167c1432cd3328efcbb0278). No runtime reproduction, destructive testing, or exploit development was performed; production failure frequency is not measured.

After spawning a background write, `autosave_now` immediately assigns `saved_revision`, `last_slot`, and `last_path`, and updates the sentinel. `autosave_wait` takes the pending job and returns its error without restoring the saved bookkeeping. Subsequent ticks skip when `saved_revision == Some(self.revision)`.

## Conditions
A background autosave fails (for example a temporary I/O or space error), the error is collected, storage becomes writable again, and the user makes no further project edit.

## Impact
The latest dirty revision remains without a successful recovery copy indefinitely despite later autosave intervals. A later crash can lose that work; recovery metadata can also refer to the failed save. The code does return the write error, so this is not a claim that failures are never reported.

## Recommended remediation
Track pending and successfully committed revisions separately. Advance saved revision/path/rotation and recovery metadata only after a successful join, or restore prior bookkeeping on failure so the unchanged dirty revision is retried.

## Suggested regression tests
Using an injected file backend, fail one background autosave, restore writes, and advance multiple ticks without an edit. Verify the same revision is successfully persisted and recovery metadata identifies only a committed snapshot. Include the successful background case.

Use unique sibling temporary files created exclusively, keep ownership of the same handle through writing/syncing, and rename only that writer's file. Clean up only owned temporaries. Consider directory syncing where crash durability is promised.

title: IndexedDB persistence: request success is treated as transaction commit
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity: high. Confidence: high (source-confirmed mechanism).**
Read-only static audit of upstream `main` at [549e9d8](https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft/commit/549e9d825132986d6167c1432cd3328efcbb0278). No runtime reproduction, destructive testing, or exploit development was performed. Resource/failure outcomes below are source-derived, not measured.

## Source and root cause
- [apps/effectcraft-web/js/host.js:56-76](https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft/blob/549e9d825132986d6167c1432cd3328efcbb0278/apps/effectcraft-web/js/host.js#L56-L76)
- [apps/effectcraft-web/src/persist.rs:106-125](https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft/blob/549e9d825132986d6167c1432cd3328efcbb0278/apps/effectcraft-web/src/persist.rs#L106-L125)

The req helper resolves on IDBRequest.onsuccess. The IndexedDB backend awaits that helper for put/delete, discarding the transaction object instead of awaiting transaction.oncomplete and handling transaction.onabort. Request success can precede a later transaction abort; the Rust flush loop consequently sees success and does not retry that write.

## Conditions
An IndexedDB readwrite transaction aborts/fails after its individual put/delete request succeeds. This is a transaction-completion failure case, not the already-handled synchronous put exception.

## Impact
Flush may report success even though the change did not commit, and the failed entry is no longer queued for retry. Reload can restore stale project/config data. Physical device durability beyond the browser transaction guarantee is not asserted.

## Recommended remediation

## Assessment
**Severity: medium. Confidence: high (source-confirmed mechanism).**
Read-only static audit of upstream `main` at [549e9d8](https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft/commit/549e9d825132986d6167c1432cd3328efcbb0278). A lost response does not establish that the server did not execute the first request. Backend::exec sends mutations through this path.

The app commits a command but its connection closes/resets before the response arrives; a reconnect succeeds.

Return an explicit outcome-unknown error after ambiguous transmission/response failure unless the operation is known to be safe to retry. Alternatively use stable operation IDs with server-side deduplication; assigning a new ID on retry cannot provide this guarantee.

title: [3D Camera Tracker] Feature points gradually vanish and are not re-seeded over long takes
author: Interlastic
body:
**Description:**
When running the 3D Camera Tracker on continuous footage with camera translation (tested on game footage with static environment geometry and static lighting), the tracker initializes feature points normally. However, after several seconds of footage, existing tracking markers gradually drop off and vanish, leaving few to no points remaining—even though high-contrast static reference geometry remains clearly visible within the frame.

**Steps to Reproduce:**
1. Import a continuous 5–10 second video clip featuring continuous camera movement across static scenery (e.g., Rocket League stadium camera).
2. Apply the 3D Camera Tracker effect.
3. Observe point distribution at frame 0 vs. mid-clip.

**Expected Behavior:**
The tracker should continuously detect and re-seed new feature points as the camera moves, maintaining a stable pool of active tracks throughout the shot to support the bundle adjustment solver.

**Actual Behavior:**
Initial points track for a brief period, then progressively fail correlation or drift thresholds and are culled. Because new points are not spawned on subsequent frames, the total tracked point count decays to near zero, causing the solve to fail or degrade.

**Suspected Root Cause:**
- Feature detection appears to run only at initialization or across a rigid initial frame window rather than periodically re-triggering
- Strict reprojection/bidirectional error eviction without a fallback replacement buffer.

**Environment:**
- OS: Windows 11
- EffectCraft v0.9.2

title: Try to install a script to test (Like Duik)
author: MATTRAX64
body:
# EffectCraft: imported ScriptUI script fails to run

EffectCraft should be able to load and run compatible imported After Effects scripts. Duik Angela is used here to reproduce a problem in that scripting support.

**The request is to fix EffectCraft's script import/execution support, not to add Duik as a built-in feature.**

## What happens

The script file is present in EffectCraft's ScriptUI Panels folder and appears in the Window menu. However, selecting it fails before its panel opens:

```text
Duik Angela.jsx (line 85): TypeError: not a callable function
```

At line 85, the imported script calls:

```javascript
app.preferences.saveToDisk();
```

EffectCraft's CLI reports `typeof app.preferences.saveToDisk` as `undefined`. The script tries to call this missing API as a function, which causes the error.

This indicates a problem in the After Effects scripting API compatibility layer used to execute imported scripts. The file is found and execution starts, so this specific error does not show a failure to copy or discover the script.

## Requested fix

Check and implement the missing scripting API support so imported scripts can run through EffectCraft's normal script/panel loader. Start with `app.preferences.saveToDisk()`. The script also calls `app.preferences.reload()` and `app.preferences.getPrefAsLong(...)` immediately afterwards; these need checking too, but this test stops before reaching them.

Please use the original, unmodified script to test the fix. Fixing the first missing API may reveal additional compatibility issues.

## Reproduce

- EffectCraft 0.9.2 on Windows
- Duik Angela 17.1.21
- Place `Duik Angela.jsx` in EffectCraft's `Scripts\ScriptUI Panels` folder.
- Open EffectCraft and select **Window > Duik Angela.jsx**.
- Expected: the imported panel opens. Actual: execution fails at line 85.

See [the complete error report](EffectCraft-Duik-Angela-erreur-complete.md) for full output and CLI reproduction commands.

title: Right sidebar panels and the timeline layer list cannot be scrolled by touch
author: Kaedo17
body:
## What's wrong

On a touch device these cannot be scrolled at all:

- the right sidebar — **Effects & Presets**, **Properties**, **Preview**, **Align**, **Audio**
- the **timeline layer list**, once a comp has more layers than fit

Dragging a finger over them does nothing, so anything past the fold is unreachable.

## Cause

Three separate scroll paths, all of which read only a mouse wheel or trackpad and none of which handle a pointer drag.

**1. `PanelScroll::begin` — `crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs:449`**

```rust
if ui.rect_contains_pointer(area) {
    offset -= ui.input(|i| i.smooth_scroll_delta.y);
}
```

`smooth_scroll_delta` is wheel/trackpad input. There is no drag handling here at all, so on a device with neither wheel nor trackpad the offset never changes. This is the main one: `PanelScroll` is used by **nine panels** —

`effects_presets`, `properties`, `effect_controls`, `info`, `media_panels`, `misc`, `render_queue`, `text_panels`

**2. `scroll_bar` — `widgets.rs:403`, track built in `PanelScroll::end` (`widgets.rs:464`)**

```rust
let track = Rect::from_min_max(pos2(self.area.max.x - 6.0, …), pos2(self.area.max.x - 2.0, …));
```

The track is **4 px wide**, hit-expanded by 3 px per side in `scroll_bar` (`widgets.rs:414`) for a **10 px** target. It is draggable in code, but 10 px is far below any usable touch target, so in practice it is not a way in.

**3. Timeline layer list — `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/timeline.rs:1900`**

Same shape: `if ui.rect_contains_pointer(rows_rect)` then `smooth_scroll_delta`. The layer outline makes it worse — it scrolls only from `dx`, or from `dy` while Shift is held:

```rust
if over_outline && overflow > 0.0 && (dx.abs() > 0.0 || (shift && dy.abs() > 0.0)) { … }
```

Neither is available from a finger.

So: no wheel, no trackpad, a 10 px scrollbar — these lists cannot move.

title: Tests: three relink path-format failures on Windows (engine, host)

body:
## Summary

Three tests from the footage relink work (#1106) fail on Windows on unmodified `main` (549e9d82). Windows 11, Rust 1.99. They compare path strings, and on Windows the relink code writes the paths it derives with `/` while the test expectations are built with `PathBuf::join`, which mixes `\` and `/`. 1. `effectcraft-engine` lib, `commands::relink_moved::tests::relinking_one_file_finds_the_others_that_moved_with_it` (`crates/engine/src/commands/relink_moved.rs:309`)

   ```
2. `effectcraft-engine` lib, `footage_check::tests::footage_moved_with_its_project_is_found_on_open` (`crates/engine/src/footage_check.rs:272`)
   ```
   ["C:/Users/…/ec-footage-moved-…/Job/shots/a.png", "/Users/x/elsewhere/b.png"]

title: OBJ colours disappear when map_Kd uses an absolute path
author: nanox333
body:
## Simple explanation
The material file (`.mtl`) gives the texture as a full path from the PC it was exported on, like `C:\Users\<name>\...\Diffuse.png`. That path doesn't exist on my computer. For a full path like this, EffectCraft only checks that exact path. It doesn't look for an image with the same name next to the `.obj`, so it misses the image even when it's there, and it gives no warning. Putting the image next to the `.obj` doesn't help. The texture is dropped, and the model shows its plain grey colour.

Separately, when the texture does load, the grey colour (`Kd`) darkens it. The question below asks whether `Kd` should tint textures at all.

## Steps to reproduce
No third-party model is needed. Any PNG works as `checker.png`.

1. Make a folder with `quad.obj`, `quad.mtl` and `checker.png`.
2. Put this in `quad.obj`:
   ```
   mtllib quad.mtl
   v -1 -1 0
   v 1 -1 0
   v 1 1 0
   v -1 1 0
   vt 0 0
   vt 1 0
   vt 1 1
   vt 0 1
   usemtl Mat
   f 1/1 2/2 3/3
   f 1/1 3/3 4/4
   ```
3. Put this in `quad.mtl`:
   ```
   newmtl Mat
   Kd 0.64 0.64 0.64
   map_Kd C:\Users\<name>\Desktop\textures\checker.png
   ```
4. Import `quad.obj`.

**Expected:** the checker texture shows.
**Actual:** a flat grey quad, in the `Kd` colour.

## Cause
In `crates/model/src/obj.rs`:
- `map_Kd` is looked up as written. The media resolver (`crates/media/src/pool.rs`) joins the name to the model's folder with `Path::join`. An absolute path replaces the folder, so the lookup fails. On macOS and Linux, a Windows path with `\` fails too.
- A failed lookup is silent. A missing `mtllib` file is skipped without a message.
- When the texture does load, the renderer multiplies `Kd` by it, so `Kd 0.64` darkens the texture.

## Workaround
Put the texture's file name next to the `.obj`, and set `Kd` to white:
```
map_Kd Diffuse.png
Kd 1.000000 1.000000 1.000000
```
This works for me.

## Proposed fix
1. For `mtllib` and `map_*`, try the name as written. If that fails, try the file name in t…

title: bench: Reject malformed JSONL results instead of silently dropping benchmark evidence
author: sp80808
body:
**Title:** bench: Reject malformed JSONL results instead of silently dropping benchmark evidence

**Repository:** `storytold/effectcraft`

**Related:** #1245

### Problem
`xtask/src/bench.rs` uses `filter_map` when parsing benchmark JSONL results. Malformed nonempty lines are silently discarded.

Consequently, benchmark comparisons can continue with missing measurements without reporting that input data was corrupt.

### Proposed implementation
- Replace silent parsing with line-numbered errors identifying the affected input file.
- Permit blank lines but reject malformed JSON.
- Validate required benchmark fields before comparison.
- Ensure `--fail-over` cannot succeed using silently discarded results.
- Preserve normal comparison behaviour for valid results.

### Regression tests
- Truncated JSONL records
- Invalid JSON values
- Missing required measurement fields
- Valid multiline benchmark results
- Failed results following successful results

### Acceptance criteria
A corrupted results file produces an actionable diagnostic and cannot generate an apparently valid regression-gate result.

**Verification:** Source-reviewed; runtime testing still required.

title: Expression-driven property values should show in red (from #1072)
author: tylerjenningsw
body:
From the #1072 checklist: a property driven by an active expression should show its value in **red** in the Timeline, Effect Controls and Properties panel, as in After Effects. After Effects documents blue as the pre-expression value colour and red as the expression-driven one ([Expression basics](https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/desktop/work-with-expressions/expression-basics/expression-basics.html)).

Currently those values stay blue whether or not an expression drives them. The pieces exist already:
- `Property::has_expression()` is true for an enabled, non-empty expression.
- The theme has an expression colour, `Tokens::expr_text`, for dark and light themes.

The numeric fields just never use them.

Expected:
- With an enabled, non-empty expression, scalar, vector and angle values are red. That includes vector separators and both parts of an angle, and the value stays red while hovered or dragged.
- With the expression disabled, removed or empty, they're blue again.
- Names, stopwatches, keyframe navigation and colour swatches are unchanged.
- Red means "an expression drives this", not "it evaluated successfully". Expression errors keep their own reporting.

title: i18n: the layer and timeline context menus draw their labels in English
author: zitann2020
body:
The interface catalog translates the menu bar, the panels and — since #1199 — effect names, but
three context menus draw their labels without asking it. In a Japanese interface they stay English
while their own headings are translated.

All three are in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/timeline.rs`.

**`layer_menu` (3877-3945)** — shared by the Timeline's layer rows (called at 3873) and the
Composition panel's context menu (`panels/viewer.rs:1277`).

- `3886` translates the heading: `ui.menu_button(crate::i18n::tr("New"), …)`
- `3887-3893` do not: `item(ui, "Text", …)`, and `item` (3879-3885) is `ui.button(label)` on the literal
- `3895-3945` is the same story for the rest of the menu (`Layer Settings…`, `Duplicate`,
  `Split Layer`, `Delete`, `Transform`, `Masks`, `Markers`, …)

**The Timeline's empty-area menu (2952-2971)** — the same seven children, drawn with
`ui.button(label)` at 2963.

**`effects_submenu` (3948-3970)** — the layer context menu's Effects submenu: `3962` draws the
category with `ui.menu_button(cat, …)` and `3965` the effect with `item(ui, e.name, …)`. Its own
doc comment says it exists to stay in sync with the Effect menu's palette; the order is in sync, the
translation is not — the Effect menu goes through `i18n::effects::category` / `i18n::effects::name`.

## The catalog already has these rows

Each label is in the Japanese menu catalog, keyed by the command the same function already passes:

```
i18n.rs:1733  ("layer.newText", "Text", "テキスト"),
i18n.rs:1734  ("layer.newSolid", "Solid...", "平面..."),
```

The engine's own menu tree (`crates/engine/src/menus.rs:727-741`) lists the same seven entries and
*is* translated, which is why the menu bar's Layer ▸ New is Japanese and the context menu's is not.

## Three details a fix has to settle

1. **The ellipsis is a different character.** These menus write `Solid…`, `Light…`, `Camera…`,
   `Layer Settings…` with U+2026; the catalog keys use ASCII `...`. `tr()` cannot match until one
   side changes.
2. **T…

title: i18n: CJK text sits off the Latin baseline in a mixed line
author: zitann2020
body:
A fallback face is drawn at `A_face + 0.5·(H_row − H_face)` (epaint's `galley_from_rows`), so a CJK
face's own ascent and row height decide where its glyphs land — and they are nothing like Inter's.

**Measured** here, with `layout_no_wrap("Aあ")`:

| size | kana sits |
|---|---|
| 12 pt | 3.00 pt high |
| 15 pt | 4.00 pt high |
| 18 pt | 4.00 pt high |

An all-CJK line looks right; only a mixed one shows it. Every script the fallback covers has it —
Simplified and Traditional Chinese today, Korean when #599 lands — not only Japanese.

**Cause**: `crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs` registers each fallback's `FontData` with no `FontTweak`, and
no `FontTweak` is set anywhere in the repository.

**Fix**: #1395 gives each fallback the factor that cancels the offset,
`(A_row − A_face)/px − 0.5·(H_row − H_face)/px`, derived at runtime from the face's own metrics. It
also settles the Arabic, Indic, Thai and Hangul fallbacks, which share the loop.

Bundling a CJK face would remove the class for the interface, but a subset still leaves the fallback
for user text, and the web build has no CJK face at all — that is a larger, separate question.

`file.exportLottie` writes the **Offset Paths** miter limit (`ml`) as a plain number. 5. Play the JSON in lottie-web.

The rectangle renders, inset by 4 px.

Nothing renders. In a larger animation, a single layer with Offset Paths blanks every layer.

title: Gradient Ramp and Echo effects are not working properly on shapes and text
author: miftahanwar
body:
## Description
Two effects appear to be malfunctioning when applied to shapes or text: **Gradient Ramp** and **Echo**. Gradient Ramp can overflow outside the object's boundaries, while Echo changes the blending mode without producing the expected trail-like effect.

## Issue 1: Gradient Ramp — Gradient overflows outside shape boundaries

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Create a rectangle shape.
2. Go to **Effects → Gradient Ramp**.
3. Click Gradient Ramp to apply the effect to the shape.
4. Observe how the gradient is rendered.

### Expected Behavior
The gradient should remain within the boundaries of the selected shape, following its outline without overflowing.

### Actual Behavior
The gradient bleeds outside the shape's boundaries, creating visible areas beyond the rectangle's edges.

### Additional Notes
- The issue is particularly noticeable with 4-color gradients.
- The same behavior may also occur when applying the effect to text.

---

## Issue 2: Echo — Trail effect is not working properly

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Create a shape.
2. Go to the effects panel.
3. Click Echo to apply the effect to the shape.
4. Move the shape and observe the result.

### Expected Behavior
The shape should produce a trail-like effect as it moves, leaving behind visible echoes or copies of its previous positions.

### Actual Behavior
Instead of producing a trail-like effect, the shape only changes its blending mode. No visible trail or echo is generated.

## Additional Information
Both issues occur when applying effects to objects and may indicate problems with how these effects are rendered or applied.

Screenshots or screen recordings demonstrating each issue would help with debugging and verification.

author: Tuttifruttithings
body:
Three scripting compatibility gaps found while running an existing After Effects import script unchanged in EffectCraft 0.9.2 (Windows x64 portable, headless `effectcraft-cli script`). The first one is silent: the script runs without errors but writes values into the wrong parameters.

`effect.property("<effect match name>-NNNN")` resolves to a different parameter than in After Effects for some effects:

|---|---|---|

title: [CRITICAL] Imported Media is trimmed to the length of the timeline
author: ifindvulnerabilities
body:
Hey everyone, I wanted to quickly write an issue for something I encountered while trying to create a .GIF for my new project.

# Overview
When a user adds media to the timeline regardless of the length of the media imported, it will trim the media to the length of the timeline.

For example: if you import a video that is 1 minute and 30 seconds long into a composition that is only 12 seconds long, it will trim the media to the timeline being 12 seconds without the ability to scrub the media backwards.

This makes it impossible to import larger videos without making the timeline (or the composition length) the same length of the largest duration of media you import.

# The only work around
To mitigate this issue, users are forced to increase their composition length (timeline) to the desired duration and adjustthe "work area" to reflect their desired duration.

This breaks numerous peoples workflows and is a major flaw with the application.

title: Add Marker has no shortcut on keyboards without a numpad
author: nanox333
body:
## Summary
Add Marker is bound only to the numpad `*` (`comp.addMarker`, shortcut `Num*`). On a laptop or any keyboard without a numpad there is no key to press, including while playback is running.

## What the code does (read from `main`, not reproduced in the app)
- `crates/engine/src/commands/comp.rs`: `comp.addMarker` has the shortcut `Num*`. `layer.addMarker` (Layer ▸ Markers ▸ Add Marker) has no shortcut.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs` (around the `Num*` handling): egui has no key for the numpad `*`, so the handler listens for a typed `*` text event. That means Shift+8 works only on layouts where it types `*`. With layers selected it marks them, otherwise it adds a composition marker (#976).
- The handler is skipped only while a dialog is open. Playback state doesn't block it, and the marker goes at the session time, which playback updates. So adding a marker during playback should work wherever `*` can be typed; I have not confirmed that in the running app.
- The shortcut editor special-cases `Num*` (`crates/engine/src/shortcuts.rs`), so it may not be rebindable like other shortcuts. Not verified.

## Suggested fix
- Add a second default binding on the main keyboard for Add Marker, and make it work while playback runs.
- Make sure `Num*` and the new binding can both be rebound in the shortcut editor.
- Give Layer ▸ Markers ▸ Add Marker the same shortcut display.
- Test: add a marker while playback is running and check it lands on the frame shown.

Related: #409 (numpad `*` did nothing, closed), #976.

title: [Bug] WAV markers not displayed on audio layer
author: nanox333
body:
## Report
Markers embedded in a WAV file are not shown on the audio layer in EffectCraft's timeline. The same file imported into After Effects shows all its markers on the layer, with their names (for example `SEQ01_Prologue`, `SEQ02_Vallee_P1_Agriculture`, `SEQ02_Vallee_P2_Thermes`).

### Steps to reproduce
1. Take a WAV file containing named markers (created in Audition, Premiere or another tool).
2. Import it into EffectCraft and add it to a composition.
3. Look at the audio layer in the timeline: no markers.
4. Import the same WAV into After Effects: the markers are visible.

### Expected
Markers from the WAV appear on the audio layer, with their names, as in After Effects.

### Actual
The audio layer shows no markers.

### Environment
EffectCraft 0.9.2, Windows 11. The reporter did not try a WAV with non-XMP markers. (Reporter's screenshots, EffectCraft versus After Effects, are not attached here.)

## What the code does (read from `main`; not run against a marker WAV)
- Nothing reads WAV markers. There is no handling of the RIFF `cue ` chunk, `LIST/adtl/labl`/`ltxt` chunks, or Adobe's XMP packet (`_PMX` chunk) anywhere in the workspace.
- Audio decoding goes through FilmCraft's crates behind `crates/media`; whether they expose marker metadata is not checked.
- The only "markers from source" feature is Layer ▸ Markers ▸ Update Markers From Source, which copies a precomp's composition markers onto its layer. It does nothing for audio or footage.

## Suggested fix
- Read WAV markers when audio is imported: the standard `cue ` + `adtl/labl` chunks first, then Adobe's XMP markers.
- Put them on the audio layer as layer markers with their names, and let Update Markers From Source refresh them.
- Parse defensively (truncated or malformed chunks, huge marker counts), per the never-crash rule.
- Tests with small generated WAV files, one per marker format.

title: Feature: Report bugs from inside the app, with logs and system details
author: nanox333
body:
**Problem**
Bug reports often arrive without what a maintainer needs first: app version, OS and GPU, the log, and the steps that led to the problem. Reporters have to find the log, guess which files to attach and type their system details by hand. Many reports never include them, and some reporters have no GitHub account.

The app already has most of the pieces, but they are separate: **Help ▸ System Compatibility Report** (OS, CPU, memory, GPU adapter), **Help ▸ Reveal Logging File**, and the log folder itself. Nothing puts them into one report, and nothing lets the user send one from the app.

**Idea**
Add **Help ▸ Report a Bug…**, with a button in the About dialog too. The dialog gathers the report and shows all of it for review. The user then clicks **Send**, and the app files the issue directly.

- **Environment:** the data from the System Compatibility Report, reused rather than duplicated.
- **Log:** the current session log and the logs of the two runs before it, so a crash from the last launch is included.
- **Steps (optional):** the last few commands the user ran, by command id, if the engine keeps that history.
- **Project (optional, off by default):** composition and layer names and counts. No media and no property values.
- **Contact (optional):** an email or Discord name, so maintainers can reply to someone without a GitHub account. It stays out of the public issue text.
- **Description:** what the user did and what they expected.

Every item has a checkbox. The review shows the exact text that will be posted.

**How it is sent**
Two routes, for maintainers to choose between:
- **Project relay:** the app posts to the Ticket Relay that already files Discord reports as issues ([storytold/effectcraft#1064](https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft/issues/1064)). No account is needed, and the relay could keep the full log and the contact details.
- **GitHub sign-in:** the user signs in to GitHub once, and the issue is filed under their account. No server is …

title: Render Queue: a failed render exits 0 under `run`/`exec` and leaves a 52-byte stub (replacing any earlier output)
author: Tokarzewski
body:
**Version**: EffectCraft 0.9.2, `effectcraft-cli`, headless, Windows 11 x64. Exit-code behaviour checked at runtime; source read at `main` 549e9d8.

## Steps

Make a one-second 22.05 kHz mono WAV and render it to H.264/AAC at that sample rate (any failing encode behaves the same; this one is easy to trigger):

```sh
python -c "
import struct, wave, math
w = wave.open('tone22k.wav','wb'); w.setnchannels(1); w.setsampwidth(2); w.setframerate(22050)
w.writeframes(b''.join(struct.pack('<h', int(8000*math.sin(2*math.pi*440*i/22050))) for i in range(22050))); w.close()"

# use absolute paths for the input and the output
effectcraft-cli --empty run \
  file.import '{"paths":["/abs/tone22k.wav"]}' \
  comp.new '{"name":"Main","width":160,"height":90,"frameRate":25,"duration":1}' \
  layer.newSolid '{"name":"BG","color":"#142850"}' \
  layer.addItem '{"item":1}' \
  renderQueue.add '{"comp":"Main","format":"h264","output":"/abs/out.mp4","sampleRate":22050,"audioChannels":"mono"}' \
  renderQueue.render '{"wait":true}'
echo "exit=$?"
```

Control: the same command with `"sampleRate":48000` renders a normal 23 kB `out.mp4`.

To see the overwrite effect, run the 48000 version first, then the 22050 version to the same `out.mp4`.

## Observed

- The process exits **0**. The only sign of failure is inside the JSON result: `"status": {"Failed": "encode: invalid configuration: bitrate out of range for the channel count and sample rate"}`, `"statusLabel": "Failed"`, `"last_output": null`.

`item.metadata` for the one-frame 30 fps file: `"frames": 0`, `"duration": 0.033`, `"frameRate": 30.0`.

title: Import: MP4s with millisecond frame times read as 30.303 / 58.824 fps, so New Comp from Selection and renders run at the wrong rate and skip frames
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
**Version / OS:** EffectCraft 0.9.2 windows-x64 portable, Windows 11, RTX 3060 12 GB (CLI, CPU renders). `main` at 549e9d8 still pins `filmcraft-media` at 2c5ba7a.

### Summary

Many phone and messaging-app MP4s store frame times rounded to whole milliseconds (frame durations of 33/34 ms at 30 fps, 16/17 ms at 60 fps). EffectCraft interprets such footage as **30.303 fps** (30303/1000) and **58.824 fps** (7353/125) instead of 30 and 60. *New Comp from Selection* creates a comp at that rate, and renders are written at that rate. The frame rate comes from the FilmCraft probe (`rate_from_fc(v.frame_rate)` in `crates/media/src/probe.rs`), so this is the same root cause as storytold/filmcraft#1700. Two open PRs there, storytold/filmcraft#1729 and storytold/filmcraft#1829, fix it for that issue's fixtures and ten extra clips (comparison in storytold/filmcraft#1700). Once one of them is merged, bumping EffectCraft's pinned FilmCraft crates (`filmcraft-codecs`, `filmcraft-media` … at 2c5ba7a in `Cargo.toml`) should fix this here too.

It is common with real footage. Of 27 phone and camera clips I tested, 6 have an `ffprobe` `r_frame_rate` of 30, 29.97 or 59.94, but EffectCraft read them as 30.303, 30.01, 30.02 or 59.484 fps. A 3 s render of a 59.94 fps 4K HEVC phone clip had 179 frames at 14871/250 fps. The fixtures below are synthetic.

title: i18n: the web build draws CJK as tofu - the catalogs ship but no CJK face does
author: FeiLiuEM
body:
The interface catalogs are offered on every platform, so the web build can be put into Japanese, Simplified or Traditional Chinese — but it bundles no CJK face, and no system fonts exist there to fall back to.

What the code does today:

- `install_script_fallbacks` returns an empty list on wasm (`crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs:389-393`: "The web build has no system fonts and installs nothing"), so no CJK family is registered.
- The bundled faces are Inter (three weights), JetBrains Mono and Noto Serif — a Latin Noto Serif at 482 KB, which is why nothing covers Han, kana or Hangul.
- So a Japanese interface in the browser draws its own labels, layer names and file names as tofu, rather than as text that is slightly off (which is what #1309 is about: there the OS supplies a face and only the baseline is off).

This is the same shape #599 was for Hangul on macOS, and the fix is a decision about shipping a face — the size question in #1309's option 2 — not about metrics. For whoever picks it up:

- A full Noto Sans JP is several MB per weight and the web build carries the same weight; subsetting to the interface's own strings brings the download down, at the price of user text (layer names, file names) still being tofu.
- The pieces already exist for a bundled face: `assets/fonts/NotoSerif-Regular.ttf` is bundled, Noto Sans JP is SIL OFL 1.1 (allowed by `AGENTS.md` §1), and the pattern to copy is the font file plus `OFL-NotoSansJP.txt`, a `.attribution` sidecar, a row in `ATTRIBUTION.md`, a line in `NOTICE`, and the registration in `crates/text/src/fonts.rs` and `theme.rs`.
- A smaller variant would be to load the face only when a CJK interface is chosen, so the default download does not carry it.

I am not proposing which of those to take — the size trade-off is yours (and it is the same decision #1309 deferred here rather than settling inside itself).

Reported by @zitann2020, who also worked out the details above while looking at #1309.
