title: i18n: choosing Deutsch, Русский or Français leaves every menu in English (entry() returns before the catalogue lookup)
author: Hamza0101
body:
## Summary

Settings ▸ General ▸ Language offers **Deutsch**, **Русский** and **Français**, and all three have a complete catalogue that the test suite keeps in sync with the others. Selecting any of them leaves every menu in English.

`i18n::entry` is the problem. It opens by picking the undo/redo wording for the active language:

```rust
let (undo, no_undo, redo, no_redo) = match language(app) {
    "ja" => (…),
    "zh-hans" => (…),
    "zh-hant" => (…),
    "uk" => (…),
    "es" => (…),
    "pt-br" => (…),
    "cs" => (…),
    _ => return shown,
};
```

`de`, `ru` and `fr` fall to `_ => return shown`, which returns the English label and never reaches the catalogue lookup lower down in the same function:

```rust
_ if shown == e.label => label(app, &e.command, &e.label).into(),
```

That lookup is the only thing that consults `GERMAN` / `RUSSIAN` / `FRENCH` for a menu entry, and `menus::entry_label` — which produces the drawn label for every menu entry — ends in `crate::i18n::entry(app, e, shown)`. So for those three languages the menus are English throughout.

`i18n::label` itself is fine: it has a `"de" => lookup(GERMAN, …)` arm and returns the right string. Only the `entry` path, which is what the menus use, misses them.

## Version

`main` @ 05955c0.

## How I ran into it

Writing a German test for #1443. The same call through the two functions disagrees:

```
label(&app, "file.revealInFinder", "Reveal in Finder")  ->  "Im Finder anzeigen"
entry(&app, &e,                    "Reveal in Finder")  ->  "Reveal in Finder"
```

With the language preference set to `de` in both cases.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Settings ▸ General ▸ Language ▸ **Deutsch**.
2. Open any menu.

Every entry is in English. The same for **Русский** and **Français**.

## What suggests it is an oversight rather than staging

Three things point at the catalogues being meant to work:

- `prefs::LANGUAGES` lists all three, and `ukrainian_catalog_matches_the_settings_registry` asserts that list's…

title: i18n: 'Reveal in Explorer' / 'Reveal in File Manager' stay English in 5 live languages (only uk and cs are special-cased)
author: Hamza0101
body:
## Summary

*Reveal in Finder* is labelled by the platform's file manager: the engine substitutes the name before the catalogue sees the label, so the source string is `Reveal in Finder` on macOS, `Reveal in Explorer` on Windows and `Reveal in File Manager` on Linux.

The catalogues only hold the macOS wording, so the other two are handled by special cases at the top of `i18n::label` — and only **Ukrainian** and **Czech** have one:

```rust
if language == "uk" && matches!(command, "file.revealInFinder" | "layer.revealInFinder") { … }
if language == "cs" && matches!(command, "file.revealInFinder" | "layer.revealInFinder") { … }
```

Every other language falls through to the catalogue, which has no entry whose English is `Reveal in Explorer`, so the label stays English on Windows and Linux while the rest of the menu is translated.

Affected and **live**: `ja`, `zh-hans`, `zh-hant`, `es`, `pt-br`. (`de`, `ru` and `fr` are affected too, but their menus are English anyway — #1449. German's two variants are added in #1454, which is where I noticed this.)

## Version

`main` @ 05955c0.

## Steps to reproduce

On Windows or Linux:

1. Settings ▸ General ▸ Language ▸ 日本語 (or 简体中文, 繁體中文, Español, Português).
2. File ▸ *Reveal in Explorer*, or right-click a layer ▸ *Reveal in Explorer*.

The entry reads `Reveal in Explorer` in English. On macOS the same entry is translated, because `Reveal in Finder` is in the catalogue.

## Note on the shape of the fix

Rather than five more copies of the same `if language == …` block, it may be worth turning the two existing ones into one table keyed by language, or giving the catalogues real entries for the two extra sources so the normal lookup handles them. Either way it is a small change, but it needs the right wording for each language's file manager (Explorer's own localised name, and whatever each language calls a file manager), which I am not able to check for any of the five. Happy to do the mechanical part if a native speaker suppl…

title: i18n: the toolbar's tool names are the last English surface, and the catalogs cannot take them alone
author: zitann2020
body:
The 31 tool names are the last thing that stays English in a translated interface. They live in
`Tool::label()` (`crates/ui-egui/src/state.rs:100-134`) and reach the screen in two places — the
tooltip (`crates/ui-egui/src/header.rs:69`) and the flyout rows (`:106`) — and neither asks the
catalog. Everything around them is translated: the panel titles, the workspace names, the shape
tool's own presets.

## Why they cannot simply be added

The panel catalog is keyed by the English source, and
`catalogs_are_unique_and_keep_the_english_shape` (`crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/ui.rs:4513-4532`) requires
every Japanese key to exist in the Simplified Chinese catalog first:

```rust
let extra: Vec<&str> = cat.iter().map(|(en, _)| *en).filter(|en| !hans.contains(en)).collect();
assert!(extra.is_empty(), "the {name} catalog lists source strings the Chinese ones don't");
```

So 31 rows have to land in `SIMPLIFIED_CHINESE` and in `TRADITIONAL_CHINESE` (the same 31, in the same
order — `assert_eq!(hans, hant)`) before `JAPANESE` can have them. That is the shape #1178 already
had: the Chinese Settings rows landed first (26b24518), the Japanese ones after (#1448).

`every_row_is_used_by_a_converted_panel` (`ui.rs:4616-4626`) also wants each English source to appear
in a file listed in `CONVERTED`, and the tool names appear only in `state.rs`, which is not listed yet.
The comment at `ui.rs:4611-4615` describes exactly this case, and `prefs.rs` is the precedent for it.

## What I think the change is

1. `CONVERTED` gains `("state.rs", include_str!("../state.rs"))`.
2. 31 rows in `SIMPLIFIED_CHINESE`, the same 31 in the same order in `TRADITIONAL_CHINESE`, 31 in
   `JAPANESE`.
3. `header.rs:69` and `:106` ask the catalog. `:67` and `:107` — the automation labels — and
   `state.rs:190` (`from_name`, which `ui.set {"tool": …}` and the `tool.*` dispatch go through) stay
   English, or the control channel breaks.

title: `effectcraft-cli render` drops the selected segmentation model and invalidates frozen Object Matte
author: prajwal-395
body:
On EffectCraft 0.9.2 at `549e9d825132986d6167c1432cd3328efcbb0278`, select MobileSAM and freeze an Object Matte in one headless CLI session, save the project, then render it with a second `effectcraft-cli render --project ...` process. The first process reports MobileSAM active, 12/12 Object Matte frames computed, and `frozen:true`. In the fresh render process, `roto.models` reports Classical selected/active and MobileSAM installed but inactive. `objectMatte.status` still reports frozen, while the model-keyed computed list is empty. The export silently recomputes with Classical and returns only the seed (30 alpha pixels on frame 0, zero on frames 1-11).

Expected: the CLI render should use the segmentation model that produced the frozen cache, or clearly refuse/report that the frozen model is unavailable instead of silently rendering a different matte. Actual: a fresh CLI render starts Classical-only, fails the model-specific frozen-key comparison, and falls back to Classical segmentation.

Repro sample: a 960x540, 12-frame PNG sequence at 2 fps; point `[488.736,308.772]`, box `[352.512,97.524,629.952,422.496]`, reference frame 0, track on, reach 0-11. With `roto.model.select`, Object Matte freeze, and `renderQueue.add` / `renderQueue.render` in one session, the same input produces 43.5k alpha pixels per frame and mean IoU 0.9545 against a SAM 2.1 reference track. The separate `effectcraft-cli render` path produces `[30,0,...,0]`.

Relevant source: `apps/effectcraft-cli/src/main.rs:342-361,655-668` (fresh session and render path); `crates/engine/src/models.rs:313-327` (session-local model selection); `crates/engine/src/roto.rs:436-454` (model used to freeze); `crates/effects/src/object_matte.rs:255-267,275-285,402-408` (model-specific frozen key and recomputation after mismatch). A useful fix is to let headless render select/load a model or restore the model setting before opening/rendering a project, and report a frozen-key/model mismatch rather than presenting the…

title: Bug: RAM preview cache is invalidated after an unrelated edit
author: earlvanze
body:
A community report says EffectCraft clears/rebuilds previously cached frames after any change, including changes that should not affect those frames.

The current parity documentation states that an edit drops every composition RAM preview, while disk cache uses content keys. Please reproduce with an .ecproj and identify whether the invalidation is expected RAM-cache behavior, a disk-cache miss, or a regression.

Requested repro details: EffectCraft version, OS/GPU, project, cached range, the exact unrelated edit, and whether the disk-cache setting is enabled.

No matching open issue was found after searching cache invalidation/re-cache terms.

title: UX Request: Transform Layer Style dialog into a fully fluid, native floating window
author: Omar7-ctrl
body: Follow-up to #1155 / #1166 UI/UX Feedback: Crucial Adjustments Needed for the Layer Style Window Thank you to the developers for the swift action in merging the draggable implementation! To make it fully functional and responsive for professional workflows, there are 4 critical UI/UX constraints that need to be addressed in the layout: 1. Titlebar Click Bounds Issue (Top Bar vs. Text): Currently, only the label row text area allows dragging (marked green in the test layout). The actual topmost window titlebar background region (marked red) does not respond to mouse gestures at all. The entire top bar header bound should be hit-testable for smooth dragging. 2. The Modal Background Dimming: The background remains heavily dimmed when the dialog opens. This color shifting defeats the purpose of dragging the window away, as it completely skews lighting, color grading, and asset preview visibility on the main composite viewer. 3. Screen Boundary Clamping: The window is tightly locked within the inner viewport dimensions. It prevents the user from sliding the dialog partially off-screen or out of the active composition view to maximize canvas visibility. 4. Fixed Window Dimensions: The dialog handles are rigid and cannot be manually resized (stretched or shrunken) to dynamically adapt to different screen monitors. For a fluid workflow, could we wire the entire top bar header for dragging, remove the dark background dimming overlay, allow boundaries to overflow partially off-screen, and enable native corner/edge resizing? This would fully perfect the tool! https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/80360f11-f2de-48af-93c1-f1146916423f

title: [Feature Request] Diagram / Flowchart Node Canvas Module ("Visio-like" visual graph editor)
author: barrile
body:
### Summary
Add a diagramming / visual canvas module (similar in concept to M.Visio or a node-based flowchart editor) for planning compositions, visual flowcharts, and procedural routing.

### Problem / Motivation
While EffectCraft focuses on timeline- and layer-based motion graphics/compositing, complex project setups benefit from high-level visual structure planning, dependency mapping, and diagrammatic workflows directly inside the application workspace.

### Proposed Solution
Introduce a dedicated diagramming/node canvas panel:
- **Canvas Panel:** A new UI panel located under `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/` that allows placing shapes/nodes, dragging connectors, and labeling blocks.
- **Engine-Driven Commands:** All operations (e.g., `AddDiagramNode`, `ConnectNodes`, `DeleteNode`, `SetNodeProperties`) implemented as commands registered via `cmd!` in `crates/engine/src/commands/` with full undo/redo support and menu entries in `crates/engine/src/menus.rs`.
- **MCP / CLI Integration:** Because actions are registered engine commands, external agents and CLI tools can programmatically inspect or generate diagrams.

### Compliance & Ground Rules
- **Layering:** Diagram data structures and logic remain strictly within the engine layer, with the UI layer (`ui-egui`) remaining a consumer.
- **Reliability:** Built strictly without panicking constructs (`unwrap`, `expect`, `panic!`, `todo!`, `unsafe`).

### Additional Context / References
Similar to node-graph canvas layouts found in modern creative suites, adapted to EffectCraft's headless-first and command-driven architecture.

I'm using EffectCraft on Fedora Linux with an AMD Radeon RX 550 GPU, and I've experienced system-wide crashes during video export, apparently related to GPU memory usage.

title: Roto Brush: a SAM 2.1 video tracker (Hiera-Tiny, in Rust on candle)
author: nanox333
body:
## Idea
Add Meta's **SAM 2.1** as an optional Roto Brush tracker, starting with **Hiera-Tiny (38.9M parameters)**, ported to Rust.

## Why
Roto Brush feedback (storytold/effectcraft#1499, storytold/effectcraft#1500) describes a crude outline and trouble with movement, colour changes, and things entering or leaving the frame. Today propagation warps the previous matte by optical flow and re-cuts a band around it, and a trained model (MobileSAM) is called on each frame without any memory of earlier frames. SAM 2 has a streaming memory built for video: it tracks an object across frames, handles occlusion, and re-acquires it when it returns.

## Approach
Port Hugging Face `transformers`' `Sam2Model` / `Sam2VideoModel` (Apache-2.0) to Rust on candle, the way `storytold/lightcraft` ported SAM 3:
- A new native-only crate (not built for wasm32), `forbid(unsafe_code)`, vendored with a NOTICE and per-file attribution.
- Reference tests against PyTorch fixtures, one per stage (Hiera encoder, neck, prompt encoder, decoder, memory encoder, memory attention), so a mismatch points at one module.
- An optional download that is SHA-256 verified and never bundled. Meta's README states the SAM 2 code and checkpoints are Apache-2.0, so it fits the registry's licence rule.
- Roto Brush integration: strokes become point prompts, tracking runs in both directions from any prompted frame, a correction stroke becomes a new prompted frame, and each frame gets a confidence value shown on the timeline.
- The existing graph-cut and matting stages stay, for edge refinement and as the fallback. With no model installed, nothing changes.
- A `bench --roto` harness (synthetic composites with known alpha) to measure it against the current path and MobileSAM, so the improvement is measured and not assumed.

## Status
I'm looking into this and plan to work on it. Nothing is built yet; I'm starting with the reference setup and the benchmark.

title: Support coordinated network rendering across multiple machines
author: earlvanze
body:
A user asks whether EffectCraft supports network rendering: https://discord.com/channels/1359579021108842617/1557582920321867876/1560098525902143500

Current source provides File > Watch Folder for queued .ecproj projects, but its status-file check and subsequent write do not establish atomic job ownership across machines. No distributed frame scheduler or documented multi-machine coordination was found in the canonical source, gaps, roadmap, or hardware parity documentation.

Please track coordinated network rendering: define whether jobs or frame ranges are distributed, prevent duplicate work/output collisions through atomic claims, handle failed workers, and document shared media/output requirements. Existing Watch Folder support should not be presented as verified distributed rendering until that behavior is implemented and tested.

Scope: feature request and documentation of current limits; no performance or release-date promise.

title: Feature Request: Support Adobe .MOGRT Templates (Lower Thirds, Titles & Motion Graphics)
author: Playwick
body:
Hi EffectCraft team!

First off, absolutely loving what you're building. EffectCraft has been a game changer for those of us working on older macOS versions who can't run newer versions of After Effects.

I'd love to suggest adding support for importing Adobe Motion Graphics Templates (`.mogrt` files).

There are thousands of free, beautifully designed `.mogrt` templates available online, especially lower thirds, animated titles, captions, and transitions. Being able to use them directly in EffectCraft would open up an enormous library of creative resources.

**Suggested functionality:**
- Import `.mogrt` files directly into EffectCraft.
- Extract and display editable text, colours, fonts, and other supported properties.
- Preserve animations and timing wherever technically possible.
- Allow users to customize imported graphics within the existing EffectCraft interface.
- Support templates originally created in Premiere Pro or After Effects, where compatible.
- Provide clear compatibility warnings for unsupported effects or expressions.

**Why this would be valuable:**

Many creators use older Macs or prefer lightweight, independent creative software. Native `.mogrt` support would make EffectCraft an even more compelling alternative for motion graphics work, without requiring an Adobe subscription.

I understand that `.mogrt` files can contain complex After Effects compositions, so full compatibility might not be feasible initially. Even partial support for simpler text-based lower thirds and animated titles would be incredibly useful.

Thanks for all the work you're putting into this project. Excited to see where EffectCraft goes next!

title: Audio: AAC in Matroska crackles in renders: each decoded frame is placed at its millisecond timestamp
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
**Version / OS:** EffectCraft 0.10.0 windows-x64 portable, Windows 11 25H2, AMD Radeon Graphics (Dx12); `effectcraft-cli`, headless (CPU renders). `Cargo.toml` at `v0.10.0` pins the FilmCraft codec crates at `2c5ba7a` (#1187).

### What happens

AAC audio in a Matroska (`.mkv`) file crackles in renders. An AAC frame decodes to 1024 samples (21.33 ms at 48 kHz), but Matroska stores block timestamps in whole milliseconds, and each decoded frame is written at its own rounded timestamp: in the fixture at 0, 1008, 2016, 3072, 4080 … samples (0, 21, 42, 64, 85 ms) instead of 0, 1024, 2048, 3072, 4096 …. Two frames in three start 16 or 32 samples early and overwrite the end of the previous frame; the third leaves 32 samples of silence before it. The same AAC stream in MP4 renders sample-exact.

Rendered WAV of the first 6 s, compared with ffmpeg's decode of the same file:

| Fixture | Container | Correlation | SNR | AAC frames out of place |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `ec_aac_tone440.mp4` (control) | MP4 | 1.0000 | 84.6 dB | 0 of 275 |
| `ec_aac_tone440.mkv` (same stream) | Matroska | 0.44 | -0.5 dB | 183 of 275 (by 16 or 32 samples) |

On real files: in a run over 92 real-world videos, all 5 Matroska files with AAC audio (stereo and 5.1) fail an audio comparison that all 66 measured MP4/MOV files with AAC pass: the rendered second correlates only 0.04 to 0.73 with ffmpeg's decode (80 Hz to 4 kHz band; MP4/MOV with AAC: 0.97 or more). title: [Audit] 5 defects with evidence and fix PRs: SMask bit-depth shift, inline-image length overflow, unclamped output size, hostile ROI crop overflow, Type 1 RD length overflow
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Round-4 audit: 5 defects on current `main`, each with an independent fix PR whose regression test fails on `main` and passes on the branch. (Distinct from issue #1446's PDF *font importer* defects: findings 1, 2 and 5 below are in `image.rs` and `type1.rs`.)

### 1. PDF soft-mask `1u32 << bpc` shift-overflow on attacker-controlled `/BitsPerComponent` — crash
`mask_image` reads `/BitsPerComponent` from the `/SMask` dict with no validation (`crates/pdf/src/image.rs:184`); the main image path checks `1|2|4|8|16` before its identical shift, the mask path doesn't. `/BitsPerComponent 32` panics in debug/test/fuzz builds and wraps in release, mistranslating alpha.
**Fix:** #1565

### 2. PDF inline-image byte-length arithmetic overflows on huge `/W`//`H` — crash + misparse
`inline_len` computes `(w * n * bpc).div_ceil(8) * h` with no size validation (`crates/pdf/src/image.rs:85`), unlike `decode`/`mask_image`. A huge `/W` overflows in debug builds; in release it wraps and the caller slices the wrong bytes, misparsing the image and shifting the `EI` resync.
**Fix:** #1566

### 3. `RenderSettings::output_size` unclamped: a 30 000 px comp at 4× requests 120 000 px frames — crash/robustness
`output_size` (`crates/project/src/render_queue.rs:445`) multiplies the repaired `MAX_SIZE` (30 000) comp by resolution 4.0 without a ceiling; the exporters' `w * h * 4` overflows `u32` (debug panic, release wrap + slice panic) after asking for a ~57 GB frame. The resize path in the same file already clamps to 30 000.
**Fix:** #1568

### 4. ROI-crop path does unchecked `f64 → i32` conversion and `i32` subtraction — crash (debug)
The `roi` quad is stored raw from the control channel (`crates/engine/src/commands/render_queue.rs:271`, unlike every sibling field, which is clamped) and never repaired on load. `Crop::edges` (`crates/project/src/render_queue.rs:765`) converts with `as i32` and subtracts raw: `x = -1e12` saturates to `i32::MIN` and `w as i32 - l` overflows.
**Fix:** #1569

### 5. Ty…

title: Web build in a sandboxed iframe: startup hangs when reading `navigator.serviceWorker` throws (opaque origin)
author: romanpert
body:
## Environment

- `effectcraft-web-0.10.0.zip` (sha256 `b922abed…46a8`), served from `http://localhost`. The same code is on `main` at `0311bdc3`.
- Chromium 140.0.7339.16 (Playwright, headless).
- Embedded as `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts" src=".../index.html">`, so the document's origin is opaque.

## Controlled reproduction

Load `index.html` with no query in the sandboxed iframe. It stays on "Loading EffectCraft…", with an uncaught `SecurityError: Failed to read the 'serviceWorker' property from 'Navigator': Service worker is disabled because the context is sandboxed and lacks the 'allow-same-origin' flag.` `effectcraftLoad` stays `{}`. With `?nosw` this step is skipped.

## Relevant code

`apps/effectcraft-web/web/index.html:86-88`: `"serviceWorker" in navigator` is true in an opaque origin, and the `navigator.serviceWorker` read on line 87 throws synchronously (Chromium) before the `try` on line 89, so neither `.catch` nor the status/`effectcraftLoad.error` handler runs.

## Expected

Skip the service worker when reading it throws (as `?nosw` does), or at least report the failure in the status and in `effectcraftLoad.error` (AGENTS.md › Never crash). `HOSTING.md` asks for `allow-same-origin` and says that without it "there's no storage"; without it, the app doesn't start, and nothing says why.

Split as asked: `info()` is #1585, the `new Worker()` hang is #1586.

title: Web build in a sandboxed iframe: startup hangs when `new Worker()` throws (opaque origin)
author: romanpert
body:
## Environment

- `effectcraft-web-0.10.0.zip` (sha256 `b922abed…46a8`), served from `http://localhost`. The same code is on `main` at `0311bdc3`.
- Chromium 140.0.7339.16 (Playwright, headless).
- Embedded as `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts" src=".../index.html">`, so the document's origin is opaque.

## Controlled reproduction

| `src` query | Result |
|---|---|
| `?nosw` | wasm loads (`wasmMs` is set), then an uncaught `SecurityError: Failed to construct 'Worker': Script at '…/worker.js' cannot be accessed from origin 'null'.` It stays on "Loading…", with no `readyMs` and no `effectcraftLoad.error`. |
| `?nosw&noworkers` | Starts (`readyMs` ≈ 330 ms). Storage falls back to memory. |

## Relevant code

`apps/effectcraft-web/js/host.js:383` (and `:297`): `new Worker(new URL("worker.js", base), { type: "module" })` throws synchronously when the page's origin is opaque. Frame workers start during startup (`src/app.rs:256-258` → `src/frames.rs`), so startup stops there. A worker that fails asynchronously is already handled (`src/frames.rs:210`: frames fall back to the page's thread); a constructor that throws is not.

## Expected

Treat a worker that can't be constructed like one that failed, so the app starts as it does with `?noworkers`.

Split from #1582.

title: Web on Chrome/Windows: creating the 224 kernel pipelines keeps the GPU process busy past Chrome's watchdog, so the device is lost ~60 s after every load
author: romanpert

- Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300, AMD Radeon RX 5700 XT, Chrome 155.0.8059.40 (headed, regular tab, no iframe).

## Controlled reproduction

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `index.html`, ×2 | The page doesn't respond until ~60 s, then: `lib.rs:719: GPU preview retired: GPU device lost (Unknown): A valid external Instance reference no longer exists.` → `lib.rs:743: graphics device lost: closing the window` → "The graphics device was lost". title: Web editor: scripts can't open files in browser storage; stored footage is reported missing
author: rahal
body:
In the browser editor (built from `main`, 0.10.0) a file you drop on the page, or import, lands in browser storage. The editor can read it, but:

1. **A `.jsx` script can't open it**, even when it sits next to the saved project: `File.open("r")` returns `false` with `File not found`, and `File.exists` is `false`.
2. **`footage.check` marks imported media as missing.** The check runs after File ▸ Open.

Desktop and CLI are not affected.

### Steps (browser console)
`effectcraft.addFile` does what dropping a file on the page does: it stores the file in browser storage and imports it.

```js
const p = await effectcraft.addFile(new File(["hello"], "data.txt"));   // stored as "/data.txt"
await effectcraft.saveToBrowser("/repro.ecproj");                        // the file is in the project's folder
new TextDecoder().decode(effectcraft.readFile(p));                       // "hello": the page reads it

// A .jsx script has only the After Effects scripting API: to read a file it must open it first.
(await effectcraft.execute("script.run", {code:
  `var f = new File("${p}"); writeLn(f.open("r") ? f.read() : f.error);`})).output
// "File not found"   expected: "hello"

await effectcraft.addFile("icon-256.png", "icon.png");
await effectcraft.saveToBrowser("/repro.ecproj");
await effectcraft.execute("footage.check", {wait: true})
// {checked: 1, missing: 1}   expected: missing: 0
```

### Why it matters
Template scripts read their data the After Effects way: `new File("props.json")`, then `open`, `read`. That is how the same `.jsx` runs unchanged in After Effects, the desktop app, the CLI and the browser. In the browser it fails at `open`.

### Cause
The file is readable: scripts read files through the editor's file layer (`Session.services`), which finds it. But `File.open("r")` first checks that the file exists, and that check asks the local disk (`std::fs`), skipping the file layer. A browser has no disk, so the answer is always no, and the read is never reached. `File.exist…

title: Proposal: embeddable web player (play a project or a template script in a canvas)
author: rahal
body:
Hi, and thank you for EffectCraft! The engine's split into clean crates (the session, the frame-worker protocol, the script engine) made what follows possible with very little glue, which says a lot about the design.

I built an embeddable browser player on the engine crates. It has no editor UI: a `<canvas>`, or `<effectcraft-player src="…">`, loads a `.ecproj`, or builds one from a template `.jsx` plus props JSON, and plays it with Web Audio. Frames render in Web Workers, on WebGPU where the browser has it in workers, else on the CPU. Each worker's copy of the project follows edits by diffs, using the editor's own frame-worker protocol (`engine::remote`).

**Why it's interesting:** a video can ship as a script. The sample template is ~14 KB of `.jsx` plus a small props file. Fonts and footage are separate files, cached by the browser. The same template plays per viewer with different props (language, RTL, brand, texts) and can be edited after publishing without re-rendering. The host page can change Essential Graphics controls live: `player.set("headline", "…")`. Templates read their props the After Effects way (`new File("props.json")`, `open`, `read`), so the same `.jsx` also runs in After Effects, the desktop app and the CLI.

**State:**
- One wasm file of 22.8 MB (size-optimised, full LTO).
- Template build ~400 ms; a full 1080×1920 frame ~50 ms on a GPU worker (~80 ms wall clock), ~130 ms on a CPU worker (Apple M-series, headless Chrome). Preview-size playback keeps 30 fps with no dropped frames. `--opt 3` trades size for ~30% faster frames.
- Native tests and a headless-Chrome smoke test.
- Branch: https://github.com/rahal/effectcraft/tree/player (`apps/effectcraft-player`, `docs/player.md`, `examples/player`), stacked on the fix below.

**What it needs from this repo:** the fix for #1593, in PR #1594. Scripts couldn't open files that aren't on the local disk, which breaks templates reading `props.json` in the browser. That's a bug in the web editor too, so …

title: Trimming Layer by shortcut causes other end to take up entire timeline
author: WaldemarLehner
body:
## Context

Given a Scene, 
- when selecting a Layer and making use of `Trim Layer In Point to Current Time`, the Layer's end is set to the composition's end;
- when selecting a Layer and making use of `Trim Layer Out Point to Current Time`, the Layer's start is set to 00:00.

## Reproduction

- Create a new composition
- Create a new layer, for example using a Rectangle Shape
- Resize the Shape to not take the entire composition (meaning you trim a bit at the start and the end, using your mouse)
- Move Timeline Seeking Head to somewhere that is not at the start or end of the composition
- Make use of `Trim Layer In Point to Current Time` or `Trim Layer Out Point to Current Time` Shortcuts. They are `Alt+[` and `Alt+]` on a DE-Layout by default. You can can adjust the shortcut as needed under `Edit` → `Keyboard Shortcuts`
- You will see that while your trim terminates on the Timeline Seek Head, it also modifies the other end of the layer

Repro Video: 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cf712e61-7143-46c7-9f1f-5ec82e053e47

## System Compatibility Report

EffectCraft 0.10.0
Operating system: Arch Linux (x86_64)
CPU: AMD Ryzen 5 3600X 6-Core Processor (12 logical cores)
Memory: 31.3 GB (17.7 GB available)
GPU: AMD Radeon RX 7800 XT (RADV NAVI32) (Vulkan)

body:
**Question, not a confirmed bug:** I can't run After Effects to check. Is Roughen Edges expected to keep this much of a stroke at a large Border?

### What I was doing
I followed an After Effects tutorial step by step in EffectCraft: Chris Moran, "How to Make Text Feel Real Like NETFLIX Docs", https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eFm43BURGSE.

For the "ink flecks" layer (5:46–6:47), the tutorial does this:

- adds Turbulent Displace at its defaults;
- adds Roughen Edges with Border 24.3, Edge Sharpness 2.42, Fractal Influence 0.71, Scale 32, Complexity 2 (values read from the Effect Controls panel in the video).

title: Expressions: propertyGroup() and a group's propertyIndex are missing (shape-group stagger fails)
author: switch87
body:
I'm working on this.

## What happens

The common After Effects technique for staggering shape groups (Adobe Community answer "Expression to offset shape group scale animation"):

```js
offset = .1;
id = thisProperty.propertyGroup(2).propertyIndex;
content("circle").transform.scale.valueAtTime(time-id*offset)
```

written on the Scale of every duplicated group fails in EffectCraft 0.10 / `main` with

```
Error at line 2: TypeError: not a callable function
```

and the groups don't animate.

## Repro (headless)

A JSX script builds a shape layer with four groups (`circle` with Scale keyed 0 → 100 over 1 s, `Dot 2`–`Dot 4` with the expression above), saves the project, then:

```sh
effectcraft-cli get Stagger Dots 'contents/group#3/transform/scale' --time 0.5 --project stagger.ecproj --json
# "expressionError":"Error at line 2: TypeError: not a callable function"
```

## Cause

The expression object model has no `propertyGroup()`: neither a property nor a property group has it, and a property group has no `propertyIndex` either. The scripting object model (ExtendScript side) has both; only the expression side is missing them.

## Expected (After Effects Expression Language Reference)

- `Property.propertyGroup(countUp = 1)` and `PropertyGroup.propertyGroup(countUp = 1)` return the group `countUp` levels above; going up from a top-level group (Transform, Effects, Contents…) reaches the layer.
- `PropertyGroup.propertyIndex`: the group's 1-based index among its siblings (so `propertyGroup(2).propertyIndex` on a shape group's Transform ▸ Scale is the group's index in Contents).

## Plan

Add both to the expression runtime (one host request that walks up from the property or group, so it also works for the property being evaluated), with tests for the stagger expression, effect parameters (`propertyGroup(1).name` is the effect), reaching the layer, and an out-of-range `countUp` giving a clear error instead of a crash.

title: Feature Request: Export Sequence as OGraf Template
author: jk162324-cmd
body:
Add a feature that allows users to export a sequence as an OGraf (Open HTML Graphics for Broadcast) template. This would enable users to reuse sequences in compatible broadcast graphics systems without having to recreate them manually.

**Expected Behavior**

- Add an option to export the current composition as an OGraf template.
- Convert supported layers, animations, and visual elements into the corresponding OGraf-compatible HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
- Preserve timing, transforms, text, and other supported animation properties as closely as possible.
- Make the exported template self-contained or include all required assets and dependencies.
- Notify users about unsupported effects, properties, or expressions that cannot be converted.

**Use Case**

A motion designer creates an animated lower third, title sequence, or other broadcast graphic in Effectcraft and exports it as an OGraf template for use in a compatible broadcast graphics workflow.

**Benefits**

- Enables Effectcraft to be used as an authoring tool for broadcast graphics.
- Bridges the gap between traditional motion graphics workflows and HTML-based broadcast graphics.
- Reduces the need to recreate animations manually in OGraf-compatible systems.
- Makes Effectcraft more useful for professional broadcast and live production workflows.

title: Pin Microsoft.Trusted.Signing.Client version and hash in sign.ps1
author: MazenGit
body: `packaging/windows/sign.ps1` (line 77 at v0.10.0) installs the latest `Microsoft.Trusted.Signing.Client` from nuget.org with no version or hash, in the step that holds the Azure signing credentials. A bad or hijacked package version would run with those credentials, and no commit would show it. Pinning an exact version and verifying the package hash is a one-line change that rarely needs bumping, so it avoids the PR churn raised in storytold/craft-common-actions#6. VectorCraft's `sign.ps1` has the same line. Related: storytold/craft-common-actions#7. Lower stakes, same pattern: `wix` is pinned by version only, and the FreeBSD/riscv64 jobs use rustup via `curl | sh` (no secrets there).

title: Position drifts between two identical keyframes (spatial path overshoots during a hold)
author: Xharig
body:
**Version:** EffectCraft 0.10.0 (latest release), Windows 11 x64, portable build

### What happens
A layer is meant to hold still between two position keyframes that have the same value, but it moves away and comes back.

Keys on `transform/position` (comp 1920×1080, 30 fps, 5 s):

| time | value |
|---|---|
| 0 s | [0, 540] |
| 0.6 s | [400, 540] |
| 4.4 s | [400, 540] |
| 5.0 s | [0, 540] |

Position read back with `get_layer` (`flat: true`, `time`):

| time | expected | actual |
|---|---|---|
| 1.0 s | 400 | **403.09** |
| 2.5 s | 400 | **449.99** |
| 4.0 s | 400 | **403.09** |

The same happens with `interpolation: "linear"` (2.5 s → 449.99), so it is the spatial path, not the temporal ease: the segment between the two identical keys gets a curved path from the auto-Bézier spatial tangents of its neighbours.

### Expected
As in After Effects: two consecutive keys with the same position are a zero-length path segment, so the layer does not move between them.

### Steps (MCP, headless)
1. `command_run` `comp.new` `{"name":"Drift","width":1920,"height":1080,"frameRate":30,"duration":5,"open":true}`
2. `command_run` `layer.newSolid` `{"name":"Box","color":"#ff0000","width":100,"height":100}`
3. `add_keyframe` `{"layer":"Box","path":"transform/position","interpolation":"easyEase","keys":[{"time":0,"value":[0,540]},{"time":0.6,"value":[400,540]},{"time":4.4,"value":[400,540]},{"time":5,"value":[0,540]}]}`
4. `get_layer` `{"layer":"Box","flat":true,"time":2.5}` → `transform/position` is `[449.99, 540]`

### Workaround
`keys.setSpatialTangents` with `in: [0,0,0]` and `out: [0,0,0]` on every position key → the layer holds exactly at 400.

### Impact
Found while building a lower third (slide in 0–0.6 s, hold, slide out 4.4–5 s): in the rendered ProRes 4444 file the whole graphic sat 58 px to the right in the middle of the hold.

Faux Italic works. A real bold face (`style: "Bold"`) also works.

title: Text: Calibri / Arial / Times New Roman / Courier New / Cambria fall back to Inter instead of installed metric-compatible fonts (Carlito, Liberation, Caladea)
author: ibakard
body:
**EffectCraft:** 0.10.0 AppImage (`effectcraft-0.10.0-linux-x86_64.AppImage`, headless `effectcraft-cli`)
**OS:** Fedora 44, x86_64

## Summary

Text set in Microsoft font names renders in the bundled Inter when those fonts are not installed. This is the normal case on Linux, and it applies to projects, templates and scripts made on Windows or macOS. The names affected include Calibri, Arial, Times New Roman, Courier New and Cambria.

The machine does have the metric-compatible substitutes, and fontconfig maps the names to them (`30-metric-aliases.conf`):

| Requested | Installed substitute (`fc-match`) |
|---|---|
| Calibri | Carlito |
| Arial | Liberation Sans |
| Times New Roman | Liberation Serif |
| Courier New | Liberation Mono |
| Cambria | Caladea |

As a result:
- serif and monospace text becomes sans-serif;
- line widths and wrapping change, because Inter's metrics differ;
- Bold Italic loses its bold, since Inter has no Bold Italic face (see #1676).

The font list itself is fine: the substitutes are scanned and listed as system fonts. This is not Fedora-specific. Any Linux system without the Microsoft fonts behaves the same, as would macOS or Windows without them.

## Steps to reproduce

```sh
./effectcraft-0.10.0-linux-x86_64.AppImage --appimage-extract >/dev/null
CLI=./squashfs-root/usr/bin/effectcraft-cli
for f in Calibri Arial "Times New Roman" "Courier New" Cambria; do fc-match "$f"; done
$CLI --empty --save-as alias.ecproj run \
  comp.new '{"name":"T","width":900,"height":300,"background":"#ffffff","duration":1}' \

title: Expressions: inside an Essential Graphics instance, valueAtTime() and numKeys ignore keys set on the instance
author: mangledmonkey
body:
## Summary

When a comp's control is exposed in Essential Graphics and the control is **keyframed on a placed instance** (the precomp layer's `essential/…` property), expressions inside the comp see the instance's value only at the current frame:

- `value` is correct (the instance's keyed value at the current time).
- `valueAtTime(t)` returns the value at the **current** time, not at `t`.
- `numKeys` is `0` (and `key(n)` is unavailable), although the instance's property is keyed.

The same keys set directly on the control in the comp work as expected. So any expression that looks ahead or behind (blending into an upcoming state, easing a switch, reading key times) can't work per instance; it snaps instead.

## Environment

- EffectCraft 0.10.0 app (macOS, Apple silicon), and `effectcraft-cli` 0.8.0 headless: same result in both

## Steps to reproduce

1. New comp `inner`, 300×100, 2 s.
2. Add a null `controls` with a **Slider Control**.
3. Add three rectangle shape layers (white, 80×80) at x = 50, 150, 250, with these Opacity expressions:
   - `now`: `thisComp.layer("controls").effect(1)(1).value`
   - `ahead`: `thisComp.layer("controls").effect(1)(1).valueAtTime(time + 0.5)`
   - `keys`: `thisComp.layer("controls").effect(1)(1).numKeys > 0 ? 100 : 0`
4. Make `inner` the primary comp and add the slider to Essential Graphics (`essential.addProperty`, name `Amount`).
5. New comp `scene`, add `inner` to it. On the instance layer, keyframe `Amount`: 0 at 0 s, 100 at 1 s (linear).
6. For comparison, duplicate `inner` and set the same two keys directly on its slider.
7. Render both at 0.25 s and read each box's opacity.

## Expected

The same in both: `now` 25, `ahead` 75 (value at 0.75 s), `keys` 100.

## Actual

| | now | ahead | keys |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| keys on the control in the comp | 25 | 75 | 100 |
| keys on the instance (Essential Graphics) | 25 | **25** | **0** |

## Suggested fix

title: Parity: switching the Polystar between Polygon and Star should add/remove the inner properties
author: elZanco
body:
Switching a Polystar's Type between Polygon and Star should add `Inner Radius` (right before `Outer Radius`) and `Inner Roundness` (right before `Outer Roundness`, default 0) when going Polygon → Star, and remove them again when going Star → Polygon — like After Effects does.

AE quirk found while testing, worth a deliberate decision before implementing: on the switch, AE gives `Inner Radius` a **fixed default of 50 px**, although a freshly tool-created star uses **Inner Radius = Outer Radius / 2**. We should either copy the 50 px verbatim (parity) or treat it as an AE bug and use Outer/2 — the more sensible default, and the one AE itself uses for new stars.

Found while implementing #1072.

title: Lottie Eport with time remapping fails animation
author: teapullpot
body:
**Title:** Lottie export: keyframe times inside layers with a start offset (`st` ≠ 0) are written relative to the layer start, so animations fire at the wrong time

**Version:** EffectCraft 0.10.0 (project saved with `savedBy: 0.10.0`)

**What happens**
In the exported Lottie JSON, layers that start later in the composition (`st` > 0) have their keyframe times (`t`) written relative to the layer start (0, 4, 10, …) instead of relative to the composition. lottie-web reads `t` as composition time, so these animations have already finished when the layer becomes visible.

**Concrete example**
My precomp has 15 matte layers (`D1_Mask`, `D2_Mask`, `M_Mask` …) that reveal a handwritten logo with an animated Trim Paths `end` value (0 → 100 over 4–10 frames). `M_Mask` starts at composition frame 21 (`ip: 21, st: 21`). In the export its keyframes are:

```json
"e": {"a": 1, "k": [{"s": [0.0], "t": 0.0, ...}, {"s": [100.0], "t": 10.0}]}
```

In EffectCraft the letter is drawn over frames 21–31. In lottie-web 5.13.0 the trim end is already 100 % at frame 21 (I read `shapeModifiers[0].e.v` = 1 from frame 21 on), so the whole letter appears in a single frame. Every letter pops in at its layer start instead of being written, even with a linear time remap, so this is independent of any easing.

**Expected**
Keyframe times are composition time (as in Bodymovin/After Effects exports), so `M_Mask` should have `t: 21` and `t: 31`.

**Verification**
Shifting every keyframe `t` in layers with `st` ≠ 0 by that layer's `st` (28 layers, 30 keyframes) fixes it: the ink grows by 1–8 % per frame instead of jumping by up to 25 % in one frame. A small script that does this (`fix_lottie_layer_start.py`) is available; I can attach it.

**Notes**
- I only checked lottie-web 5.13.0 (SVG renderer). I have not tested lottie-ios, lottie-android or other players.
- The time remap (`tm`) and position easing handles were exported correctly. I compared them with the values in the `.ecproj` (influence/spee…

title: Web build: automatic language ignores the browser's language
author: mccoy88f
body:
In the browser build (v0.10.0), the interface language set to *Auto* always shows English, even when the browser is set to a language the app has a catalog for. The desktop build follows the system language correctly.

**Steps:** open the web build in a browser set to Spanish (`navigator.languages` = `["es-ES"]`) with no saved preferences → the interface is in English.

**Cause:** `system_language()` in `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n.rs` uses `sys_locale::get_locale()`, which finds nothing in the browser build, so *Auto* resolves to English — even for a browser set to Spanish or Japanese, which have catalogs.

**Suggested fix:** on wasm, use `navigator.languages` (falling back to `navigator.language`) as the system language tags. GridCraft (`crates/ui-egui/src/i18n.rs`, `navigator().language()`), FilmCraft (`apps/filmcraft-web/src/lib.rs`, `navigator().languages()`), VectorCraft, WordCraft and CadCraft already do this in their browser builds.

---
Found while hosting the Craft Apps on a self-hosted ArtCraft Launcher server: https://github.com/mccoy88f/craft-launcher-docker

title: Media: broad AVI import support across legacy codecs and DV variants
author: tylerjenningsw
body:
EffectCraft can't import `.avi` files yet. AVI is a container, so accepting the extension doesn't mean decoding every codec it can hold. This issue tracks broad AVI support as a set of focused PRs, with a published compatibility matrix.

## What exists
- FilmCraft, EffectCraft's media backend, already has an AVI reader ([filmcraft#650](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/pull/650)). It covers AVI 1.0 and OpenDML, with decoding for MJPEG, several raw formats, H.264/HEVC and common audio.
- EffectCraft pins a FilmCraft revision from before that reader. Its central video-extension list (`crates/media`) also leaves out `avi`, though the Media Browser's own list has it.
- DV: [filmcraft#2092](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/pull/2092) (open) covers NTSC DV25 in MOV. It doesn't yet cover PAL DV, DV in AVI or embedded DV audio. That shared decoder should be extended rather than a second one written.

## Support target
| Area | Target |
|---|---|
| Container | AVI 1.0 and OpenDML; large files (offsets beyond 4 GB); indexed and unindexed recordings; bounded handling of truncated files |
| Existing codecs | FilmCraft's MJPEG, raw video, H.264/HEVC and supported audio, exposed and validated |
| DV cameras | PAL and NTSC DV25; DV/DVCAM/DVCPRO25 where applicable; Type-1 (`iavs`) and Type-2 AVI; embedded or separate audio ([Microsoft's DV AVI specification](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/directshow/dv-data-in-the-avi-file-format)) |
| Older compressed video | MPEG-4 Part 2 Simple / Advanced Simple Profile (applicable DivX / Xvid files), from the public specification; older Microsoft-derived variants identified separately, not fed to it |
| Older audio | Existing PCM / MPEG audio / AC-3, then MS ADPCM, IMA ADPCM and G.711 |
| Picture interpretation | Frame rate, pixel and display aspect ratio, field order, stream start offsets (with an interpretation override where the file says nothing) |
| Later, each scoped on its own | Palette / RLE video, Cinepak, M…

title: Reverse-edit keyframe preset reportedly fails when applied to a clip (reproduction needed)
author: earlvanze
body:
A user reports that a reverse-edit animation preset made from their keyframes does not work when applied to a clip. This is an unverified report; the exact failure and reproduction are not yet known.

Source: https://discord.com/channels/1359579021108842617/1557582920321867876/1560848286569472130 (2026-10-17 02:53 UTC). The same author repeated the request at message IDs 1560848919007854614 and 1560849578201317407; these describe one report.

Expected: applying the saved keyframe preset to a compatible clip reproduces the intended reverse animation at the chosen playhead position.
Reported actual: “it don’t work when I apply to clip.” No project, preset file, error text, version or OS was provided. It is unknown whether keys fail to appear, playback direction is wrong, or application fails entirely. It is also unknown whether “reverse” means reversed property keyframes or Time Remapping.

Current triage:
- Animation preset save/apply exists in crates/engine/src/commands/animation.rs. Property keys are saved relative to their earliest key and applied at the current layer time; incompatible property paths can be skipped.
- Open PR #1317 addresses dragging animation presets onto layers. It could explain this report if the user is dragging, but that application method has not been confirmed.
- #1681 concerns copied Shape Contents operators, a different reported workflow. Searches of existing issues/PRs for reverse presets found no exact match.
- No reproduction was executed and no fix is claimed. Preserve this distinction from a confirmed engine regression.

Details needed: EffectCraft version and OS; animated property (especially whether Time Remapping); how the preset is saved and applied; whether keys appear on the target; minimal original .ecpreset/project and a short recording if available. Compare menu-based application on a fresh duplicate clip with drag-and-drop before narrowing the cause.

title: Saved assets show in Project Panel but render black / fail to load source on reopen.
author: 123sainianjali456-blip
body:
### Bug Description
When opening a saved `.ecproj` project file, media items appear correctly in the Project Panel (and render fine in the Footage preview tab), but all layers in the active composition render as a black screen in the main viewer (`Composition Comp 1`).

### Root Cause / Technical Analysis
Inspecting the saved project JSON reveals a **time-unit tick deserialization bug**. 

Upon saving, high-precision time ticks are written to disk. When the project is reloaded (`load_project`), layer time properties (`start_time`, `in_point`, `out_point`) appear to be double-scaled or multiplied by the frame-rate tick base again. 

As a result, layer start times get shifted to massive tick integers (e.g., `start_time: 144086342400`), placing composition layers hours or days down the timeline out of range of the playhead at `0:00:00:00`.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Create a new composition (e.g., 1080x1920 @ 59.94 fps).
2. Import PNG/media files and place them on the composition timeline at `00:00f`.
3. Save the project file (`File > Save`).
4. Close and reopen the saved project file.
5. Observe that the playhead at `00:00f` displays a black screen in the main composition viewer, and layer time bounds on the timeline are misplaced.

### Expected Behavior
Composition layers should load back at their originally saved timeline positions and render immediately in the main viewer at `0:00:00:00`.

### System Info / Context
- **Version:** `0.10.0`
- **JSON Excerpt:**
```json
"layers": [
  {
    "id": 461,
    "name": "crown.png",
    "start_time": 144086342400,
    "in_point": 1334917584000,
    "out_point": 12853349308800
  }
]

body: I'd like to propose an FX Console-style quick effect search for EffectCraft, inspired by the workflow of Video Copilot's FX Console. ### Proposed workflow 1. Select one or more layers. 2. Press Ctrl+Space to open a compact search popup. 3. Search effects by name, category, or ID. 4. Press Enter or click a result to apply it. 5. Press Esc to close the popup. Applying an effect should use EffectCraft's existing undo system. ### Working prototype I have a local prototype built with AI assistance that includes: - A modified EffectCraft host. - A Rust-compiled WASM module running through wasmi. - An experimental workflow API that lets the module request a host-owned effect-search popup. - Automated checks for opening the popup, searching, applying an effect, and undoing it. The prototype's API versioning and implementation are experimental and open to redesign. It is an independent implementation and does not use Video Copilot code. title: Reported rendering artifact: lights create lines in shadows
author: earlvanze
body:
A user reports that lights create visible lines in shadows. This is a reported rendering defect, not yet independently reproduced.

Source: <https://discord.com/channels/1359579021108842617/1557582920321867876/1560930954518732812> (2026-10-17 08:22 UTC).

The report says: "light creates lines in shadows" and includes an image.png attachment in the source message. The attachment could not be inspected because its CDN request returned HTTP 403. No version, operating system, GPU, renderer mode, light type, project file, or exact reproduction steps were provided. The root cause is unknown; shadow-map bias or sampling should not be assumed from this report alone.

Expected: shadows render without unintended lines.
Reported actual: lines appear in shadows when using a light.

Triage checked the current open issues and PRs plus docs/gaps.md, docs/roadmap.md and 3D parity notes. No matching tracking item was found. Issue #1691 and PR #1704 concern an opaque shadow catcher with Accepts Shadows Only, a different reported symptom. Existing shadow rendering includes bias and filtering logic, but that does not establish the cause or a fix for this report.

Next investigation needs a minimal project and the missing environment details, then comparison of preview/export and applicable CPU/GPU renderer paths. No verified workaround or released fix is known from the available evidence.

body: # Feature Request: Add Native 3D Primitive and Parametric Mesh Creation Tools ## Summary I would like to request the addition of **native 3D primitive creation tools** in EffectCraft, allowing users to create and edit basic 3D geometric objects directly inside a composition without relying on external 3D modeling software or importing pre-made 3D models. The feature could be inspired by Adobe After Effects' Parametric Mesh Tools, which provide a workflow for creating basic 3D shapes directly within the composition. This would make EffectCraft more capable for 3D compositing, motion graphics, visual effects, and scene construction. ## Problem Statement Currently, when users want to add simple 3D geometry to a composition, they may need to create the object in external software such as Blender, export it, and then import it into EffectCraft. This creates unnecessary steps for simple objects such as cubes, cuboids, cylinders, cones, and planes. For example, while compositing a 3D car into tracked footage, a user might need a simple 3D plane to represent the road, a cube to represent a building, or a cylinder to create a basic environmental object. Having to create and import these objects externally interrupts the editing workflow. Basic 3D geometry should be accessible directly within the editor. ## Reference: Adobe After Effects Adobe After Effects provides native 3D parametric mesh tools in its Advanced 3D workflow. Users can create basic geometric meshes directly in a composition and work with them as 3D objects. Reference documentation: https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/using/3d-models.html The purpose is not to copy another application's interface exactly, but to provide a similarly convenient workflow within EffectCraft. ## Proposed Feature ### 1. Native 3D Primitive Tools Add a toolbar tool or menu named **3D Shapes** or **Create 3D Primitive**.

title: [Feature Request] Shift + Parent Pick Whip to Snap Child Layer to Parent Position
author: HexaGhost-09
body:
# [Feature Request] Shift-Assisted Layer Parenting Like Adobe After Effects

### Proposed Feature

Implement **Shift-assisted parenting** using the Parent & Link pick whip in the timeline, matching Adobe After Effects behavior.

### Expected Behavior

1. Select the child layer in the timeline.
2. Drag its Parent & Link pick whip onto the intended parent layer.
3. Hold **Shift** while completing the parenting operation.
4. The child layer becomes parented to the target layer and snaps to the parent’s position.

Normal parenting should preserve the child layer’s existing visual placement, while Shift-assisted parenting should snap it to the parent’s position.

### Why Is This Important?

Layer parenting is a fundamental motion graphics workflow. This shortcut makes it faster to create layer hierarchies, reduces repetitive steps, and provides a familiar experience for users transitioning from Adobe After Effects.

**Priority:** Important , a valuable workflow improvement for motion graphics and animation.

title: # [Feature Request] Rename Layers by Pressing Enter
author: HexaGhost-09
body:
# [Feature Request] Rename Layers by Pressing Enter

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

Renaming layers in EffectCraft could be faster and more intuitive. Users working with multiple layers need a quick way to organize and identify them.

### Proposed Feature

Allow users to rename a selected layer by pressing **Enter**, similar to the workflow in Adobe After Effects.

### Expected Behavior

- Select a layer in the timeline.
- Press **Enter** to activate the layer name field.
- Type the new name and press **Enter** again to confirm.
- Press **Esc** to cancel renaming.

### Benefits

- Faster layer organization.
- Improved workflow for projects with many layers.
- Familiar behavior for Adobe After Effects users.

Optimize camera updates, layer transformations, and composition rendering to maintain smooth performance with multiple layers.

title: Animation presets: applyPreset skips the effect properties savePreset writes (effects/<match name>/…)
author: mangledmonkey
body:
## Summary

`anim.savePreset` writes effect properties as `effects/<effect match name>/<property>` (for example
`effects/ec.control.slider/slider`, or `effects/ec.control.dropdown#2/menu` for the second dropdown). `anim.applyPreset`
can't resolve that form: it lists the property under `skipped` and leaves the value unchanged, even when the preset is
applied to the same layer it was saved from. So a preset saved from the app never restores an effect value.

The same preset edited by hand to `effects/#1/slider` (index) or `effects/<effect name>/slider` (the effect's display
name) applies correctly. Transform properties (`transform/rotation`) round-trip fine.

A related case: on a precomp layer with Essential Properties, `savePreset` writes the controls as
`essential/eg<control id>`. The ids are renumbered every time the template is imported, so the preset only fits the
instance it was saved from. `essential/<control name>` (for example `essential/Arm R bend`) applies correctly to any
instance and would be a portable form to save.

## Environment

- `effectcraft-cli` 0.8.0 headless (EffectCraft app 0.10.0 on macOS, Apple silicon)

## Steps to reproduce

1. New comp, add a solid `box`, apply **Slider Control** to it.
2. Set the slider to 30.
3. Select only `effects/#1/slider` and run `anim.savePreset {path: "repro.ecpreset"}`. The file contains
   `"path": "effects/ec.control.slider/slider"` with value 30.
4. Set the slider to 0.
5. Run `anim.applyPreset {path: "repro.ecpreset", layers: ["box"]}`.

## Expected

`{applied: 1, skipped: []}`, and the slider is 30 again.

## Actual

`{applied: 0, skipped: ["effects/ec.control.slider/slider"]}`, and the slider stays at 0. The command still reports
ok, so a caller only notices by reading `skipped`.

## Suggested fix

Have `applyPreset` resolve `effects/<match name>[#n]/…` the way `savePreset` writes it: the nth effect with that match
name on the target layer. Or have `savePreset` write a form that `applyPreset` already resolv…

title: Collapse Transformations ignored on a precomp layer whose Essential Properties are overridden: the nested comp clips to its frame
author: mangledmonkey
body:
## Summary

With **Collapse Transformations** on, a precomp layer normally draws its comp's layers beyond the nested comp's frame
(tested: a solid that sticks out of the nested comp's top edge shows in full). That stops working when the nested
comp's content is moved by a value set on the **instance** through Essential Properties. The render then clips at the
nested comp's frame, as if the switch were off. The same value set inside the nested comp is not clipped.

This matters for character templates, where a pose (an instance override) lifts a figure or raises its arms past the
template comp's frame.

## Environment

- `effectcraft-cli` 0.8.0 headless (EffectCraft app 0.10.0 on macOS, Apple silicon)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Comp `inner`, 400×300. Add a null `controls` with a **Point Control** `Offset` (0, 0), and a white solid `box`
   (100×100) at (200, 100) whose position expression is
   `value + thisComp.layer("controls").effect("Offset")(1).value`.
2. Make `inner` the primary comp and add `Offset` to Essential Graphics.
3. Comp `outer`, 400×600. Add `inner` to it, centred (its frame covers rows 150–449), and turn on Collapse
   Transformations for that layer.
4. **A:** in `inner`, set `Offset` to (0, −120). Render `outer`.
5. **B:** set `Offset` in `inner` back to (0, 0), and on the instance in `outer` set the Essential Property `Offset` to
   (0, −120). Render `outer`.

## Expected

A and B render the same: the box spans rows 80–179 of `outer`, reaching 70 px above the instance's frame.

## Actual

- A: rows 80–179, as expected.
- B: rows 150–179. The box is clipped at the top edge of `inner`'s frame.

We saw the same with the full puppet template: the figure raised 30 pt in the comp drew from row 76 with collapse on;
raised by the same amount through the instance's override, it was cut at row 160, the frame's top.

## Suggested fix

When a collapsed precomp layer carries Essential Properties overrides, apply the overrides and still render the
nested layers…

title: UI Parity Gap: Hidden layers (Eye icon off) completely erase viewport Gizmo controls for Shapes and Masks
author: Omar7-ctrl
body:
Executive Summary (Parity Gap)

There is a workflow discrepancy regarding hidden layers. In EffectCraft, toggling a layer's visibility off (clicking the Eye icon) completely erases its transformation and orientation Gizmo handles from the viewport, even if the layer or its mask path remains actively selected.
This causes friction when manipulating Shape Layers and Masks, as artists cannot see the vector paths or bounding box handles to edit masks precisely without being forced to keep the layer's solid pixels fully visible.

📐 Expected Behavior (After Effects Parity):

• When a layer is hidden via the timeline visibility toggle, selecting the layer or its Mask path should still render the spatial bounding box outline, rotation/scale Gizmos, and path vertices in the viewport.
• This allows clean vector and mask manipulation against background assets without the hidden layer's own fill pixels blocking the artwork view.

🖼️ Visual Context:

title: Feature Request: Add dedicated Transform keyframes (Position, Scale, Rotation) directly to Masks
author: Omar7-ctrl
body:
Executive Summary

In traditional compositing workflows, animation on a Mask is limited entirely to the Mask Path property (animating raw shape vertices over time). This makes scaling, rotating, or offsetting a mask via keyframes tedious and reliant on manually pushing vector points or using external parenting scripts.
I propose introducing native, dedicated Transform properties (Position, Scale, Rotation, and Anchor Point) directly nested under each individual Mask component inside EffectCraft.

📐 Workflow & Technical Logic:

• Independent Mask Matrix: Each mask should evaluate its own local transformation matrix relative to the layer's source space.
• Ease of Animation: Instead of triggering Mask Path vertex keys, artists can simply drop a Keyframe on Mask Position or Mask Rotation to smoothly glide, spin, or stretch the mask shape.
• GPU Efficiency: Since the rendering is driven by wgpu, translating a mask via matrix properties instead of recalculating individual vector vertices on every single frame will be highly memory-efficient and perform flawlessly at 120fps.
This native integration would be a massive usability upgrade, setting EffectCraft apart from Adobe's legacy path architecture.

title: [Feature Request] [EffectCraft] Layer sequencing
author: ticket-craft
body:
### Description

Feature Request: Layer Sequence (Similar to After Effects)

I'd like to suggest a Layer Sequence feature that automatically arranges multiple layers one after another in the timeline, with optional overlapping.

How it works:

1. Select the layers
Users select multiple layers in the timeline that they want to sequence. These could be text, images, shapes, or other supported layers.

2. Open the Layer Sequence command
The user opens the command from the Layer menu or by right-clicking the selected layers.

3. Determine the sequence order
The software uses the selected layers' existing timeline order by default. Users can optionally reverse the sequence.

4. Set the sequence timing
Users choose how the layers should be arranged:

- No overlap: Each layer starts when the previous layer ends.
- With overlap: The next layer starts before the previous layer ends.
- Overlap duration: Users specify the overlap in frames or seconds.
- Sequence from playhead: Optionally, start the first layer at the current playhead position.

5. Calculate the new start times
The software automatically calculates the start time of each layer based on its duration and the chosen overlap.

For example, if five layers each last 2 seconds:

- No overlap: 0s, 2s, 4s, 6s, 8s.
- 0.5-second overlap: 0s, 1.5s, 3s, 4.5s, 6s.

The sequence should work with layers of different durations, too.

6. Preserve existing animations
The software should shift each layer's timing without changing its existing keyframes, animation curves, effects, or duration. The relative timing of keyframes within each layer should remain the same.

7. Preview and apply
Before applying, users should be able to review the sequence timing. Applying the command updates the timeline automatically.

8. Support undo and redo
Users can undo or redo the entire sequencing operation in one action.

9. Optional transitions

title: Time Displacement: extra "Layer Source" parameter at index 2 shifts the After Effects parameter order (scripts set wrong values silently)
author: empatvf
body:
## Summary

`ADBE Time Displacement` has five parameters in EffectCraft and four in After Effects. The extra "Time Displacement Layer Source" sits at index 2, so every later parameter is shifted by one. A script that sets the effect by index (common in After Effects scripts, since the parameter names are localized) writes its values into the wrong parameters without any error.

## Environment

- effectcraft-cli 0.10.0 (`effectcraft-cli-0.10.0-macos-universal.zip`), headless `effectcraft-cli script … --empty`
- macOS 26.3, Apple silicon
- Compared with After Effects 2026 (26.5) running the same script

## Repro

```js
var c = app.project.items.addComp("repro", 1920, 1080, 1, 5, 25);
var s = c.layers.addSolid([1, 1, 1], "s", 1920, 1080, 1);
s.property("ADBE Effect Parade").addProperty("ADBE Time Displacement");
var td = s.property("ADBE Effect Parade").property(1), names = [];
for (var i = 1; i <= td.numProperties; i++) if (td.property(i).name != "Compositing Options") names.push(i + "=" + td.property(i).name);
names.join(", ");
```

- **After Effects 2026:** `1=Time Displacement Layer, 2=Max Displacement Time [sec], 3=Time Resolution [fps], 4=If Layer Sizes Differ`
- **EffectCraft 0.10.0:** `1=Time Displacement Layer, 2=Time Displacement Layer Source, 3=Max Displacement Time (sec), 4=Time Resolution (fps), 5=Stretch Map To Fit`

## Impact

The usual After Effects code

```js
td.property(1).setValue(mapLayer.index);
td.property(2).setValue(1);    // Max Displacement Time
td.property(3).setValue(100);  // Time Resolution
td.property(4).setValue(1);    // Stretch map to fit
```

sets Layer Source, Max Displacement Time and Time Resolution to the wrong values in EffectCraft. In our case, a slit-scan title built from the "Modern Glitch Titles" recipe (Time Displacement with a gradient map, max 1 s, 100 fps), the result looked broken with no error.

## Workaround

Address the parameters by their EffectCraft match names (`ADBE Time Displacement-0001`, `-0003`, `-0004`, `-00…

title: Shift Channels: menu value 10 is "Half On" instead of After Effects' "Full Off" (RGB split renders pastel)
author: empatvf
body:
## Summary

Shift Channels' "Take … From" menus have 11 entries in EffectCraft and 10 in After Effects. EffectCraft adds "Half On" at position 10, so value **10**, which is **Full Off** in After Effects, gives 50 % grey in EffectCraft, and Full Off becomes 11. After Effects scripts and projects that use 10 for "Full Off" render pastel colours instead of isolated channels, with no error.

## Environment

- effectcraft-cli 0.10.0 (`effectcraft-cli-0.10.0-macos-universal.zip`), headless
- macOS 26.3, Apple silicon
- Compared with After Effects 2026 (26.5)
- Still present on main at f36b2b3: `crates/effects/src/channel.rs` line 54, `SHIFT_NAMES: [&str; 11] = [… "Full On", "Half On", "Full Off"]`

## Repro

Menu range:

```js
var c = app.project.items.addComp("repro", 40, 40, 1, 1, 25);
var s = c.layers.addSolid([1, 0.6, 0.2], "s", 40, 40, 1);
s.property("ADBE Effect Parade").addProperty("ADBE Shift Channels");
var p = s.property("ADBE Effect Parade").property(1).property(3), maxOk = 0;   // Take Green From
for (var v = 1; v <= 12; v++) { try { p.setValue(v); if (p.value == v) maxOk = v; } catch (e) {} }
maxOk;
```

- **After Effects 2026:** `10` (`setValue(11)` throws "Value 11 out of range 1 to 10")
- **EffectCraft 0.10.0:** `12`

Rendered value of green on an orange solid `[255, 153, 51]` with Take Green From = 10:

- **After Effects:** 0 (Full Off)
- **EffectCraft 0.10.0:** 128 (Half On). Value 11 gives 0.

## Impact

The classic RGB-split glitch (three copies of a layer, each with Shift Channels keeping one channel and setting the other two to Full Off = 10, blended with Add) renders as pink, light green and light blue copies instead of pure red, green and blue. We hit this porting the "Modern Glitch Titles" recipe.

## Suggestion

Match After Effects' menu (Alpha, Red, Green, Blue, Luminance, Hue, Lightness, Saturation, Full On, Full Off), or keep Half On but put it after Full Off so values 1 to 10 mean what they mean in After Effects. Projects or presets saved wit…

title: Scripting: setValueAtTime at a sub-frame time snaps the key to the previous frame (After Effects keeps the exact time)
author: empatvf
body:
## Summary

Keyframes set from a script at a time between two frames are moved to the previous frame in EffectCraft. After Effects keeps the exact time: `setValueAtTime(1.5, …)` in a 25 fps comp creates a key at 1.5 s, which `keyTime()` reports as 1.5. In EffectCraft the key lands at 1.48 s. Motion starts up to one frame early and values between keys differ, most visibly on steep eases.

## Environment

- effectcraft-cli 0.10.0 (`effectcraft-cli-0.10.0-macos-universal.zip`), headless
- macOS 26.3, Apple silicon
- Compared with After Effects 2026 (26.5)

## Repro

```js
var c = app.project.items.addComp("repro", 400, 400, 1, 5, 25);
var r = c.layers.addNull().property("ADBE Transform Group").property("ADBE Rotate Z");
r.setValueAtTime(1.5, 0); r.setValueAtTime(2.5, 90);
r.keyTime(1) + " / " + r.keyTime(2) + ", value at 2.0 = " + r.valueAtTime(2.0, false).toFixed(2);
```

- **After Effects 2026:** `1.5 / 2.5, value at 2.0 = 45.00`
- **EffectCraft 0.10.0:** `1.48 / 2.48, value at 2.0 = 46.80`

## Impact

Templates often put keys on half frames (for example 1.5 s at 25 fps) and nested comps are often offset by fractions of a frame. With steep eases such as speed 0 and influence 100 % on both keys, a 0.02 s shift moves the value a lot near the middle of the move. In our test a title layer at t = 2.0 s was at y = 754 in EffectCraft and y = 869 in After Effects, from the same keys.

## Suggestion

Store and evaluate keyframes at the exact time the script passes, as After Effects does. Snapping to frames could stay a UI behaviour when dragging keys.

Found while running an After Effects title build script unchanged in EffectCraft (investigated with Claude Code).
